News.title: A fire in a building in southern Thailand kills 11 people
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A fire burned through a building in southern Thailand early Monday, killing 11 people, authorities said.

The fire started around 2 a.m. in the building in Phuket that has a motorcycle rental shop on the ground floor and residences on the upper floors, officials of the local government said. It took firefighters about an hour to bring the fire under control.

There were 17 other people who were slightly injured.

Phuket police commander Surachai Sooksai said officers are still investigating the cause of the fire, but initial investigations found an electrical transformer near the building had exploded shortly before the fire started.

Phuket Gov. Chodnarin Koedsom said the rental shop had about 100 motorcycles, along with stored gas, engine oil, plastic materials and tires. He said these combustible materials may have contributed to the rapid spread of the fire and the thick, toxic smoke.

He said the victims appeared to try to escape the fire to the higher floors. One body was found on the third floor and 10 others were found on the fifth floor.

Phuket is on an island in southern Thailand and a popular tourist destination.

Sports.title: Mahomes has a new star and Cousins fights back tears - NFL Sunday Review
Sports.content:
"There's more of the story to be written." Kirk Cousins could barely fight back the tears as he processed a day he thought might never come, a second chance he thought might never arrive. But football can't keep Kirko Chainz down, and suddenly the Minnesota Vikings have hope.

It is the easiest story in the NFL to get behind. A 38-year-old Kirk Cousins, written off more times than he can count, deemed deep into the back nine of his career, coming back to a hero's welcome to spearhead a playoff charge while lighting a fire under an offense in desperate need of inspiration. His inspiration.

He is football's lovable goof, with the unpretentious, unflashy dad clothes and a 'down with the kids' willingness to sling on Justin Jefferson's chains should it lift his teammates. He is also now Minnesota's great hope of rewarding defensive mastery with an attack capable of competing in January football.

The Vikings were limping behind Kyler Murray, limping behind Carson Wentz but sitting a coveted 6-2, and on Tuesday rolled the dice by trading to bring back Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders.

It was three years ago that Cousins played the final game of his first chapter with the Vikings when he tore his Achilles tendon in Week Eight against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. On Sunday he was back where it ended - but could it yet be where it all started again?

Cousins, who had revived his starting career as mentor to No 1 pick Mendoza in Las Vegas, finished 21 of 31 for 207 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in his first game back as the Vikings stunned the Packers 30-10.

His start featured a perfectly placed sideline strike between two defenders to a reception-starved Justin Jefferson on third-and-second in the first quarter, and so too a high-level tight-window bullet to Myles Price for a 38-yard touchdown catch-and-run on third-and-23.

It would become Jefferson's best game of the season as he made eight catches from nine targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns, Cousins' reconnecting with one of the stars of the league having seen him suffer for the first half of the season.

Much of the debate and, at times, criticism around Cousins throughout his career has been the shortage of point guard ability as a needle-moving creator. The Patrick Mahomes' and Josh Allens and Joe Burrows and Lamar Jacksons of the world have unfortunately heightened that bar for all quarterbacks across the league. But what has never been in doubt with Cousins is the efficiency at which he feeds his best players, and at which he moves the ball and at which he can accentuate an offense's strengths without being spectacular. Spectacular isn't exactly needed when there is a Brian Flores defense foaming at the mouth in wait of their chance to go hunting on the sideline.

In one game the Vikings looked a more polished, more accomplished operation behind Cousins, and alongside that came another rampant defensive play that saw Minnesota sack Jordan Love eight times.

In the first half alone they produced five sacks, 12 pressures, one interception and one fumble recovery, including sacks on back-to-back plays at the end of the second quarter. Their sixth sack then arrived on the very first play from scrimmage after the break, followed by the third of their four turnovers when Dallas Turner recover a wayward snap.

They were frightening, and the perfect complement once Cousins had helped the Vikings get on top early. The impact was evidenced through the time of possession, Cousins' offense holding the ball for 17.55 minutes in the first half and 35.16 a week on since the Vikings mustered just 17 minutes and 28 seconds of possession against the Bills. What a difference some respite for one of the league's most potent defenses makes.

There was a nice moment in the second half when former New Orleans Saints quarterback Drew Brees paid tribute to Cousins' communication at the line of scrimmage, where he shifted personnel and changed the play like an orchestra conductor. It was long-lost control and assurance under center.

Cousins later executed a trick play that saw him pump fake left and the swivel to pump fake to his right before tossing to Gavin Bartholomew over the middle of the field for a touchdown. For Kevin O'Connell to dial up a play like that just days after Cousins' arrival is testament to the footballing brain now leading Minnesota's offense.

"It was emotional coming to this stadium three years ago, tearing my Achilles here. It's been a tough three years, just grateful for the opportunity to play here, grateful for my teammates and what they did to make this outcome possible.

"It's been a tough three years. There's more of the story to be written," said Cousins post-game, his voice cracking several times."

Cousins won just one playoff game in six seasons during his first stint with the Vikings, before signing a four-year $180m contract with the Atlanta Falcons in 2024, only to be bench for Michael Penix Jr in his first season. He was then released in March earlier this year before landing in Las Vegas as something of a bridge towards their new era under Mendoza.

What looked like a declining career hurtling towards its end is instead flirting with one final twist.

What we learned

Patrick Mahomes' new friends are alright. The Kansas City Chiefs were without their best player this season in Kenneth Walker III on Sunday; it did not matter. The absence of last season's Super Bowl MVP paved the way for an increased role for fifth-round rookie running back Emmett Johnson, who capitalised emphatically with 22 carries for 101 yards and six catches for 70 yards and two scores through the air as Kansas City beat the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 in a five-touchdown day for Patrick Mahomes. Johnson showcased his menu of evasive manoeuvres in the open field with a clinic in tackle-missing jukes and the yards-after-catch threat primed to see him become one of Andy Reid's favourite weapons over the second half of the season.

There was also a debut for wide receiver Josh Downs, who had four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown in his first game since arriving via a trade from the Indianapolis Colts. It's been a long time since Mahomes and the Chiefs posed a consistent vertical threat but Downs could prove an answer to as much. Mahomes completed seven of 12 attempts on passes of 10-plus air yards for 206 yards and three touchdowns, while going three of six on attempts of 20-plus yards for 132 yards and two scores. The Chiefs offense is clicking.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player All of Patrick Mahomes five touchdowns in the Kansas City Chiefs' win over the Atlanta Falcons

Denzel Ward is playing at an All-Pro level. It is hard to be one of the best players on the league for so long on a team that has been bad for so long; Myles Garrett did it in Cleveland, and Denzel Ward is still doing it. He stepped up when the Browns needed him most on Sunday with a stunning diving pass break-up against Xavier Hutchinson to deny the Houston Texans with 30 seconds left in Cleveland's 27-24 victory. Ward allowed just four receptions for 16 yards from nine targets on Sunday while lining up against Nico Collins in man coverage on 10 of 11 routes, according to Next Gen Stats. Pat Surtain II may still hold the honour of top dog in the eyes of many, but Ward will feel he holds a strong argument as being the best corner in football.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Veteran NFL referee Gene Steratore admitted he'd never seen this play from Tory Horton, who jumped him to keep the ball from going out of the endzone for a touchback

There are encouraging signs for Fernando Mendoza. The Raiders ushered in a new chapter this weekend as No 1 overall Draft pick Mendoza led his side out against the Seattle Seahawks in his first regular season start following Cousins' trade to the Vikings. It started strongly with a touchdown run on his opening possession before Mike Macdonald dialled the pressure up a notch on defense in the second half as the Raiders offense suffered without star weapon Brock Bowers. He went 11 of 13 for 90 yards through the air in the first half, before managing just six of 16 for 53 yards following the interval. Mendoza finished the game 17 of 29 passing for 143 yards, zero touchdowns and zero turnovers while being sacked six times. Facing the league's best defense always beckoned as a baptism of fire, so the shortage of interceptions or apparent ball security issues was a plus point.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Seattle Seahawks against the Las Vegas Raiders from Week 10 of the NFL season

Overreaction or reality?

Brock Purdy is a top five quarterback in the NFL. For somebody so often pigeonholed as a 'system quarterback', he sure does do a lot of good outside of the system. Purdy continues to showcase an elite ability to extend plays and create outside of the pocket, perhaps best epitomised by the 74-yard McCaffrey touchdown catch-and-run that saw him side-step a near-certain sack, slide to his left, cut back inside and fire a dart to his open running back. Poise in the face of chaos and a ground threat that makes him dangerous off-script. Purdy finished the game 22 of 28 for 389 yards and three touchdowns with a 154.5 passer rating. He is in the MVP hunt and playing at a level among the premier play-callers in football. By now, though, he knows his true judgement comes around playoff time.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Detroit Lions wide receiver Isaac TeSlaa makes an unbelievable catch against the New England Patriots in Munich

Winners and losers

Winners:

Christian McCaffrey: If you thought injury setbacks had zapped the juice in the 49ers running back, think again. McCaffrey went off for 223 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns to tear apart of hobbling Cowboys defense, which surrendered a franchise-worst 584 yards at home. McCaffrey's 161 receiving yards were the most by a running back in a game since Jamaal Charles' 195 in 2013, while he is the first 49ers player with 200 scrimmage yards and three scores in a regular season game since Jerry Rice in 1995.

Parker Washington: Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen called him the best player on the field, and a man possessed. The Tennessee Titans could not live with Parker Washington as the Jags receiver took another major step closer towards a bumper new contract with a career-best seven catches for 152 yards and a touchdown in his side's 40-23 win. One play saw him put Alontae Taylor in a blender with another clinic in route-running, another play saw him levitate to haul in Trevor Lawrence's pass at the sideline, and another saw him race free for a 50-yard catch-and-run. His outstanding season continues.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Detroit Lions' Aidan Hutchinson injured himself while celebrating a sack of New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye in Germany

Losers:

Mike Vrabel: On more than one occasion on Sunday, the camera captured Mike Vrabel closing his eyes in excruciating thought at the sight of another setback for his Patriots, be it an injury or a pre-snap penalty. The game was over before it ever really began for last year's beaten Super Bowl finalists, Drake Maye departing after the opening drive through injury and a sputtering offense later losing AJ Brown in the latest disruption to what is threatening to become a nightmare maiden season in New England. They are 5-5 with the Buffalo Bills, Minnesota Vikings and Kansas City Chiefs coming up over the next month; their season is teetering on the edge.

Aidan Hutchinson: Perhaps it is unfair to kick a man when he is down, but it is hard to overlook a game-ending, potentially season-ending injury caused by a celebration. Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson is feared to have suffered a serious knee injury after landing awkwardly during a post-sack celebration on the opening drive of New England's defeat to the Lions in Munich. It was the same play that saw Maye suffer his own game-halting injury, with neither returning to the field. His absence would leave Detroit without their star edge rusher heading into the second half of their playoff charge

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Amon-Ra St. Brown scores a stunning 56-yard TD in Munich for the Detroit Lions

Player of the Weekend - Jahmyr Gibbs, RB, Detroit Lions

Jahmyr Gibbs is a familiar resident in this slot, but he is impossible to ignore as the clear frontrunner for Offensive Player of the Year through 10 weeks. The Lions running back was at his scintillating best in Munich as he put up 252 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns to torch the Patriots defense, his 62 career touchdowns breaking Terrell Davis' record for most by a player through his first four seasons in NFL history. He is not only the perfect cocktail of speed and shiftiness, but one of the smartest crease detectors in football. He runs hard, he runs fast, he runs with high-powered intelligence as the focal point of Drew Petzing's Lions offense. Another clinic, this time on European soil, to extend his lead as the NFL leader in scrimmage yards.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Amon-Ra St. Brown scores his second touchdown of the game to extend the Detroit Lions' lead over the New England Patriots

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Miami Dolphins cornerback Chris Johnson intercepts Daniel Jones to score a touchdown

Game of the Weekend

The 49ers and the Cowboys go way back as one of the NFL's most storied rivalries between two of football's most prestigious franchises. They renewed their dislike to the sight of record numbers as they combined for a series-high 86 points, with San Francisco beating Dallas 46-40 to improve to 8-1 on the season. While the 49ers flexed their offensive power, in doing so there were more glaring concerns over the Cowboys and a defense ranked third worst in yards allowed. Dak Prescott threw five touchdown passes, three to George Pickens, as the Cowboys put up 439 yards of offense, only to come out second best. Purdy produced two scoring strikes to McCaffrey and one to Deebo Samuel.

"The second half was unacceptable; tackling was atrocious, you can't give up three explosive plays of over 65 yards for touchdowns and expect to win. Totally unacceptable defense in the second half," said Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer.

Sports.title: Khawaja ready to be frozen out by Cricket Australia after sandpaper storm
Sports.content:
Usman Khawaja says being frozen out by Cricket Australia would be a "small price to pay" after his claims about the 2018 ball-tampering affair in South Africa.

Khawaja alleged in his autobiography 'Sabr' that every member of the Australia dressing room was aware of the plot to alter the condition of the ball with sandpaper and not just the players who copped bans in Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft.

The 39-year-old's account has been backed up by former team-mates Warner and Chadd Sayers but vehemently denied by current Test captain Pat Cummins, who was part of the bowling group in the series against the Proteas eight years ago.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Former Australia seam bowler Chadd Sayers has backed up Khawaja's claims that knowledge of the application of sandpaper was widespread

Khawaja retired from international cricket after Australia's 4-1 Ashes thrashing of England earlier this year but continues to play for Brisbane Heat in the Big Bash League.

'I have stood up for three guys I feel were treated unfairly'

Speaking on an episode of the They Used to Be podcast, which was recorded before Cummins' called Khawaja's claims about 'Sandpapergate' "100 per cent wrong and "utter nonsense", the batter said: "I still have a very good relationship with (Cricket Australia chief executive) Todd Greenberg.

"What happens to that relationship in the future, honestly [I don't know]. If Cricket Australia for some reason doesn't want to, it's a small price to pay in my mind for doing what I did.

Image: Khawaja has retired from international cricket but still plays for Brisbane Heat in the Big Bash League

"I have stood up for three guys I feel were treated unfairly (Warner, Smith and Bancroft).

"But there are other guys that are still playing in the team right now that there might be some sort of cost. I have tried my best to balance that out.

"There is always a cost in everything you do. There has been a cost to my family, too. But I am also not playing the victim here, because I knew what I was getting into.

"I knew what was coming. I just didn't realise it would be so personal."

Khawaja: 'Sandpapergate' bans were 'grotesquely overboard'

On the podcast, Khawaja spoke of an "awkward" conversation with Smith before the release of his book.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Australia's stand-in ODI captain Mitchell Marsh declined to comment on 'Sandpapergate' ahead of their series against England

He also called the penalties dished out following the sandpaper storm as "grotesquely overboard" and "over the top" with then-skipper Smith and vice-captain Warner hit with year-long suspensions and Bancroft banned for nine months.

Warner was also told he could not captain again before that sanction was lifted years later.

Cricket Australia CEO Greenberg said recently that there was "no compelling reason" to re-open any investigation into the scandal.

Khawaja added: "I'm not here to say 'he did this', 'that person did that, or 'he knew this or he knew that'.

"It was more a case of 'we win as a team, we lose as a team, we take chances as a team'. I think if there is an opportunity to do that, we can move forward once and for all."

Sports.title: 'All the force!' - Mercedes open to prioritising Russell in final races
Sports.content:
Toto Wolff says Mercedes could throw their weight behind George Russell over the final three races of the season to help him finish second in the Drivers' Championship.

Mercedes have already secured a world championship double this year, with Kimi Antonelli clinching the drivers' title in Mexico before the team wrapped up the constructors' crown a week later in Brazil.

But a difficult run of results for Russell since his last win at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in September has seen the Briton slip out of the top two in the Drivers' Championship. He is third, 17 points behind Red Bull's Max Verstappen in second and only one point ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton in fourth.

Speaking after the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, Wolff was asked whether, with both titles now won, Mercedes would prioritise Russell over the final three rounds to help get him back into second place behind Antonelli.

"I haven't thought about the driver championship yet, but we absolutely want him to score the maximum and hopefully finish second," said the Mercedes team principal.

Drivers' Championship - Battle for second 2) Max Verstappen, Red Bull - 279 points

3) George Russell, Mercedes - 262 points

4) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari - 261 points

5) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari - 249 points

6) Lando Norris, McLaren - 246 points

"And we need to think about what we're going to do about it.

"But it could be a possibility that we're giving it all the force."

Pre-season title favourite Russell has endured a disappointing season in which under-performance relative to Antonelli and misfortune have combined to leave him more than 100 points behind his team-mate.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli having won the world title at the last race, George Russell reflects on what has been a tough season for him

But Wolff is expecting the 28-year-old to bounce back strongly in 2027.

"He will recover," said Wolff. "I have no doubt about that for next year.

"And all the very best sports people have gone through difficult periods and that's going to be a part of his continued development."

Russell's hitherto best F1 championship finish is fourth, which he achieved in 2022 and 2025.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater gives his verdict on a wet Sao Paulo GP, where Lando Norris won, Max Verstappen fought from the back and Mercedes took the constructors' title

'2027 season has started now' - Wolff says next season won't be easy for Mercedes

While Mercedes have become world champions again with room to spare this year, the early-season dominance that laid the significant groundwork for their title triumphs in the first season of the sport's latest ruleset appears a long time ago now.

Antonelli's win at the United States Grand Prix last month is their only victory in the last five races amid ever-increasing competitiveness between the grid's four teams at the front of the field.

Wolff believes all three of Mercedes chief rivals will be in next year's world title fight.

"Look at the last few races, we haven't won," said Wolff.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following Mercedes claiming the 2026 F1 Constructors' Championship, team principal Toto Wolff sends a message to the team's workforce back in the UK

"At the beginning of the race [in Brazil], Kimi was just storming away, it looked like this could be ours. But the competition has been getting tougher between Ferrari, McLaren, Red Bull and ourselves.

"It's four teams that can win races and will be challenging for a world championship.

"And I have no doubt that it's going to be very difficult for us next year. For me, the 2027 season has started now.

Sports.title: Grand Slam of Darts: Four seeds crash out as Greaves exits despite win
Sports.content:
Seeds Jonny Clayton, Ross Smith, Josh Rock and Luke Woodhouse were all knocked out of the Grand Slam of Darts on Sunday, while Beau Greaves was also eliminated.

Fifth seed Clayton was demolished 5-1 in barely 10 minutes by former world champion Rob Cross, who posted an impressive 114 average and finishing stats of 83 per cent.

Clayton was the second seed to be eliminated on Sunday after 15th-seed Luke Woodhouse lost 5-1 to Krzysztof Ratajski.

In the final match of the afternoon session, eighth seed Josh Rock knew he could not afford to lose three legs to Kevin Doets, but he ultimately lost the match 5-3.

And in the evening session, sixth seed Smith beat Gabriel Clemens 5-4, but conceded too many legs and exits the tournament following Saturday's shock loss to Rusty-Jake Rodriguez.

Meanwhile, three-time Women's World Matchplay champion Greaves enjoyed a 5-3 win against Niels Zonneveld, but the scoreline was not enough to keep her in the competition.

Lisa Ashton, Cam Crabtree, Raymond Smith, Adam Sevada, Maik Kuivenhoven, Jan Schmidt, Carl Sneyd and Joe Hunt also had group-stage exits confirmed on Sunday.

Sunday's Grand Slam of Darts results

Group A: Niels Zonneveld 3-5 Beau Greaves

Beau Greaves recovered from 3-1 down to beat Niels Zonneveld 5-3, but the scoreline was not good enough to see her progress from this year's 'Group of Death'.

Greaves dominated her opponent in the second half of the match, but her 5-2 defeat to Luke Littler on Saturday night sees her once again fail to get out of a group with The Nuke now the hot favourite to progress to the last 16.

Group B: Alan Soutar 5-2 Lisa Ashton

Lisa Ashton will need to wait another year for her first win in the Grand Slam of Darts, as she fell to a 5-2 loss to Alan Soutar. That result means whoever wins Monday's clash between Soutar and Jermaine Wattimena will progress.

Group C: Josh Rock 3-5 Kevin Doets

After losing his opening match to Tommy Morris on Saturday, Premier League star Josh Rock knew he needed to beat Kevin Doets and concede no more than two legs in order to stay in the tournament.

However, Doets posted a 100 average and five 180s as he stormed to a 5-3 victory to eliminate Rock and set up a Monday night showdown with Morris.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cam Crabtree nailed a mega 146 checkout against Ricky Evans during their Group K clash

Group D: Cameron Menzies 5-4 Raymond Smith

Cameron Menzies fought back from 3-1 down to beat Raymond Smith 5-4 and set up a Monday night decider with Stephen Bunting to see who tops the group.

A spectacular 162 finish in the sixth leg levelled the scores and helped to eliminate the unfortunate Smith, who lost final-leg deciders in both of his matches at the Grand Slam.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look as Wayne Mardle was left in hysterics after Joe Hunt dropped a dart whilst trying to juggle

Group E: Sebastian Bialecki 5-4 Joe Hunt

Joe Hunt averaged more than 94 and threw a dozen 140s, but was still eliminated from the Grand Slam of Darts in a thrilling 5-4 defeat to Sebastian Bialecki on Sunday evening.

The Polish player edged a last-leg decider to pick up two points and he will now face Gerwyn Price on Monday night to decide who reaches the knockout stage.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Andrew Gilding punished Charlie Manby's wayward finishing to win their Grand Slam match on the bullseye

Group F: Andrew Gilding 5-4 Charlie Manby

Andrew Gilding averaged just 81, but still found a way to eliminate Charlie Manby from the Grand Slam with a 5-4 victory.

Manby missed his first 12 darts at double in the match before recovering to establish a 3-2 lead, but his opponent won three of the final four legs, ultimately securing the win with a classy 124 checkout on bullseye. He will face Ryan Searle on Monday to decide who progresses.

Group G: Jonny Clayton 1-5 Rob Cross

Jonny Clayton won the opening leg of his must-win clash against Rob Cross, but didn't attempt another double as he was knocked out of the tournament in brutal fashion.

Cross reeled off five legs in a row, including finishes of 138 and 137 in a ruthless performance and will look to take that form into his group decider with Anton Ostlund on Monday.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Niko Springer almost threw an amazing three 'Robin Hoods' in his match against Adam Sevada

Group H: Niko Springer 5-1 Adam Sevada

Niko Springer managed TWO Robin Hoods (where a dart lands in the flight of a previous dart and scores no points) but still cruised to a 5-1 win over Adam Sevada.

That means the winner of Springer's clash with Wessel Nijman on Monday night will reach the last 16.

Group I: Joe Cullen 2-5 Paolo Nebrida

Joe Cullen suffered a surprise defeat to Paolo Nebrida who kept his hopes of qualification alive with a 5-2 victory.

In a game of poor-quality finishing, the players missed 30 darts at a double between them in seven legs, and while Luke Humphries is now a heavy favourite to progress from Group I, all three players can still technically qualify.

Group J: Luke Woodhouse 1-5 Krzysztof Ratajski

World No 17 Luke Woodhouse became one of the biggest casualties of the tournament so far as he lost five legs in a row in a 5-1 defeat to Krzysztof Ratajski.

That makes it two defeats in two games for 'Woody', while Ratajski will take on Tom Sykes on Tuesday night to decide who makes it into the next round.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cam Crabtree nailed a mega 146 checkout against Ricky Evans during their Group K clash

Group K: Ricky Evans 5-4 Cam Crabtree

After losing 5-1 to James Wade on Saturday, Cam Crabtree needed to avoid losing two legs against Ricky Evans on Sunday to stay in the competition.

The pair served up a quickfire contest to the Wolverhampton crowd and Crabtree missed two match darts, but was ultimately knocked out by Evans who will now face Wade to decide the group.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look as Henry Coates roared after hitting a sensational 130 against Jeffrey De Graaf

Group L: Jeffrey de Graaf 4-5 Henry Coates

Henry Coates took Michael van Gerwen to a last-leg decider on Saturday night and the 20-year-old was involved in another thriller on Sunday as he beat Jeffrey de Graaf 5-4.

The result means all three players could still technically qualify from the group.

Group M: Bradley Brooks 5-3 Carl Sneyd

Carl Sneyd's tournament was ended by an impressive display from Bradley Brooks, who threw five 180s and averaged more than 97 in a 5-3 win.

Brooks will now take on third seed Gian van Veen on Tuesday night, seeking an upset victory to make his way into the second round.

Group N: Martin Schindler 5-0 Jan Schmidt

Martin Schindler whitewashed Jan Schmidt 5-0 in the opening match of the evening session to eliminate his fellow German from the tournament.

Both players struggled on their doubles, but Schindler is the only player who hasn't lost a leg and can now focus on Tuesday's winner-takes-all clash with Chris Dobey to decide who tops the group.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look as Gabriel Clemens hit a classy 130 bullseye checkout against Ross Smith

Group O: Ross Smith 5-4 Gabriel Clemens

Ross Smith was one of the favourites to win the Grand Slam of Darts, but exits at the group stage despite a gutsy win over Gabriel Clemens.

The European champion needed to win 5-3 or better to keep his tournament hopes alive, but a checkout ratio of less than 19 per cent proved his undoing.

Group P: Karel Sedlacek 4-5 Maik Kuivenhoven

Maik Kuivenhoven was eliminated from the tournament but still recovered from 4-1 down to beat Karel Sedlacek 5-4.

That leaves Sedlacek needing a big win over Nathan Aspinall on Tuesday night to qualify.

Sports.title: England talking points: Tuchel learns Argentina lesson as full-backs shine
Sports.content:
After England beat Spain in their own back yard in a statement result, we look at the main talking points from a memorable moment in Madrid...

Bold England show their strengths with front-foot approach

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Thomas Tuchel believes victory over world champions Spain was England's best performance so far under his leadership

England's football DNA has been in focus this autumn. In Madrid, we saw the English style at its best. From the first whistle, England were boldly on the front foot, overwhelming Spain with pace, power and directness.

They snapped into tackles and gave short shrift to their opponents when they called for fouls. It was physical, it was aggressive. It was certainly not England trying to replicate the Spanish style.

The set-piece routine for the second goal was a reflection of how those phases have risen in importance in the Premier League and fittingly saw two Arsenal players combine to score it. Then, when down to 10 men, there was fight, heart and commitment to get over the line.

Roy Keane called England's performance "perfect" at half-time. The errors from Jarell Quansah, Elliot Anderson and Anthony Gordon meant it certainly couldn't be called that in the end. But England's attitude and approach outweighed their mistakes. This is football England fans will get behind.

Peter Smith

Tuchel has learned from the Argentina game

Image: Tuchel was more measured in his substitutions

Tuchel didn't want to be drawn too much on comparisons between this win and the World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina.

He signalled a few times that the main takeaways about his team should come in the first 65 minutes before the red card - and even said the dogged defensive display was more like the last 16 win over Mexico. "The Azteca reloaded," he said.

But the England manager has clearly learned his lessons from the Argentina heartbreak. This was a very different approach to hanging on.

There was no back five this time. Not for a single second, even with the man disadvantage. It was so different to the World Cup. Against Argentina, he went to a back five on 72 minutes. Against Mexico, it was Dan Burn time on 75 minutes.

But Elliot Anderson's red card prompted no panic from the England bench. Anderson's hole was replaced by Jude Bellingham, who shifted back from the No 10 role. The first sub came with 10 minutes to go. Burn was only introduced on 89 minutes, but only for another defender.

There was trust from the England manager that his team could hold off the best team in the world in a back four defensive shape. That confidence led to a composed challenge, whereas against Argentina, there wasn't that faith.

And as a result, England fans have more faith in Tuchel.

Sam Blitz

Kane shows his Ballon d'Or class

Image: Kane did brilliantly to win the penalty that he eventually converted

'Harry Kane, he's the best in the world' sang the England supporters about their Ballon d'Or winner, goading their Spanish hosts and a certain Lamine Yamal who finished in third place for the coveted prize.

In the build-up to this game, Spain player after Spain player came out to say their team-mate should have won it instead of Kane. But England's captain showed his brilliance where it mattered - on the pitch.

He won and coolly converted the penalty for the opening goal. Nerves of steel after crucially missing from the spot against the same opponents in September. He helped orchestrate the third goal, too, which was just one example of his many connections with Jude Bellingham.

England's record scorer and record appearance-maker is at the peak of his powers right now.

Peter Smith

Hall stars in battle with Lamine Yamal

Image: Lewis Hall won the battle up against Lamine Yamal

This was the night Lewis Hall went to a whole new level.

He won praise earlier this year for the way he marshalled Lamine Yamal at St James' Park in the Champions League. But Barcelona put seven past Newcastle in the second leg of that tie, so there was no guarantee this would be a positive experience for the left-back.

Hall, however, leaves Madrid with the England left-back spot nailed down and plenty wondering why he wasn't at the World Cup.

There was brilliant defending, including a couple of tackles just before half-time where he single-handedly stopped Lamine Yamal and Mikel Merino in the England box. And even in the final seconds, he expertly won a goal-kick when Alex Baena threatened.

His appetite to take the game to Spain also impressed. He made five dribbles, epitomising England's front-foot gameplan. An all-round excellent display.

Peter Smith

And don't forget Ben White too!

Image: Ben White has completed an incredible England comeback

Imagine scoring to put England 3-0 up against Spain in Madrid and it's not your best moment of the match.

For Ben White, that standout moment came on 84 minutes. With Nico Williams bearing down on goal, White pulled off a superb sliding challenge as the last defender to prevent the one-on-one.

It was like Djed Spence against Argentina all over again, only this time England got the job done.

Image: White denied Nico Williams a Spain equaliser with a last-ditch tackle as the last defender

White has completed an incredible comeback in England colours. For so long, many thought he'd never play for his country again. Many have hounded him for coming back into the fold.

But this time the headlines are not about England fans booing him. Now it's whether he can hold down this right-back spot as his own.

Like Hall at left-back, England's right-back spot has been far from settled. White is England's sixth starting right-back in their last 11 games, dating back to the start of the World Cup knockout stages.

But this was a reminder of how good White is, why he deserves his England spot after impressing for the best club team in the country.

Sam Blitz

Trafford makes his case to be No 1

Tuchel was keen to play down talk of James Trafford ousting Jordan Pickford as England's No 1 after the game. But the young goalkeeper showed he has the ability to shine on the biggest stage in Madrid.

His double save late in the game was a decisive moment, with his reactions to keep out the second, deflected shot razor sharp. Tuchel was equally keen to praise his distribution and composure as England built up from deep.

He may have conceded four goals in two appearances against Spain in this Nations League group phase but he comes out of this period with his reputation enhanced and as the clear challenger to Pickford.

The Everton shot-stopper has never let England down but if the changing of the guard is to come in the near future, Trafford is in pole position to step in.

Peter Smith

England find out who they will face in the Nations League quarter-finals when the draw takes place on Friday November 20 at 11am.

The two-legged ties are scheduled for the March international break, with the first legs to be played between March 25 and 27 and the second legs between March 28 and 30.

Sports.title: Ten-man England hold on to claim famous win over Spain
Sports.content:
England withstood a Spain fightback after Elliot Anderson's red card to secure a famous 3-2 victory and finish above the world champions at the top of their Nations League group.

Thomas Tuchel's side were sensational for an hour in Madrid, taking the lead when Harry Kane scored a penalty at the end of the first half and then adding quickfire goals from Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

But a one-sided game was turned on its head when Elliot Anderson was sent off for a last-man foul on Lamine Yamal following Jarell Quansah's error, allowing Mikel Oyarzabal to score from the spot.

Spain reduced the deficit to one goal when substitute Nico Williams converted Lamine Yamal's cross after Anthony Gordon had been dispossessed, but England clung on thanks to James Trafford.

Image: Bellingham and Kane celebrate England's win over Spain

The goalkeeper, selected ahead of Jordan Pickford, made a string of saves as Spain peppered the England goal, including a stunning double stop when he denied Fermin Lopez then somehow pushed Oyarzabal's follow-up around the post at full stretch.

His heroics, in addition to a vital last-man challenge by White on Williams, allowed the Three Lions to end Spain's 43-game unbeaten run with a historic victory which ensures they will be seeded in the Nations League quarter-final draw.

Image: Harry Kane was fouled by Pau Cubarsi for England's penalty

Image: Kane dispatched the penalty for his 93rd England goal

It appeared certain to be a more emphatic victory when White drilled the third goal through the legs of Unai Simon after Konsa had headed in Declan Rice's corner for the second. Spain had not even registered a shot on target at that point.

But Anderson's red card, after Quansah was caught on the ball by Lamine Yamal, reinvigorated Spain and meant England had to show the qualities demonstrated in their World Cup last-16 win over Mexico at the Azteca Stadium in July.

Their steel, and the contribution of their goalkeeper, got them over the line - and showed evidence of progress from their World Cup semi-final exit to Argentina, when they lost their lead late on.

Image: James Trafford celebrates his double save with Ezri Konsa

Tuchel: We were at the highest level

England boss Thomas Tuchel:

"We are fully aware of the performance we put out there for 60-65 minutes. To be 3-0 up and deservedly 3-0 up.

"Of course the red card and penalty changed the momentum and the characteristic of the game. Thirty minutes against Spain, in Spain, feels like three hours.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Thomas Tuchel believes victory over world champions Spain was England's best performance so far under his leadership

"That is the statement and significance of this victory: that it was deserved and the result followed the performance.

"It was on the highest level in terms of belief, team spirit and togetherness. It was on highest level football wise on all aspects of the game.

"That was an excellent performance. A wonderful feeling in the dressing room. Everyone was very tired. We overcame some difficult moments.

"We're aware what steps we took now after the World Cup. It's the best feeling."

Rice: We knew we were going to beat them

England midfielder Declan Rice to ITV:

"We knew we could beat them. We knew we were going to beat them today.

"The message from the manager after the Croatia game was so positive. The message from the boys, everyone pushing together, knowing that we're going to come here and not sit back and hit them on the counter.

"We knew from the first minute - our first 10 minutes was probably the best we've played in a 10-minute spell. Pressure, pressure, pressure, we could have had two or three.

"The red card changes the course of the game as it could have been a couple more goals if I'm being honest."

Analysis by Sky Sports' Peter Smith:

England's football DNA has been in focus this autumn. In Madrid, we saw the English style at its best. From the first whistle, England were boldly on the front foot, overwhelming Spain with pace, power and directness.

They snapped into tackles and gave short shrift to their opponents when they called for fouls. It was physical, it was aggressive. It was certainly not England trying to replicate the Spanish style.

The set-piece routine for the second goal was a reflection of how they have risen in importance in the Premier League and fittingly saw two Arsenal players combine to score it. Then, when down to 10 men, there was fight, heart and commitment.

Roy Keane called England's performance "perfect" at half-time. The errors from Quansah, Anderson and Gordon meant it certainly couldn't be called that in the end. But England's attitude and approach outweighed their mistakes.

This is football England fans will get behind.

Sports.title: Grand Slam permutations: How Littler can be knocked out on Monday
Sports.content:
The Grand Slam of Darts has a brutal new format for 2026, which means every match on Monday and Tuesday night has something riding on it.

The 48-player field is split into 16 groups of three with only one going through, meaning each player has only two pool matches to try and earn a place in the second round.

Monday sees the conclusion of Groups A-H with Groups I-P to be concluded on Tuesday.

Read on to see how Luke Littler, Luke Humphries and Nathan Aspinall can all lose their final matches and still qualify for the last 16...

Group A

Sat Nov 14: Luke Littler 5-2 Beau Greaves

Luke Littler 5-2 Beau Greaves Sun Nov 15: Niels Zonneveld 3-5 Beau Greaves

Niels Zonneveld 3-5 Beau Greaves Mon Nov 16: Luke Littler v Niels Zonneveld

Luke Littler can afford to lose to Niels Zonneveld on Monday night and still have a chance of progressing.

The Nuke simply needs to win three legs to reach the last 16 with Zonneveld needing to win 5-2 or better to reach the knockout stages.

Beau Greaves is one of the few players to be eliminated despite winning one of her matches.

Group B

Sat Nov 14: Jermaine Wattimena 5-2 Lisa Ashton

Jermaine Wattimena 5-2 Lisa Ashton Sun Nov 15: Alan Soutar 5-2 Lisa Ashton

Alan Soutar 5-2 Lisa Ashton Mon Nov 16: Jermaine Wattimena v Alan Soutar

Lisa Ashton has been eliminated after losing both of her first two matches, which means whoever wins Monday's match between Jermaine Wattimena and Alan Soutar will reach the last 16.

Group C

Sat Nov 14: Josh Rock 2-5 Tommy Morris

Josh Rock 2-5 Tommy Morris Sun Nov 15: Josh Rock 3-5 Kevin Doets

Josh Rock 3-5 Kevin Doets Mon Nov 16: Kevin Doets v Tommy Morris

Eighth seed Josh Rock has been eliminated after two defeats, which means whoever wins the Kevin Doets v Tommy Morris clash on Monday will qualify for the knockout round.

Group D

Sat Nov 14: Stephen Bunting 5-4 Raymond Smith

Stephen Bunting 5-4 Raymond Smith Sun Nov 15: Cameron Menzies 5-4 Raymond Smith

Cameron Menzies 5-4 Raymond Smith Mon Nov 16: Stephen Bunting v Cameron Menzies

Two last-leg defeats mean that Raymond Smith has been eliminated from the competition. Cameron Menzies will face Stephen Bunting in a winner-goes-through decider on Monday.

Group E

Sat Nov 14: Gerwyn Price 5-3 Joe Hunt

Gerwyn Price 5-3 Joe Hunt Sun Nov 15: Sebastian Bialecki 5-4 Joe Hunt

Sebastian Bialecki 5-4 Joe Hunt Mon Nov 16: Gerwyn Price v Sebastian Bialecki

Joe Hunt crashed out after losing both of his match, so Gerwyn Price and Sebastian Bialecki will clash on Monday night with the winner reaching the knockout rounds.

Group F

Sat Nov 14: Ryan Searle 5-4 Charlie Manby

Ryan Searle 5-4 Charlie Manby Sun Nov 15: Andrew Gilding 5-4 Charlie Manby

Andrew Gilding 5-4 Charlie Manby Mon Nov 16: Ryan Searle v Andrew Gilding

Charlie Manby has been eliminated from the competition after suffering two last-leg defeats, meaning the victor in Monday's clash between Ryan Searle and Andrew Gilding will secure a spot in the last 16.

Group G

Sat Nov 14: Jonny Clayton 4-5 Anton Ostlund

Jonny Clayton 4-5 Anton Ostlund Sun Nov 15: Jonny Clayton 1-5 Rob Cross

Jonny Clayton 1-5 Rob Cross Mon Nov 16: Rob Cross v Anton Ostlund

Jonny Clayton was the highest-ranked player to be knocked out of the tournament on Sunday, meaning Rob Cross and Anton Ostlund will face off on Tuesday with the winner qualifying.

Group H

Sat Nov 14: Wessel Nijman 5-1 Adam Sevada

Wessel Nijman 5-1 Adam Sevada Sun Nov 15: Niko Springer 5-1 Adam Sevada

Niko Springer 5-1 Adam Sevada Mon Nov 16: Wessel Nijman v Niko Springer

Adam Sevada has been eliminated after two 5-1 losses, meaning the winner of Wessel Nijman vs Niko Springer on Monday night will reach the last 16.

Group I

Sat Nov 14: Luke Humphries 5-3 Paolo Nebrida

Luke Humphries 5-3 Paolo Nebrida Sun Nov 15: Joe Cullen 2-5 Paolo Nebrida

Joe Cullen 2-5 Paolo Nebrida Tue Nov 17: Luke Humphries v Joe Cullen

In Group I, all three players are still in the tournament.

Luke Humphries needs to win four or five legs against Joe Cullen on Monday night to reach the last 16. A 5-4 defeat would still be enough for him to qualify.

Cullen must win that match 5-0 to get through - while Paolo Nebrida will reach the last 16 if Cullen wins by a scoreline of 5-1, 5-2 or 5-3.

Group J

Sat Nov 14: Luke Woodhouse 3-5 Tom Sykes

Luke Woodhouse 3-5 Tom Sykes Sun Nov 15: Luke Woodhouse 1-5 Krzysztof Ratajski

Luke Woodhouse 1-5 Krzysztof Ratajski Tue Nov 17: Krzysztof Ratajski v Tom Sykes

Any sort of win for Michael van Gerwen on Tuesday will see him qualify for the last 16. However, a victory of 5-3 or better would see Jeffrey de Graaf take top spot.

Chris Dobey 5-2 Jan Schmidt Sun Nov 15: Martin Schindler 5-0 Jan Schmidt

Ross Smith 3-5 Rusty-Jake Rodriguez Sun Nov 15: Ross Smith 5-4 Gabriel Clemens

Ross Smith 5-4 Gabriel Clemens Tue Nov 17: Gabriel Clemens v Rusty-Jake Rodriguez

Gabriel Clemens is one of the few players to have lost a match but can still qualify for the last 16. He must beat Rusty-Jake Rodriguez 5-3 or better to top Group O.

Rusty-Jake Rodriguez simply needs to win four legs to qualify. A victory of a 5-4 defeat would be enough for him.

Group O favourite Ross Smith has already been eliminated, but can still finish second in the group if Rodriguez wins Tuesday's final match.

Group P

Sat Nov 14: Nathan Aspinall 5-1 Maik Kuivenhoven

Nathan Aspinall 5-1 Maik Kuivenhoven Sun Nov 15: Karel Sedlacek 4-5 Maik Kuivenhoven

Karel Sedlacek 4-5 Maik Kuivenhoven Tue Nov 17: Nathan Aspinall v Karel Sedlacek

Nathan Aspinall doesn't even need to win on Tuesday night. He will qualify if he wins just three legs against Karel Sedlacek.

After throwing away a 4-1 advantage against Maik Kuivenhoven, Karel Sedlacek knows he must beat Aspinall 5-2 or better if he wants to reach the next round.

Kuivenhoven has been eliminated from the tournament but will finish second in the group if Aspinall wins.

How does the new format work?

Instead of eight groups of four, the expanded 48-player field is now split into 16 groups of three.

Rather than the top two in each group progressing like in previous editions, only the top player from each group will progress.

In the group stage, two points will be awarded for a win, and no points are awarded for a defeat.

Should there be a three-way points tie in any group after the round-robin games have been played, these would be split as follows:

Total leg difference

Total legs won

Total legs won against throw

Highest total tournament average (to two decimal places)

Highest winning match average (to two decimal places)

If players cannot be split after the above criteria, a play-off will be organised between the players at the end of the session in which the final group game is played and will be a two or three-way nine-dart shootout in which the player scoring the most points is deemed the winner.

The order of throw would be determined by PDC ranking, with the highest ranked player having the option to throw first, second, or third.

Following the completion of the Group Stage, each group winner will progress to the knockout stage from the last 16 onwards, and the tournament will proceed in bracket order as follows:

Winner Group A v Winner Group B

Winner Group C v Winner Group D

Winner Group E v Winner Group F

Winner Group G v Winner Group H

Winner Group I v Winner Group J

Winner Group K v Winner Group L

Winner Group M v Winner Group N

Winner Group O v Winner Group P

Sports.title: England fend off fiery Spain fightback after Anderson’s red to top Nations League group
Sports.content:
It was the game to show Thomas Tuchel where his rebooted England team had got to; surely the ultimate test in international football. Spain in Spain. A world champion team who, in Tuchel’s words, had “forgotten how to lose.” Before this Nations League group decider, they had been beaten only once in 43 matches – on penalties against Portugal in the final of this competition last year.

What England produced for 65 minutes was extraordinary. What followed was equally so for different reasons. When it was over, England had made the most sensational of statements. Back in 2018, on their previous visit to Spain, England won 3-2 in Seville in the Nations League; it was one of Sir Gareth Southgate’s most famous results, an ignition point. It was the same scoreline and the same feeling for Tuchel on Sunday night.

England led 3-0. It was Harry Kane, of course, who put them in front from the penalty spot; the best player in the world damaging the best team. When Ezri Konsa and Ben White added the others, the travelling supporters were pinching themselves. With Jude Bellingham to the fore, England had run riot.

It was not over. Far from it. Everything changed when Jarell Quansah made a big error as the last man, robbed by Lamine Yamal, who got into the area and was fouled by Elliot Anderson. It was a red card for the England midfielder and a penalty for Spain. When Mikel Oyarzabal converted, it was the prompt for a siege.

Spain knocked hard at the door. They scored again through the substitute Nico Williams, created by an assist from the frankly ludicrous Lamine Yamal, a talent who sprinkles his magic liberally, and England were placed in grim survival mode. We have been here before under Tuchel and the equaliser looked on. The manager made a couple of defensive changes – Myles Lewis-Skelly for Kane and Djed Spence for Anthony Gordon. Bellingham was removed, too, and he departed shaking his head. Dan Burn came on towards the very end.

England held out. One of Tuchel’s major selection calls was to start James Trafford over Jordan Pickford in goal and he produced a remarkable stoppage-time double save to ensure England got the result they needed to leapfrog Spain and advance to the quarter-finals as the group winners. The second part of it was to deny Aymeric Laporte. It was a breathtaking moment; one to advance Trafford’s claim on the No 1 jersey. There were many others on a night that pulsed wildly from the outset – pretty much from when Spain paraded the World Cup trophy before kick-off. Had they not already had their homecoming with the gold? It was a power play.

England brought the swagger. They pressed hard on to the front foot. It was thrilling to see how they took on those in red and beat them, creating the sense of possibility. It was worth mentioning a spin move by Lewis Hall on halfway in the eighth minute when he could not afford to lose the ball. He did not, getting England up the field. There were other examples of the proactivity from other players; the desire to drop shoulders and surge forward, to be direct.

View image in fullscreen Harry Kane wheels away after opening the scoring from the spot – he got up from the foul that resulted in the penalty. Photograph: Michael Regan/The FA/Getty Images

It was England who looked likely to score first and Spain needed a superb save from Unai Simón to deny Bellingham in the early going. He ran on to a Declan Rice corner, centrally placed and, with the ball slightly behind him, he had to dig out the half-volley rather than hit it more cleanly. Simón’s reflexes were nevertheless impressive. Gordon had a shot blocked by Martín Zubimendi. Kane fizzed another one just wide.

Spain kicked out a foothold in the 15th minute. It was Lamine Yamal, inevitably, who dragged them back into it. He nutmegged Hall and blasted away from him, Rice bringing him down to pick up a yellow card. What Hall did next spoke volumes about England’s approach, not to mention his courage. It was a slicing run from him, on a diagonal towards goal, which laid waste to a host of Spain players. He almost found Morgan Rogers with his cross.

It was an excellent first half for England; Rogers bristled with confidence on the ball, Bellingham threatened. They deserved to take a lead into the interval. Bellingham appeared to be fouled by Marc Cucurella, but Anderson did not stand on ceremony, driving a first-time pass up the inside right channel for Kane, who cut inside Pau Cubarsí to set up the shot.

View image in fullscreen England's Ben White scores their third goal. Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/Reuters

Kane cleverly got his body between Cubarsí and the ball; the Spain centre-back had a problem. His challenge was necessary but clumsy; it was a clear penalty. Kane had a long wait while the video assistant referee checked for an Anderson foul on Cucurella as he followed through after his pass. It was accidental but nasty. Anderson got away with it. Kane had missed decisively in England’s 3-2 defeat against Spain at Wembley at the start of this competition. He made no mistake this time. It was his 93rd England goal.

England continued to push after half-time, especially Bellingham. He won the corner that led to Konsa heading in unmarked from a Rice outswinger and it was Bellingham who played in White, who was adventurous all night, for the third.

Quick Guide Nations League roundup: Belgium knock Italy out with victory Show Italy went into their clash in Brussels top of Group A1 after their 3-1 win against France on Thursday but came crashing back to Earth as they were comfortably beaten by Belgium. Pio Esposito gave Italy ⁠an early lead but their joy was short-lived as Belgium scored ​three times before the ​interval through Maxim De Cuyper, ​Nathan Ngoy and Jérémy Doku (pictured). Diego Moreira made it 4-1 in the 80th minute. France beat Turkey 2-1 in Bordeaux ​thanks to an own ‌goal by Emirhan ​Topcu and ​an effort by Bournemouth's Eli Junior Kroupi, meaning they won the group with 13 points, ahead of Belgium who ended on 12. Italy, on 10 points, missed out. England and Spain had already confirmed qualification to the quarter-finals before Sunday's dramatic clash between the sides in Madrid, which England won 3-2, but the remaining match in Group A3 saw Croatia beat Czechia 2-1, thanks to Lovro Majer's 87th-minute winner. In Group C1, Albania sealed top spot and promotion to League B after a 2-0 win over Belarus in Budapest. Rey Manaj and Elseid Hysaj scored goals in each half. Finland ended their campaign in the group with a 7-2 thumping of San Marino in Helsinki, headlined by a hat-trick by forward Adrian Svanbäck. San Marino are relegated to League D after failing to register a single point from their six games, ending with a goal difference of -22. In Group C2, Montenegro completed an unbeaten group campaign with a 4-1 victory in Cyprus. Genoa forward Milutin Osmajic got them off to a fast start in the fifth minute while Nikola Krstocic added a second-half double. Armenia and already-relegated Latvia played out a goalless draw in Riga. Reuters and Guardian sport Photograph: John Thys/AFP Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Nothing silly, Tuchel had to have thought. Quansah did something silly and the entire mood changed. Trafford made his first big save from the substitute Fermín López, but then it was 3-2 after Gordon was robbed in midfield. Spain went right to Lamine Yamal and his low cross for Williams was perfect.

Spain piled on the pressure. Williams went close. Lamine Yamal forced Trafford into a fine save, the goalkeeper denying Cucurella on the rebound. White made a saving tackle on Williams after a wonderful Lamine Yamal pass. Trafford saved his best until the last.

Sports.title: Mary Earps frustrates Arsenal as London City Lionesses earn battling draw
Sports.content:
Arsenal’s fifth draw from five home games in the Women’s Super League left them frustrated once again but this was a wholly different story to the previous four, as they played out an entertaining 1-1 draw with a London City Lionesses side inspired by their goalkeeper Mary Earps.

Aston Villa, Birmingham, Manchester United and Crystal Palace all came to this stadium for a point, defending resolutely and exposing Arsenal’s inability to break down low blocks, whereas London City came to play and were rewarded with a draw that maintains their six‑point advantage over Arsenal in the race for a European place, and moving within six points of the leaders Chelsea.

Earps, producing her best performance to date for the team she joined in the summer, repeatedly denied Frida Maanum and Lisa Baum and was named player of the match in a contest where both goals were scored inside the space of 99 seconds. The impressive Maanum finished off a superb team move for Arsenal to open the scoring in the 10th minute but her goal was cancelled out by a terrific finish from Isobel Goodwin whose head coach, Eder Maestre, said: “We came here to take risks. We really wanted to win.

“Our identity is playing with bravery – we were brave today. We weren’t scared about the context, the opponent, the stadium, nothing. We tried to play as we play at home.”

Arsenal had secured an impressive result in Barcelona on Thursday, drawing with the European champions, but this game against the WSL’s third-placed side felt as though it was of even greater importance, particularly if Arsenal wish to continue visiting venues such as the Camp Nou next season, and they were unable to find a way past Earps to win and close the gap in the table.

View image in fullscreen Isobel Goodwin shows her delight after equalising. Photograph: Ben Whitley/PA

Just like they had done away at Anfield last Sunday, Renée Slegers’s team made a bright start with energy, pace and the threat of Alessia Russo. Emily Fox’s shot was deflected wide, after a good move that included some excellent Maanum buildup play, before Ona Batlle’s long-range effort bounced wide. It was not long before Maanum tucked in the opening goal after an intelligent cutback from Russo.

The visitors struck back almost immediately, though, as Goodwin did superbly to turn inside Leah Williamson and then demonstrated strength and composure to hold off Baum and fire a lethal finish past Misa Rodríguez with power and precision. It was a timely moment of class from the English striker in front of the England head coach, Sarina Wiegman, who was in the stands before naming her next England squad on Tuesday morning.

Earps then twice saved from Baum from range. After the break, Earps did well again to dive low to her left to divert a Caitlin Foord strike wide, and what followed was a sustained spell of London City possession, territory and chances. Maestre’s team spent a good part of 20 minutes firmly camped in Arsenal’s half and they carved open a good chance for Kadidiatou Diani but her relatively tame, low, near-post effort was saved by Rodríguez.

Diani’s 62nd-minute replacement from the substitutes’ bench, Delphine Cascarino, drew gasps from the crowd as she unleashed a dipping strike that bounced off the top of the crossbar. It was a lucky escape for Arsenal, who had won all seven of their previous meetings with London City across all competitions but were denied by two more fine Earps stops, firstly from a Maanum close-range effort and then from Maanum’s curler, which looked destined for the top corner before Earps touched it on to the bar.
