Sports.title: England deliver the spectacular as Three Lions strip world champions Spain of their invincibility and give Thomas Tuchel the proof that his coaching IS working, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel had said he wanted evidence. He needed to believe his coaching was working. He needed to see something that told him he could help England overcome those DNA deficiencies he had identified in the aftermath of the devastating World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina.

He needed a glimpse of his England team closing the gap to the best. He needed to cling on to the idea that they could overhaul Spain, that the work he was doing could improve England so much they could win the European Championship in 2028 and end this country’s cursed cycle of despair.

Proof of concept, he called it on Saturday night when England arrived in Madrid. ‘This will be proof of concept on the highest level,’ Tuchel predicted. ‘It's the biggest test in world football. Spain seems unbeatable but we are trying to take it away from them. We are up for something spectacular.’

Something spectacular is what Tuchel promised and something spectacular is what both he and England delivered. Spain had not lost for 43 matches, a world record, but number 44 was beyond them. For just over an hour, England destroyed them. They outplayed them. They stripped them of their invincibility.

And then, when Elliot Anderson was sent off after 63 minutes for pulling back Lamine Yamal, and Spain stormed back into the game, England somehow managed to hold on for a momentous victory in the screaming, yelling cauldron of the Metropolitano. This was proof alright. This was proof positive.

Sure, it was nervy for half an hour. And, yes, England nearly found a way to throw it away. But the way they played when it was 11 v 11 was enough for any England fan to believe that England under Tuchel can climb back to the summit of a major tournament and gaze down on a view they have not seen for 60 years.

England recorded a famous victory over Spain in Madrid as they won a five-goal thriller

Elliot Anderson's red card opened the door for the world champions to mount a comeback

James Trafford made a superb double save in stoppage time to preserve England's lead

Yes, this was a Nations League dead rubber because both teams were already guaranteed progress to the quarter-finals next March, but there was no mistaking its wider significance. This was proof England are good enough to turn away from the trail of tears that has been their path for so long. Before the game, Spain had held the World Cup aloft again as one final reminder of England’s failure but by the end, by the time goalkeeper James Trafford had added to the drama with a miraculous double save, the glory and the 3-2 triumph was England’s.

Spain had won their last 12 matches in succession and the sport’s last two major tournament. They had not been beaten since March 2024 and had not lost at home since September 2022. England ended that run with 10 men. What a night. It was a special kind of crazy.

England had celebrated Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or triumph and caps record at Wembley last week but Spain took things a stage further before the game. The boys who won the U15 World Cup were introduced to the crowd. Then the World Cup itself was carried on for goalkeeper Unai Simon to hold aloft.

England ignored it all. They started the game like an express train. They nearly took the lead inside the first two minutes when Jude Bellingham met a corner from Declan Rice on the edge of the six-yard-box and was only denied by a brilliant reaction save from Simon. Gordon’s follow-up was destined for the bottom corner before it was blocked by a Spain defender.

Spain were rattled. The crowd whistled. England forced their opponents into mistake after mistake at the back. From one of those successful presses, Kane drilled a shot inches wide. Gordon, who has made such a fine start to his Barcelona career, revelled on the stage and caused right back Marc Pubill all manner of anxieties.

Spain could barely break out of their own half but when they did, after a quarter of an hour, Yamal ran at Lewis Hall and nutmegged him before Rice chopped the teenager down. Rice was booked by French referee Clement Turpin and Lamal windmilled his hands in the air to wind up the crowd.

Pubill was replaced midway through the half. It looked like an injury but it could have been hurt pride or twisted blood. Gordon had barely given him a moment’s rest. In fact, Gordon was tireless. He harried Martin Zubimendi off the ball with ease and almost set up a chance for Bellingham.

England got the goal they deserved a minute before half-time. The build-up was controversial. Anderson played a fine through ball to Kane that doubled as a crunching tackle on Marc Cucurella. Cucurella went down as if he had been shot, which is what Cucurella always does.

Ben White slotted the ball through the keeper's legs after a brilliant England move

Harry Kane celebrates goal No 93 for England after giving them the lead from the penalty spot

The referee allowed play to continue. Kane advanced on goal and turned inside Pau Cubarsi, Spain’s brilliant young defender. Cubarsi brought him down and the referee pointed to the spot. Cucurella still lay prone. Bellingham, his Real Madrid teammate, leaned over him and told him what he thought of him.

There were a whole host of VAR checks but England passed all of them. The crowd whistled their distaste. Kane missed a penalty in the Wembley game between these two teams in September but he did not miss this one. Simon guessed the right way but Kane hit it too fiercely and it bulged the back of the net. It was his 93rd goal for England.

Spain are not used to being bossed around like this. Tempers flared after the whistle blew for half-time. Ben White and Fabian Ruiz joined in a disagreement of some sort and soon there was a flurry of pushing and shoving. It stopped short of being a melee but it was obvious Spain were shaken.

Eight minutes into the second half, England went further ahead. Rice swung a corner into the centre of the box and, as the usual wrestling match unfolded, Ezri Konsa ran in gloriously unmarked and nodded the ball down and past the helpless Simon from close range.

Four minutes later, against a general backdrop of disbelief, England were three ahead. What a goal it was, too. Bellingham, who had been his usual superhuman self, muscled his way free in the centre and fed the ball out to Kane.

Kane held the ball up and played it back to Bellingham on the edge of the box. Bellingham spotted the overlapping run of White and found him with a clever pass. White took a touch and slotted the ball past Simon. It was the Arsenal full-back’s first competitive England start, too. Maybe now England fans will stop booing him.

This was the night Thomas Tuchel had been crying out for as he got the evidence he demanded

Ezri Konsa met Declan Rice's set-piece to plant an unstoppable header in the back of the net

But then, midway through the half, England gave Spain a lifeline. Jarell Quansah was caught in possession by Yamal and as Yamal bore down on goal, Anderson pulled him back. Anderson was shown a red card and Spain were awarded a penalty. Oyarzabal waited for Trafford to commit himself and then stroked the ball into the opposite corner.

The atmosphere in the stadium was transformed. Spain sensed vulnerability in England for the first time. Fifteen minutes from time, they pulled another goal back. Yamal sprinted away down the right and slid the ball into the middle for substitute Nico Williams, who sidefooted it past Trafford.

Now, it was like the Alamo. Yamal tormented England. Trafford dived at full length to push away one of his shots and then got down at his near post to divert a shot that was creeping in. White produced another of the moments of the night with a flying block to keep out a goalbound shot from Williams.

Spain through everything at England but England would not yield. When Trafford made that double save, everyone knew. It was to be England’s night. Tuchel had his proof of concept.

Sports.title: Jarrad Branthwaite left out of England squad for Nations League decider with Spain - as James Hill and Dan Burn leapfrog defender in Thomas Tuchel's pecking order
Sports.content:
Jarrad Branthwaite left out of England squad for Nations League decider with Spain - as James Hill and Dan Burn leapfrog defender in Thomas Tuchel's pecking order

Jarrad Branthwaite has been left out of England’s matchday squad for the Nations League decider in Spain, raising questions over his future involvement under Thomas Tuchel.

The Everton centre back’s omission means that two rivals who were not in the original squad but were added last week, Dan Burn and James Hill, are now seemingly ahead of him in the pecking order.

There was a clue as to Tuchel’s uncertainty over Branthwaite when, ahead of last Thursday's Croatia game, he revealed concerns over his suitability to England’s way of playing.

‘Jarrad Branthwaite is doing very well but it's a very different style of play for him from Everton towards us,’ said the head coach.

Tuchel then selected Burn ahead of him for the 2-1 win, and said: ‘You can see that Dan Burn is straight away a big voice in training and is more used to the style with Newcastle from the last two seasons with Eddie Howe, where they followed in a high press and man-to-man.’

It had been thought that Branthwaite, 24, could emerge as a starter at left-sided centre back, given his good club form this season. That now feels unlikely, with Burn and Marc Guehi, who is currently injured, preferred by Tuchel.

Jarrad Branthwaite has been left out of the England squad for their clash against Spain

James Hill and Dan Burn, who were both added to the England squad last week, appear to have jumped above Branthwaite in the pecking order

Branthwaite has made two substitute appearances under the German, totalling 28 minutes. Also left out of the matchday squad for Sunday’s game in Madrid are Josh King and James Garner.

Everton midfielder Garner came off the bench against Croatia at Wembley and thought he had scored his first England goal, only for VAR to rule it out for offside. He now misses the chance to build on that cameo against the world champions.

For King, 19, the wait for a senior debut continues after his maiden call-up, a reward for an impressive start to the season with Fulham. Tuchel was forced to trim three players from his 26-man travelling squad, with the return to fitness of defenders Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence increasing competition for places.

Sports.title: Spain 2-3 England PLAYER RATINGS: Which star was the man of the match for Thomas Tuchel? Who was key to their energy and adventure? And who now deserves a run in the side?
Sports.content:
Spain 2-3 England PLAYER RATINGS: Which star was the man of the match for Thomas Tuchel? Who was key to their energy and adventure? And who now deserves a run in the side?

England secured a historic victory over Spain in the Nations League to secure top spot in their group ahead of their quarter-final matchup next year.

Thomas Tuchel's side raced out the blocks to cause the world champions trouble early on, but Unai Simon ensured Spain held firm and weathered the early storm.

England did get their reward, though, just before half-time when Harry Kane won and scored a penalty to give his side a deserved lead.

After the break, they went up a gear, with Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White netting to leave England in dreamland.

That was until Elliot Anderson was sent off – conceding a penalty against Lamine Yamal in the process – and Spain were back in it through Mikel Oyarzabal. Nico Williams then ensured it would be a nervy last 15 minutes for England, but they held on and secured the 3-2 victory.

Daily Mail Sport's CRAIG HOPE was in Madrid to rate the Three Lions players.

England secured a thrilling 3-2 win over Spain on Sunday to top their Nations League group

James Trafford produced a fantastic double save in stoppage time to keep his side in front

ENGLAND (4-2-3-1)

James Trafford – 8

His big test and was hardly tested first-half. That changed when down to 10 and produced three big saves, including a stunner in stoppage-time.

Ben White – 8

Solid if unspectacular… at least until spectacular, overlapping goal for England’s third. Shades of Carlos Alberto. Warrants a stay in side.

Jarell Quansah – 5

Looked composed until needless dawdling on ball that cost his team a penalty, a goal and a man. Spoilt decent display.

Ezri Konsa – 9

Furthered claims as first-choice centre back. Was commanding, organised well and headed brilliant second goal. Player of the match.

Lewis Hall – 8

Surely England’s No1 left back now. Two early dribbles were Yamal-esque. A tougher second-half and was out of position for Spain’s second.

Elliot Anderson – 6

Superb ball to free Kane for penalty and was his usual commanding self, until desperate tug on Yamal at expense of penalty and red card.

Elliot Anderson was sent off after bringing down Lamine Yamal in the penalty box at 3-0

Declan Rice – 7

Best work was in own half for most part but set-piece deliveries were teasing and accurate, including corner for Konsa goal. A strong showing.

Morgan Rogers – 6

Quieter than star-man display on Thursday but his work was diligent on right and included some classy touches.

Jude Bellingham – 8

Drove England forward second-half and was key to energy and adventure. Won corner for second and assisted third.

Anthony Gordon – 7

More energy and purpose than Croatia, even if killer ball was still missing. An honest shift and played his part.

Harry Kane – 7

Showed cunning and class to win and convert first-half penalty. Sacrificed at 2-3 after another masterclass in centre forward play.

Substitutes

Myles Lewis-Skelly (on for Kane) – 6

Dominic Calvert-Lewin (on for Gordon 83) – 6

Djed Spence (on for Bellingham 83) – 6

Dan Burn (on for White 90) – 6

Manager

Thomas Tuchel – 8

At 1-0 up against a top nation (remember Argentina) he kept his side on the front foot and was rewarded, until they went down to 10 men. A big night for the head coach.

Thomas Tuchel kept his side on the front foot when ahead against a top nation and was rewarded until the red card

SPAIN (4-3-3)

Unai Simon 5; Pubill 5 (Porro 20, 5), Cubarsi 4 (Huijsen 46, 6), Laporte 5, Cucurella 5; Merino 4 (Lopez 46, 6), Zubimendi 5 (Williams 72, 7), Fabian Ruiz 5 (Pedri 46, 6); Lamine Yamal 7, Oyarzabal 6, Baena 5

Manager

Luis de la Fuente – 5

Referee

C Turpin (France) – 7

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel questions Elliot Anderson red card after 10-man England hold off Spain
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel questions Elliot Anderson red card after 10-man England hold off Spain

Elliot Anderson was sent off for fouling Lamine Yamal and denying a goalscoring opportunity, with Spain scoring from the resulting penalty to set up a nervy finish in Madrid

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel questioned the red card and penalty decision (Image: David Ramos/UEFA via Getty Images)

Thomas Tuchel claimed England’s famous victory was like the “Azteca reloaded” after they beat world champions Spain in their own backyard.

‌



‌



England produced a heroic win despite having Elliot Anderson sent off and they were made to hang on for dear life as Spain came back from 3-0 down to push for a late equaliser.

‌



It was shades of England’s win in Mexico’s Azteca Stadium when they also went down to 10 men and were left hanging on for victory to end Spain’s 43-game unbeaten run and top their Nations League group.

‌



England boss Tuchel said: “We got it [the statement win]. We got it deserved. That's even more important. We were focused on our performance and our attitude, that's what we did. Cannot praise the team high enough.

Sports.title: England banish Argentina demons with gritty win over Spain after Elliot Anderson self destructs
Sports.content:
England banish Argentina demons with gritty win over Spain after Elliot Anderson self destructs

SPAIN 2-3 ENGLAND: Elliot Anderson's red card made it harder for The Three Lions, but their backs-to-the-wall defending saw them over the line in Madrid

View 4 Images England defended for their lives to get over the line (Image: Thomas COEX / AFP via Getty Images)

This should have gone down as one of England’s greatest nights.

‌



Instead, it became torture as well as being unforgettable as England’s heroic 10 men overhauled the world champions with a sensational performance.

Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White put them 3-0 up and in sight of one of their best and most convincing victories on foreign soil. Then Elliot Anderson pressed the self-destruct button by getting himself sent off after some reckless defending by Jarell Quansah and England made us all suffer once more.

Blimey, can’t they ever make life easy? Mikel Oyarzabal scored the penalty, Nico Williams got a second and suddenly England were manning the barricades as if they were back at the World Cup on that famous night in Mexico.

But, unlike that woeful semi-final surrender to Argentina, this time Thomas Tuchel’s braves somehow held out for a famous, gritty and heroic victory.

England keeper James Trafford made a string of heroic saves as England saw it out to see off Spain and top their Nations League Group with a famous win in the Metropolitano Stadium.

Just to remind England of the task in front of them, Spain paraded the World Cup in front of the Metropolitano Stadium before kick-off.

The reigning world and European champions went into this game on the back of a 43 game unbeaten run and you could understand why Thomas Tuchel described it as “the biggest test in world football.”

Tuchel’s men just took the game to Spain from the start with a high defensive line, a high press which showed no respect to the world champions. They put them to the sword.

View 4 Images Harry Kane put England 1-0 up from the penalty spot (Image: Chris Brunskill/Getty Images)

England were fast out of the blocks, Spain looked slightly bewildered and were caught on the back foot. Tuchel’s men were on a mission. This night will live long in the memory.

Within the first two minutes, Jude Bellingham was denied by an incredible save from Spain keeper Simon. Declan Rice sent over a corner, the ball carried to Bellingham whose shot looked destined for the net until Simon’s sensational reflex stop.

It was all England from then on. It was surely one of the best first halves of football England have produced - and showed just what they are capable of. Lewis Hall typified England’s dominance by owning the left flank as he put Lamine Yamal in his back pocket.

View 4 Images Lewis Hall shone at left-back (Image: Michael Regan/The FA via Getty Images)

Rice was booked for a foul on Yamal and the Barcelona teenager turned to the crowd to try and whip up the home support because they had been left painfully quiet.

And suddenly the 3,515 travelling fans were making all the noise. Elliot Anderson won the ball, Marc Cucurella screamed foul but Kane led a charge, cleverly waited for the challenge and was brought down by Pau Cubarsi.

It was a clear penalty. But there was huge pressure on Kane’s shoulders and deafening whistles but none of that stopped England’s Captain Marvel dispatching the spot kick into the far corner in the 44th minute.

Spain are not used to losing - and took it badly. Cucurella was still protesting and it took giant Dan Burn to intervene and stop a bust-up with Ben White and Spanish players as they headed down the tunnel at half time.

England’s major problem at the World Cup was not seeing the job through. But clearly all the disappointment from that Argentina collapse did not haunt them as much as inspire them this time.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 4 Images James Trafford made a crucial double save late on (Image: Diego Souto/Getty Images)

Soon it was 2-0. Rice sent over another corner and there was Ezri Konsa racing into the box and headed powerfully into the net. It was an England goal straight from an Arsenal set-piece.

Then, five minutes later, England were 3-0 up. Kane held the ball up, Bellingham threaded the ball through to Ben White and the Arsenal defender fired the ball through the legs of the so-called best keeper in the world.

But then England became their own worst enemies. And the nightmare of the World Cup came back to haunt them. Jarell Quansah was caught in possession, Elliot Anderson pulled back Yamal as he got himself sent off and up stepped Mikel Oyarzabal to convert.

Suddenly England were down to ten men, there were shades of Mexico in the summer and a touch of Argentina as they sunk deeper with a man less.

It soon became torture. Nico Williams set up a grandstand finish as he made it 2-3 against England’s 10 men but they somehow got the job done.

Sports.title: Aryna Sabalenka addresses accusation she fired Russian insult at Ukraine's Elina Svitolina
Sports.content:
Aryna Sabalenka addresses accusation she fired Russian insult at Ukraine's Elina Svitolina

Aryna Sabalenka was accused of hurling a Russian insult at Elina Svitolina during her loss in the WTA Finals whilst the war in Ukraine continues

View 2 Images Aryna Sabalenka has rejected claims she insulted her opponent in Russia

Aryna Sabalenka has denied that she hurled an insult in Russian at Elina Svitolina, her Ukrainian opponent, during her loss in the WTA Finals.

‌



‌



The recently dethroned World No 1 was seen cursing during her loss to Svitolina, who secured a 6-3 3-6 6-1 success. Immediately her words were interpreted by some as a dig at her opponent, whose country remains at war with Russia.

‌



Sabalenka has denied that and maintained that her anger was directed at a section of the crowd who were cheering against her, but concedes she could've handled the situation differently.

‌



She said: “My comment was not directed at Elina. I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment.

"That said, I should have handled my frustration differently, and I apologise to anyone offended. Elina played a great match, and I wish her all the best for the rest of the tournament.”

Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils supported after divorce as 'nasty' comments cause fury READ MORE :

Since Russia's invasion into Ukrainian their players do not shake hands with Russian or Belarusian players, nor do they take pre-match photographs with each other. Svitolina has been one of the most outspoken Ukrainian athletes regarding the war and its impact.

‌



Despite that she's still called for Sabalenka to be respected. She said: "As we see there's many, many Ukrainians, many, many flags and of course they want me to win this particular match. We've played many times with Aryna. She has her fans. I have my fans.

"I just hope the matches between us [are] respected. Sometimes in some matches that we've played also there have been not great comments towards me in regards of the war. It is like this in the social media, sometimes the things are turned around a little bit."

‌



View 2 Images Elina Svitolina marched on in the WTA Finals

Svitolina recently announced her divorce from fellow tennis star Gael Monfils after five years. She cited however the Russia-Ukraine war and its emotional impact had caused her to lose herself in her marriage.

Article continues below

"When you've been living through the reality of war for more than 4.5 years, experiencing so many different situations, emotions, and difficult moments, you naturally start seeing life differently. Your perspective changes, your values and priorities shift, and you begin to understand what you truly want out of life," she said.

Svitolina will face Mirra Andreeva, this year's French Open champion, in the showpiece event of the WTA Finals after the Russian teenager hammered Linda Noskova 6-2 6-1 in the semi-finals.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola's stance on replacing Mauricio Pochettino as US boss after next job hint
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola's stance on replacing Mauricio Pochettino as US boss after next job hint

Mauricio Pochettino will leave his role with the United States men's national team next week to join Manchester United - and they want Pep Guardiola to replace him

View 2 Images US Soccer want Pep Guardiola to replace Mauricio Pochettino (Image: Darren Staples/AFP via Getty Images)

Pep Guardiola is expected to 'resist' any approach from US Soccer in their search for a successor to Mauricio Pochettino.

‌



‌



Pochettino was confirmed as the new manager of Manchester United this week despite signing a contract extension with the United States men's national team until 2030 recently. The Argentine will take up his new post following the second game of the US' double-header against Haiti, who they thrashed 6-0 on Saturday.

‌



With Pochettino's departure imminent, talk has swiftly turned to potential successors with Guardiola emerging as an ambitious target for US Soccer.

‌



However, The Telegraph claim that Guardiola will resist any attempts to lure him back into management after leaving Manchester City earlier this year.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



That's because Guardiola remains determined to enjoy a year-long sabbatical following his trophy-laden decade at The Etihad. He has been unattached since walking away from City at the end of the 2025-26 campaign, meaning any potential return to management is not expected until some time in 2027.

It is no secret that Guardiola wishes to experience international management with the 55-year-old confirming back in 2024 that he wanted to lead a team at a major international tournament in the future.

‌



Guardiola has already been approached for such roles since leaving Manchester City with Italy launching a failed bid for his services earlier this year.

He was also sounded out by the Football Association for the England job while at City before Thomas Tuchel was appointed back in 2024.

‌



View 2 Images Guardiola left Manchester City at the end of the 2025/26 season (Image: Getty Images)

Guardiola lived in New York during a previous sabbatical following his time in charge at Barcelona and has reportedly had contact with US Soccer in the past.

‌



Italy's bold bid to lure Guardiola back to the dugout earlier this year failed because of his determination to enjoy time out of the game, underlining the difficulties the US may also face if they do approach the Spaniard.

Italian football federation president Giovanni Malago confirmed as much to La Repubblica, saying: “Pep was honest. He took a sabbatical, partly for family reasons, but if he’d done anything, he would have done it with us.”

Sports.title: I'm A Celeb's Wayne Rooney cut one habit to lose weight in pre-jungle health kick
Sports.content:
I'm A Celeb's Wayne Rooney cut one habit to lose weight in pre-jungle health kick

The footballing star recently admitted this helped his health

View 2 Images Wayne Rooney, set to appear on I'm a Celebrity 2026, admitted to 'drinking a bit too much' (Image: © ITV)

Wayne Rooney has recently been confirmed as a campmate entering the latest I'm A Celebrity series - just two years after his wife, Colleen Rooney, claimed the runner-up spot in 2024. Ahead of his jungle stint, the ex-Manchester United and England player had to address the fact that he has not turned to weight-loss medication to help speed up his recent health kick.

‌



‌



He told ITV's This Morning: "I feel great. I haven't drank, actually, for a while. I just wanted to feel a bit healthier and be healthier. Obviously, my eating habits are a lot better, and I'm training.

‌



"Everyone's saying I'm on this pen thing, which I'm not. I want to get that out there. I'm working hard to try and look better and be healthier."

‌



Rooney admitted that he "got into a bit of a rut" after he quit playing football and ended up "drinking a bit too much". He said: "I just thought, you know what, I want to enjoy my time with my kids while they're at this age - and with Colleen as well."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

The former footballer did not go into detail about his go-to diet and approach to training during the interview. The ex-player retired from football five years ago and has since managed four clubs.

‌



Now working as a pundit for the BBC and Sky Sports. He also appeared in a 10-episode lifestyle docuseries alongside his wife and kids The Real Rooneys,, streaming now on Disney+.

‌



View 2 Images Ditching alcohol can have some immediate and long-term benefits (Image: Getty Images)

What happens when you quit drinking alcohol?

According to the NHS, people who drink alcohol regularly should start to notice the benefits "almost immediately" when quitting. Even occasional drinkers will start to look and feel better about themselves.

‌



The health service claims that short-term benefits can include feeling better in the mornings and having more energy. It adds that skin tends to be "better-looking", and quitting the habit could also make your bank balance look healthier.

By sticking with the plan of binning off booze, people may eventually start to notice major changes. The NHS claims that lowering alcohol intake can lead to:

‌



lower blood pressure

lower risk of stroke, hypertension, cancer and liver disease

lower cholesterol levels

better mood, memory and quality of sleep

help with weight management

The NHS advises that both men and women should not consume more than 14 units of alcohol per week. That's around six medium (175ml) glasses of wine, or six pints of 4% beer.

Article continues below

There's no completely safe level of drinking, but sticking within these guidelines lowers your risk of harming your health. Always remember to drink responsibly (18+) and be Drinkaware.

Sports.title: Man Utd's January offer to Mauricio Pochettino is needed - but also a recipe for disaster
Sports.content:
So Mauricio Pochettino is set to be backed in January as he bids to turn Manchester United's season around and get his tenure off to a positive start.

Is that needed? Undoubtedly. Is it still a recipe for disaster? Absolutely.

United's recruitment post Sir Alex Ferguson has, on the whole, been pretty poor. Their January dealings have been even worse and, were it not for a certain Bruno Fernandes, then their midseason transfer business would be looked upon woefully.

The senior figures at Old Trafford missed out on a number of their targets in the summer, and the team are now feeling the impact of that. A left-back and a No 9 would be most welcome right now, but any success is dependant on quality actually being landed in those positions.

‌



As we know, that is never easy in January. And it will probably prove even harder for a club whose talent identification and scouting has not proved a strength over the past decade or so.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Fernandes is an example of what can go right with a January arrival, inspiring the team in his opening six months and, largely, continuing to do so ever since.

‌



But that capture in January 2020 is an outlier. Every football executive up and down the country will tell you signing players in the New Year is a tough gig. Clubs don't want to sell, so as a result they'll hike any prices. Players that are available are often making the step up from the, so called, lesser clubs. Take a look at Patrick Dorgu from Leece as an example.

In January you'll tend to sign one of four things.

Genuine quality, unlikely. Overpriced stars, Alexis Sanchez. Young stars for the future, Ayden Heaven. Or players jumping up a level or two, which is a decision you take at your risk, Dorgu.

View 3 Images Ineos have made a number of underwhelming moves in the transfer market (Image: Jacob King/Press Association)

‌



It was only last weekend that a former United player remarked that a back four containing Dorgu and Heaven would get the team relegated. They both are January signings.

In fact, since 2013 and the ending of United's dominance, the club have signed seven players permanently in January. Juan Mata, Victor Valdez, Sanchez, Fernandes , Amad, Dorgu and Heaven.

Bar Fernandes none of those could be classed as a 'hit'. That is the challenge that faces Pochettino and the Ineos hierarchy. It must be said, for all Pochettino's managerial quality, signing players hasn't actually been his greatest strength. Enter the likes of Vincent Janssen and Moussa Sissoko.

So here we have a concoction of Pochettino, an Ineos hierarchy who have shown themselves to be among England's worst decision makers and a United team whose transfer market history suggests they overpay for players who underdeliver.

‌



View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes is Man Utd's most successful January signing but others, like Patrick Dorgu, have not totally convinced

Whilst Pochettino may look at this United team and think 'I need players' - of which he is right by the way - there is also a school of thought that says bringing in two or three players who don't cut the mustard and pen two or three years deals will only set the whole project back even further.

The irony, and frustration for those sitting in the Old Trafford stands, is that their rivals have constantly shown that value and quality very much exists in the New Year's market. Virgil van Dijk heading to Liverpool, Luis Diaz's move to Anfield, Newcastle signing Bruno Guimaraes, Arsenal's capture of Martin Odegaard. To name a few.

United's neglect in the summer, which means their defence is now more than two years without a major arrival, leaves the club with little option but to go into the market in around 7 weeks time.

‌



The danger of course, as the latest new era begins, is that the fanbase watch the club and their hugely unpopular owners undertake business that will only set the club back even further.

Sports.title: Cousins emotional after win in Vikings return, reflects on 'tough three years'
Sports.content:
Open Extended Reactions

GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Kirk Cousins managed to hold back tears Sunday morning when he arrived at Lambeau Field. He didn't even try on the way out.

After the Minnesota Vikings' 30-10 victory over the Green Bay Packers, Cousins' first game since the Vikings reacquired him at Tuesday's trade deadline, Cousins let it all out.

"It was emotional coming to the stadium," Cousins told ESPN's Lindsey Thiry, his voice catching several times before he headed into the locker room. "Three years ago, tearing my Achilles here. It's been a tough three years. I was just grateful for the opportunity to play here today, and grateful for my teammates and what they did to make this outcome possible."

Kirk Cousins completed 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns Sunday to lead the Vikings to a victory over the Packers. Patrick McDermott/Getty Images

Cousins' six-season tenure as the Vikings' quarterback effectively ended Oct. 29, 2023, when he tore his right Achilles tendon during a 24-10 victory over the Packers. He signed that offseason with the Atlanta Falcons, only to see the Falcons use the No. 8 pick of the 2024 draft on quarterback Michael Penix Jr. After two years in limbo, Cousins signed last spring with the Las Vegas Raiders, who then selected quarterback Fernando Mendoza with the No. 1 pick.

But the Vikings needed him to do nothing short of rescuing their season when they traded a 2027 third-round pick Tuesday to bring him back. Week 1 starter Kyler Murray is nursing a strained hamstring, and in Week 9, backup Carson Wentz had the worst outing by QBR of any NFL quarterback in a game this season. The Vikings had lost consecutive games after a 6-0 start.

On Sunday, Cousins became the first quarterback since at least 1950, when the NFL began tracking quarterback snaps, to start games for different teams in consecutive weeks. He completed 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns, including a season-high nine completions to receiver Justin Jefferson, and was particularly effective in critical moments of the NFC North matchup.

Cousins completed all eight pass attempts during a fourth-quarter drive that gave the Vikings a three-score lead. On third downs, he completed 9 of 12 passes for 110 yards and seven first-down conversions. Jefferson said afterward that with a defense that is playing as well as the Vikings' -- it sacked Packers quarterback Jordan Love eight times and forced four turnovers -- the Vikings' offense needs only to be "mediocre" to do its part."

"He did what we needed him to do," Jefferson said, "and that was just pitch and catch, just kind of getting it to the open guys and just letting them be the playmakers. It wasn't really too much of big shots down the field, but it was just dumping it off and getting those extra three, four yards after the catch. So it was definitely great for us. And his composure, his confidence in the huddle, all of that, it definitely created a positive vibe in the huddle."

Cousins arrived in Minnesota on Tuesday night, attended his first meeting Wednesday morning and participated in two practices Thursday and Friday. Right tackle Brian O'Neill said the Vikings changed most of their cadences to accommodate Cousins' preferences during the short week, and Cousins said that on a couple of occasions he let coach Kevin O'Connell know what playcalls with which he was most and least comfortable.

"He's always been mature," O'Connell said. "He's always been meticulous in his preparation. He's always done everything in his power to prepare himself for games. But there was a level of poise. It never felt like at any point from the time we talked on the phone [before the trade] all the way through to giving him a game ball today, where it was anything other than just rock solid, consistent."

Said O'Neill: "I can't say enough about what he did all week to prepare. I mean, he has been gone for a couple years, learned a language in Atlanta, learned a language in Vegas, and then in three days switched back to the language we talk about here. And he was running the show and he was in command. It was so awesome to see that. ... [and] a little bit of full circle to have a good feeling again in this locker room, but we got a lot of work to do and we'll keep going."

O'Neill was referencing the morose atmosphere in the visitors locker room after their game at Lambeau in 2023, knowing that Cousins would be lost for the season. The Vikings tiptoed around that coincidence this week, and O'Connell said he knew Cousins well enough to avoid the topic entirely.

"Kirk's not really wired like that," O'Connell said.

But Cousins had clearly thought about it himself.

"There's so much football up ahead," Cousins said, "but certainly it's gratifying to be able to come back here with the purple on. I think to come back here with another team isn't quite the same. To come back here with the purple on, similar time of year, three years later, it's a blessing, to be able to have a win like we had today.

"But there's just so much football ahead, and the story is going to get written much later."

Sports.title: 'Punched in the face,' Raiders' Mendoza vows to learn from first NFL start
Sports.content:
Open Extended Reactions

LAS VEGAS -- The beginning of Fernando Mendoza's first career NFL start seemed like a fairy tale before the Seahawks' defense turned it into a horror show.

On the Raiders' first possession, Mendoza scrambled into the end zone for a 10-yard touchdown run -- a play that resembled one he had during Indiana's win over Miami in the CFP National Championship in January, his final college game.

But the Raiders then went stagnant on offense.

They punted seven straight times. Mike Macdonald-led defenses have made life difficult for rookie quarterbacks in the past, and Mendoza, who was pressured 19 times and sacked six, became another victim in Las Vegas' 21-13 loss to Seattle on Sunday.

"It's good to get punched in the face because now it's a great opportunity to grow and learn and to really unveil all the deficiencies that I have in my game," said Mendoza, who completed 17 of 29 passes (58.6%) for 143 yards and had a passer rating of 71.5.

Mendoza is the fourth straight No. 1 draft pick to be held under 150 passing yards in his first NFL start, joining Cam Ward, Caleb Williams and Bryce Young.

Raiders coach Klint Kubiak called Mendoza's debut start "good." He added that Mendoza was well prepared and began the game strongly as he orchestrated back-to-back scoring drives.

He was effective in play-action while he used his mobility to escape pressure and extend plays. He completed 11 of 13 passes for 90 yards while rushing for 21 yards on five carries in the first half as the Raiders took a 10-7 lead.

"[Mendoza] was poised in critical situations," Raiders left guard Spencer Burford told ESPN.

"That just shows how much maturity he has as a player, especially playing a defense like that for the first time in his first start."

After tight end Brock Bowers was ruled out at the start of the third quarter because of an ankle injury, the Raiders' offense fell apart. Mendoza and Kubiak couldn't keep up in the chess match against Macdonald as Seattle outscored the Raiders 14-3 in the second half, holding them to 27 total yards and keeping them without a third-down conversion.

"We have to play better," Kubiak said. "We've got to support him better. I've got to help him better in the second half. What happened in the second half to go 0-for-7 on third down is unacceptable. No reason that we should do that."

Mendoza was 6-of-16 for 53 yards and was sacked four times in the second half. He had just 15 passing yards until a 38-yard completion to running back Ashton Jeanty with under four minutes to go in the fourth quarter.

"Macdonald dialed it up and did great," Mendoza said. "He fooled me a couple of times."

Fernando Mendoza used his mobility to keep a stout Seahawks defense off-balance in the first half. John Locher/AP Photo

Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon gave Mendoza his "Welcome to the NFL" moment, sacking him twice on three blitzes. Witherspoon sprinted into the pocket untouched on both sacks.

"A lot of sacks today were on me, not any on the offensive line," Mendoza said. "I thought they played great and displayed great leadership today. I need to be better, especially with those DB blitzes."

Despite the loss, Mendoza showed enough to have the Raiders hopeful moving forward. Fullback Connor Heyward said Mendoza is "going to be a hell of a quarterback in this league."

Burford said Mendoza's mobility will add a "whole different dynamic" to the offense because it will be able to incorporate quarterback reads into the game plan. Defensive end Maxx Crosby added that Mendoza will only get better and that the team is excited for the Heisman Trophy winner to be leading the way.

"He's a natural leader," Crosby said. "That's why he went No. 1 overall. Obviously, he's extremely talented and a great player, but as a quarterback, you've got to have those traits [to be] a great leader. And I think he definitely has every bit of those, and he's going to keep growing as a player and as a leader."

Sports.title: Oklahoma, boosted by crowd's ire at postponement, beats Ole Miss
Sports.content:
Open Extended Reactions

Ole Miss officials insisted they couldn't do anything more to prevent the SEC from pushing their game at Oklahoma to Sunday because of the Rebels' travel woes.

After a 24-17 victory over the No. 19 Rebels at Memorial Stadium, the Sooners made sure their parting shots arrived on time.

From blasting the song "Airplanes" by rapper B.o.B, as well as the children's classic "Wheels on the Bus" throughout the stadium, to showing the image of a "no smoking" sign from an airplane on the scoreboard, the Sooners let the Rebels not-so-subtly know that they aren't buying the explanation.

Much of the rain-soaked crowd booed the Rebels as they took the field.

"They were loud, engaged and pissed," said Oklahoma coach Brent Venables, who opened his postgame news conference with "Victory Sunday." "Helped us win the game today."

The Ole Miss-Oklahoma game was pushed back a day after the Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop Friday, which disrupted travel for college football teams around the country. Transportation officials cited "extraordinary circumstances" caused by communications issues at regional air traffic control centers for the stoppage.

Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny opposed the SEC's decision to postpone the game, calling it an "inexplicable" situation that "unfairly burdens" the Sooners.

Ole Miss officials said they did everything they could to try to travel Friday but were informed by their charter broker that JetBlue could not fly the team to Norman, Oklahoma, on Friday night.

The delay didn't seem to bother the Sooners on Sunday. Oklahoma took an early 14-0 lead on quarterback John Mateer's eight-yard touchdown run and receiver Isaiah Sategna III's 75-yard punt return for a score.

The Sooners took a 21-7 lead into the fourth quarter, but the Rebels got as close as 24-17 on Lucas Carneiro's 41-yard field goal in the final minute.

Then the Rebels recovered an onside kick and reached the OU 29. But quarterback Trinidad Chambliss' pass into the end zone was knocked down on the final play.

"It's been weird, for sure, but our guys never blinked," Chambliss said after the game. "We stayed locked in; we stayed focused. We had a lot of walk-throughs, a lot of meetings. We just came mentally prepared for the game because we knew we were going to play a game, whether it was today, yesterday or even next week."

Venables said OU didn't tell its players that the game was being postponed until around 12:30 a.m. ET on Saturday. The Sooners reconvened after breakfast on Saturday, stretched in the weight room and then went to the stadium in rain cleats to prepare for the wet weather. The team had walk-throughs in the indoor facility before Venables released the players for a few hours to visit with their families.

"I'm disappointed that we were forced to not [have] the impact of having everybody here in the stadium," Venables said. "All the logistics that go into that, and just kind of knocked off our routine for the players and certainly for the fans. It's not really fair to them. And then obviously, there's a cause and effect for everything. Now, we've to play Texas A&M on a short week with an early kick."

The SEC announced Sunday that the Sooners' home finale against the Aggies next week will kick off at 3:45 p.m. ET. It was originally scheduled for 12 p.m. ET.

"I'm glad that we were able to get a couple of more hours," Venables said. "That matters in a short week. I'll take every minute we can get."

Ole Miss coach Pete Golding told reporters Sunday that the travel delay was an inconvenience for his team.

"I promise you, nobody was more frustrated than our team," Golding said.

Golding said his players arrived at the Manning Center in Oxford, Mississippi, at 8:45 a.m. ET on Friday and sat on buses for three hours waiting to leave for the airport. Then they were taken off the buses and held in meeting rooms until a final decision to not travel was made.

"There was nobody more frustrated," Golding said. "I can assure they didn't want to wait another day. Everybody wanted to exhaust everything that we could to get here Friday night. They called us and told us we weren't able to do that."

Golding compared the situation to the unusual circumstances of practicing and playing games during the COVID-19 pandemic.

"I told the players this very much felt like COVID-19 to me," Golding said. "We didn't get to decide this, we didn't get to choose this, but it is what it is. So, let's show up tomorrow, and we've got to be ready to go, because I know they will be."

Golding said he was worried about his players sleeping in their homes Friday night, but noted the Rebels showed up with "good energy and good attitude."

Sports.title: Toronto Tempo win 2027 WNBA draft lottery, land No. 1 pick
Sports.content:
Open Extended Reactions

The Toronto Tempo will have the No. 1 pick in the 2027 WNBA draft after winning the draft lottery Sunday night.

After completing its inaugural season in 2026, Toronto becomes the first franchise to have the top pick heading into its second season since the Dream in 2009, when Atlanta selected Angel McCoughtry. The Tempo will make their selection April 12.

Lottery odds are based on teams' two-year cumulative records, except for Portland and Toronto, which were expansion teams in 2026. Their odds were solely based on their records from this past season.

The Houston Comets, formerly the Connecticut Sun (22-66), and Toronto (11-33) had the best odds to land the No. 1 pick, each with 329 chances out of 1,000. This marked the first time since 2015 that two teams had the same odds for the first selection.

The Sun, relocating to Texas from Connecticut this offseason, went 1-2 against Toronto in 2026 -- which is the first tiebreaker -- so the franchise couldn't fall past the third pick. Toronto was guaranteed at least the fourth selection.

"I [felt] like something amazing was going to happen," said Tempo forward Aneesah Morrow, the team's lottery representative. "We're here now ... The future is bright. We have great and amazing players, and we have a country on our back. It feels different when you play like that."

Houston will select second in the draft. All of the other selections are in line with what the odds projected heading into Sunday. Washington, which had the next-best odds after acquiring Chicago's first-round pick in the trade that sent Ariel Atkins to the Sky, will pick third.

Seattle will select at No. 4, followed by Portland at No. 5. The Los Angeles Sparks have the sixth and seventh picks -- one that is their own and the other acquired from Phoenix in the Kelsey Plum trade in August.

USC's JuJu Watkins is projected to go No. 1 in ESPN's latest mock draft released Thursday, with Texas' Madison Booker slotted at No. 2.

Notre Dame's Hannah Hidalgo, Virginia's Kymora Johnson, LSU's Mikaylah Williams, Kansas' S'Mya Nichols and Sarah Cisse of France are projected to round out the lottery picks.

The Tempo had a strong start to their season before veteran Brittney Sykes was sidelined indefinitely because of a plantar fascia injury. After she went down, Toronto went 4-21, including a 12-game losing streak. But Sykes and Marina Mabrey combined to form one of the highest-scoring backcourts in the league.

WNBA Draft Lottery Results 1. Toronto 2. Houston 3. Washington (from Chicago) 4. Seattle 5. Portland 6. Los Angeles 7. Los Angeles (from Phoenix) 8. New York 9. Dallas 10. Indiana 11. Chicago (from Washington) 12. Chicago (from Atlanta) 13. Dallas (from Las Vegas) 14. Golden State 15. Minnesota

Toronto has some young talent in Morrow, whom the team acquired in a midseason trade, and last year's No. 6 pick Kiki Rice, who was the team's third-leading scorer but missed nearly two months because of a Grade 2 left ankle sprain. The combination of Mabrey, Sykes and Rice gives the Tempo perimeter depth. However, they are somewhat thin in the front court.

"[Toronto] is amazing," Morrow said. "Ever since I walked in the locker room, from the beginning, I was able to see the chemistry ... it's all about building the future of the Toronto franchise."

The WNBA schedule will increase from 44 to 50 games in the 2027 season, making it the longest in league history. The added games were part of the new collective bargaining agreement, which also vastly increased pay, secured a $2.2 billion media deal and slated six expansion teams to join the league between 2024 and 2030.

The 2027 WNBA season is expected to start May 7 and has a latest possible end date of Oct. 24, sources told ESPN's Alexa Philippou last week.

"We're excited about the momentum; it's never been stronger," said Bethany Donaphin, senior vice president and head of WNBA league operations. "We think there's a demand, and we're excited to expand to 50 games."

The rest of the first-round draft order is: No. 8 New York, No. 9 Dallas, No. 10 Indiana, No. 11 Chicago, No. 12 Chicago, No. 13 Dallas, No. 14 Golden State and No. 15 Minnesota.

Sports.title: Tiering all 32 teams' chances to make the NFL playoffs, from the locks to the long shots
Sports.content:
Open Extended Reactions

The back half of the 2026 NFL season is upon us, and the playoff race is heating up. Though the standings tell us a lot about teams' chances to reach the postseason, they don't tell us everything. Team strength, injuries, tiebreakers, future strength of schedule and more can shift those odds up or down and don't show up in the win or loss columns.

So, ESPN analytics writer Seth Walder placed all 32 teams into eight tiers of playoff hopes, ranging from clear Super Bowl contenders to those already looking ahead to 2027. There is some fluidity in between, because for as confident as we feel about the league right now, things could look quite different once Week 18 rolls around. The tiers are based on information from ESPN's Football Power Index (FPI), betting lines, metrics, health status and some instinct.

Walder ranked the teams within each tier too. All percentages and statistical rankings are through the Sunday late afternoon window unless otherwise indicated, and playoff chances are from the FPI.

Jump to a team:

ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN

CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND

JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN

NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF

SEA | TB | TEN | WSH

Tier 1: True Super Bowl contenders

Chances to make the playoffs: 99.8%

Chances to win the NFC West: 96.2%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 39.8%

Injuries have hit some of the 49ers' best players -- edge rusher Nick Bosa missed five games and wide receiver Mike Evans hasn't played since Week 6 -- but San Francisco is the FPI's Super Bowl favorite for two main reasons. The Niners are basically a lock to reach the playoffs and a heavy favorite to win the NFC West given their current lead and head-to-head wins over the Rams and the Seahawks. Brock Purdy entered Week 10 as the No. 1 quarterback in QBR, and he is arguably the league's MVP thus far. Kyle Shanahan might be the Coach of the Year thus far too.

See remaining schedule

Chances to make the playoffs: >99.9%

Chances to win the AFC East: 99.7%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 31.0%

The Bills entered this season as the AFC favorite, and nothing that has happened in the first 10 weeks has dispelled that notion. Their hold on the conference looks even stronger now than it did then thanks to their conference-best record and the Ravens falling out of contention. Buffalo's defense (16th in EPA per play) is still a concern, but quarterback Josh Allen, running back James Cook III and the Bills' offensive line do more than enough damage on offense.

See remaining schedule

Chances to make the playoffs: 99.9%

Chances to win the AFC South: 98.8%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 22.9%

The Jaguars were already playoff locks and clearly one of the top two teams in the AFC before the trade deadline, when they acquired safety Jessie Bates III along with defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux. The Davis deal from the Jaguars' perspective is one of the worst trades in years, but there's also little doubt Jacksonville is better today than it was a week ago. And the Jaguars were great a week ago! The Jaguars rank in the top five in EPA per dropback on offense and EPA allowed per dropback as well as EPA allowed per designed rush on defense.

See remaining schedule

play 2:53 Andrew Hawkins: The Jaguars are the 'most complete team in the AFC'

Tier 2: Playoff locks

Chances to make the playoffs: 99.3%

Chances to win the AFC West: 45.8%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 18.2%

The Chiefs faced three major questions entering the season:

The answer to every question has been positive for Kansas City. In particular, Walker has helped transform the Chiefs' rushing attack into a strength. And coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has managed to keep the defense strong too: It ranks sixth in EPA per play.

See remaining schedule

Chances to make the playoffs: 99%

Chances to win the AFC North: 77.4%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 14%

It's something we've wondered about for years: What would happen if the Bengals could manager to combine a peak Joe Burrow season with simply mediocre defense? Well, we're finding out. Burrow is in the MVP race, and Cincinnati's defense is ranked 11th in EPA per play. Wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have been outstanding and provide a sky-high ceiling for the passing offense. Plus, the Bengals have a very easy schedule the rest of the way.

See remaining schedule

Chances to make the playoffs: 99.3%

Chances to win the AFC West: 54.2%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 9.2%

Somehow, it's working. Despite Bo Nix falling well short of expectations -- he entered Week 10 ranked 24th out of 31 qualifiers in QBR -- the Broncos are a virtual lock to reach the playoffs and have a great shot at winning the AFC West. The defense hasn't quite lived up to its reputation (13th in EPA per play), but Denver also hasn't had All-Pro cornerback Pat Surtain II for every game, either. If the offense can keep its recent momentum (the Broncos have put up 26 points in each of their past three games), Denver can be a threat in the postseason. The Broncos have a soft schedule the rest of the way too.

See remaining schedule

Tier 3: Likely in, barring a collapse

Chances to make the playoffs: 95.5%

Chances to win the NFC North: 42.0%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 13.1%

Minnesota's trade-deadline deal for quarterback Kirk Cousins breathed new life into its season. That move instantly increased the Vikings' playoff chances from 65% to 83% at the time of the deal, according to the FPI. But that deal was about what comes next. With Brian Flores' incredible defense leading the way, the Vikings can and should have legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. The moment Flores leaves, a real possibility in this upcoming offseason, the team's contention window vanishes, so the Vikings need to take advantage of this opportunity. Minnesota's 30-10 dismantling of the Packers on Sunday only reinforced what a good trade it was.

See remaining schedule

Chances to make the playoffs: 85.9%

Chances to win the NFC North: 21.7%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 12.1%

Chicago entered its bye week as a near lock to reach the playoffs and very much a team that could go all the way. Quarterback Caleb Williams has taken a significant step forward, and the fact that the Bears are 7-2 despite Williams missing three games is a testament to the coaching staff and how strong this team is. Coordinator Dennis Allen was already getting the most out of a lacking defensive roster when the Bears acquired the best defensive tackle in the league in Jeffery Simmons as they prepare for what they hope is a Super Bowl run.

See remaining schedule

ESPN

Chances to make the playoffs: 89.8%

Chances to win the NFC North: 35.2%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 10.2%

If they played in a normal division, the Lions would be even safer than this, especially after the team's blowout win over the Patriots in Munich on Sunday -- albeit with New England missing quarterback Drake Maye for most of that contest. But Detroit's record has it on the verge of a playoff berth despite playing in a stacked NFC North and with the Seahawks and Rams looming as other wild-card threats. There's little doubt the Lions can score points. But the X factor down the stretch and in the postseason will be their defense, which ranks 23rd in EPA per play and now faces the possibility of a significant knee injury to star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson.

See remaining schedule

Chances to make the playoffs: 87.3%

Chances to win the AFC North: 19.9%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 2.6%

The Steelers are barreling toward another playoff berth thanks to their running game and defense. No team in the league is more efficient (by EPA per play) on the ground than the Steelers -- hello, Jaylen Warren! -- and the team's run defense hasn't allowed opponents to rush successfully against them. Getting past the Bengals to win the division will be a tall order, but the fall of the Ravens helps widen the Steelers' path to the postseason.

See remaining schedule

Tier 4: We're leaning yes

Chances to make the playoffs: 61.1%

Chances to win the NFC South: 60.9%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 5.0%

The FPI believes the Bucs are the best team in the NFC South by a wide margin. That's a low bar to clear, but finishing atop the division is all that matters for Tampa Bay to reach the playoffs -- as it's the only way it will get there. Quarterback Baker Mayfield missed three games (and didn't complete a pass in a bizarre win Nov. 1 over the Falcons in a monsoon), but he has played poorly when on the field. Mayfield entered Week 10 ahead of only Justin Herbert in QBR. And now Mayfield's status is in doubt for Week 11 due to an injury suffered last week. Still, thanks to Todd Bowles' defense -- and a reasonable belief that the passing offense will be better going forward -- the Bucs are the NFC South favorites.

See remaining schedule

Chances to make the playoffs: 48.8%

Chances to win the NFC West: 2.3%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 5.6%

This isn't how the Seahawks envisioned their title defense going. The defense has lived up to its end of the bargain, ranking fourth in EPA per play entering Sunday. But Sam Darnold has not. Darnold ranked 23rd in QBR entering Sunday, registering only 6.8 air yards per attempt (27th highest out of 31 qualifiers) and a 3.8% interception rate (30th). A quad injury knocked Darnold out of the lineup in Weeks 9 and 10, but the Seahawks managed to win both games. With all four teams in the NFC North in the playoff picture along with three NFC West teams (49ers, Seahawks and Rams), there will be a fight for the wild cards. After their win Sunday, the Seahawks are essentially a coin flip to make the playoffs.

See remaining schedule

Tier 5: On the fringe of hope and despair

Chances to make the playoffs: 46.0%

Chances to win the NFC West: 1.5%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 7.6%

If the Rams can reach the playoffs and get wide receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams back, they will absolutely be a Super Bowl contender. But that's a big if at this stage. Los Angeles' offense never looked as prolific as we imagined it would in the offseason -- ranking only eighth in EPA per play -- and it will now have to navigate at least a few more weeks without either of its top two receivers. The good news is that edge rusher Myles Garrett (who missed seven games) and cornerback Trent McDuffie (missed three) are back on the field, though CB Jaylen Watson is lost for the season.

See remaining schedule

play 0:23 Matthew Stafford finds Tyler Higbee for a Rams TD

Chances to make the playoffs: 49.0%

Chances to win the AFC North: 2.6%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: <0.1%

Seemingly against all odds, the Browns are still in the playoff mix. The team's young core has been impressive and playing well, with the 2026 draft class contributing right away and following in the footsteps of the exceptional 2025 crop. Two factors are holding Cleveland back: the offensive line and quarterback Deshaun Watson. Despite the narrative about his improved play, Watson ranked 28th in QBR entering Sunday. Still, after the Browns came back to beat the Texans on Sunday (their sixth come-from-behind win of the campaign), the Browns' playoff chances took a big jump. They have a real shot.

See remaining schedule

Chances to make the playoffs: 44.7%

Chances to win the NFC East: 44.5%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 0.7%

There's a shocking amount of optimism for the Giants during a season in which they lost starting quarterback Jaxson Dart to injury. J.J. McCarthy (acquired via trade) has looked better than expected, rookie linebacker Arvell Reese seems like a big hit and somehow the Giants are in first place in the lowly NFC East. But can McCarthy (who has only a 53.9 QBR this season) really be trusted? We'll find out in the back half of the campaign. And after New York's loss to the Commanders on Thursday, the Giants' playoff position is looking shakier than it was entering Week 10.

See remaining schedule

Chances to make the playoffs: 41.6%

Chances to win the NFC East: 41.4%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 2.5%

The NFC East has been there for the taking, but the Cowboys haven't managed to seize control. The FPI believes Dallas is the best team in the division, but the Cowboys have stumbled throughout the first half of the season, with the defense -- which entered Sunday ranking 30th in EPA per play -- holding the team back, per usual. That was never more evident than in Sunday's 46-40 loss to the 49ers. Washington's win over the Giants on Thursday helped Dallas, because essentially the only way the Cowboys can reach the playoffs is by winning the NFC East.

See remaining schedule

Chances to make the playoffs: 36.5%

Chances to win the AFC East: 0.3%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 0.9%

The Patriots' playoff chances potentially took a big hit at the end of their first drive Sunday, when Drake Maye was knocked out of the game with an ankle injury. The Patriots went on to lose 35-10 to fall to .500. Suddenly, the Patriots, who had a good chance at reaching the playoffs before Sunday, are on the rocks -- and Maye's health will be a huge factor in where their season will ultimately end up. The Patriots' 1-2 start -- and Maye's 51.1 QBR across those first three games -- could loom large and reduces the margin for error even more.

See remaining schedule

Chances to make the playoffs: 33.1%

Chances to win the NFC North: 1.1%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 2.2%

There have been moments when quarterback Jordan Love has looked like an MVP candidate and the Packers seem like one of the best teams in football. But because of their offensive-line-hindered 1-2 start, their 30-10 home loss to Minnesota on Sunday and their placement in a division with four good teams, Green Bay is suddenly on shaky playoff ground. Like many NFC wild-card hopefuls, the Packers would be real contenders -- with Love throwing to wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden -- if they can get into the postseason. But there is work to do to get there.

See remaining schedule

Chances to make the playoffs: 31.6%

Chances to win the NFC South: 31.2%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 0.8%

A hot start from Bryce Young (ranked seventh in QBR through Week 5) had the Panthers at 3-2. But he hasn't kept up that pace, and the defense has been below average. The result? A three-game losing streak that dropped Carolina back into the messy mix that is the NFC South. But it could still win the woebegone division, especially after beating the Saints at the buzzer on Sunday to end that losing skid. So, Carolina is atop the division right now, though the FPI still believes the Buccaneers are the favorites.

See remaining schedule

Tier 6: Stranger things have happened

Chances to make the playoffs: 21.9%

Chances to win the AFC South: 1.1%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 1.0%

An 0-4 start put Houston in a dire situation, but the Texans clawed themselves back into the playoff race with a 3-1 stretch. However, they threw away many of those gains after an upset loss at Cleveland on Sunday that set Houston way back. C.J. Stroud has played well (he was sixth in QBR entering Sunday), but the Texans' defense has been surprisingly mediocre. Such is the variant nature of that side of the ball sometimes -- even when a team has young stars like the Texans do.

See remaining schedule

Chances to make the playoffs: 14.0%

Chances to win the NFC East: 13.9%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 0.3%

The Commanders gave themselves hope with their victory in a back-and-forth game against the Giants on Thursday night. Not only do the Commanders now have three wins (and a tie), they hold the head-to-head tiebreaker over New York. Quarterback Jayden Daniels has played fairly well when active (12th best QBR entering Sunday), so if the Commanders can keep him upright, they have a long shot chance.

See remaining schedule

Chances to make the playoffs: 5.0%

Chances to win the AFC North: <0.1%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: <0.1%

Can the Jacoby Brissett-led Ravens win enough games to keep the team in contention and buy time until Lamar Jackson is able to return from injury? Basically, everything hinges on that and Jackson's return timeline. If the Ravens can somehow reach the playoffs with a healthy Jackson, they would be Super Bowl contenders. But that is a tall, tall order.

See remaining schedule

play 0:29 When will Lamar Jackson return to the field?

Tier 7: Yes, I'm telling you there's a (slight) chance

Chances to make the playoffs: 6.1%

Chances to win the NFC South: 6.0%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: <0.1%

Just like the other NFC South teams, the Saints' season hasn't been great. New Orleans has had its moments -- including the surprising Week 2 win over Lamar Jackson and the Ravens -- but ultimately has seen more downs than ups. Still, the Saints remain in the sub-.500 mix for the division crown, though they're a long shot now after Sunday's home loss to the Panthers.

See remaining schedule

Chances to make the playoffs: 1.8%

Chances to win the NFC South: 1.8%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: <0.1%

Atlanta signaled what it thought of its season at the trade deadline when it dealt away star safety Jessie Bates III and starting center Ryan Neuzil. Unloading Bates made sense given that the Falcons aren't really contenders (they're just lucky enough to play in the NFC South) and were unlikely to get a compensatory pick for him if he left. But it accentuated that the Falcons don't have real expectations about 2026; the FPI agrees, giving Atlanta the lowest odds to win the NFC South.

See remaining schedule

Chances to make the playoffs: 1.4%

Chances to win the AFC West: <0.1%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: <0.1%

The Raiders got out to a hot 3-0 start before dropping four straight. Even though they were 4-5 at the trade deadline, they (rightfully!) decided to deal quarterback Kirk Cousins for a third-round pick, prompting the start of the Fernando Mendoza era in Week 10. No matter who was at quarterback, reaching the playoffs would have been something of a dream for Las Vegas at this point. I'm leaving the door the slightest bit ajar, though, in case Mendoza can take the league by storm from this point forward.

See remaining schedule

Chances to make the playoffs: 1.4%

Chances to win the AFC South: <0.1%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: <0.1%

Even though quarterback Daniel Jones was able to play at the start of the season, the Colts were never able to rediscover the magic they possessed at the outset of the 2025 campaign. Instead, they fired general manager Chris Ballard and kicked off a fire sale, dealing away many of their good players (but not Jonathan Taylor, for some reason). This team has little shot in 2026, and to make it sting even worse, the Jets own Indianapolis' 2027 first-round pick.

See remaining schedule

Tier 8: Just rest up for 2027

Chances to make the playoffs: 0.2%

Fret not, Eagles fans, because if there's one thing Philadelphia does better than any other team in the league, it's taking advantage of the opportunity a losing season provides. Recognizing that they had virtually no shot at the playoffs with quarterback Jalen Hurts out for the season, the Eagles made some amazing pre-deadline trades, somehow getting a second-round pick (plus a Day 3 pick swap!) for center Cam Jurgens and first- and second-round picks for Jordan Davis. So sure, 2026 is effectively over for the Eagles, but they set themselves up so well for 2027 and beyond.

See remaining schedule

Chances to make the playoffs: <0.1%

On the surface, it's been a rough season for the Jets; but in some ways, it's actually been perfect for New York's long-term growth. The Jets' core young players -- edge rusher David Bailey, wide receivers Omar Cooper Jr. and Adonai Mitchell, and tight end Kenyon Sadiq -- have all played well or at least flashed their abilities. But the Jets have still lost games, which helps their draft stock for next year that includes three first-round picks. Sure, this season is over. But give this team a new quarterback and a new head coach, and it can get good, fast. I am uncomfortably bullish on the Jets for 2027 and beyond.

See remaining schedule

Chances to make the playoffs: <0.1%

Any optimism around Arizona after its shocking Week 1 win over the Chargers (which is less shocking given what we know about Los Angeles now) was short-lived. Fast-forward to now and the Cardinals have traded their first bridge quarterback, Jacoby Brissett, while their second bridge quarterback (Gardner Minshew II) is on injured reserve. So, they have turned to rookie Carson Beck -- which is where this season was always destined -- and are looking ahead to 2027.

See remaining schedule

Chances to make the playoffs: <0.1%

This has been a pure, unmitigated disaster. Like so many others, I fell for the Chargers in the offseason. I thought they were legitimate contenders with Mike McDaniel running the offense and offensive tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater back from injury. How wrong I was. I'm still confused over how things got to this point. Justin Herbert entered Sunday ranked last in QBR, and the Chargers' season has been over for weeks.

See remaining schedule

Chances to make the playoffs: <0.1%

After Sunday, the Titans rank 26th in offensive EPA per play and 29th in defensive EPA per play. That's not a recipe for success, and there has been very little of it in Tennessee this season. Cam Ward has played better this season (21st in QBR entering Sunday) than last, but how he plays down the stretch and how the upcoming draft shakes out will determine his role in 2027 and beyond.

See remaining schedule

Chances to make the playoffs: <0.1%

The Dolphins have shown fight; but ultimately, this team's lackluster roster wasn't quite frisky enough to pick off a few games. The Malik Willis experiment at quarterback went OK. I personally had lofty expectations for Willis heading into this season that he did not meet, but it hasn't been awful, either. He ranked 20th in QBR heading into Sunday, but Willis is now on injured reserve with a groin injury. His status beyond this season likely hinges on how Miami approaches the 2027 NFL draft.
