Sports.title: WNBA mock draft: Toronto wins lottery, projected to pick JuJu Watkins
Sports.content:
Open Extended Reactions

In what could be the JuJu Watkins sweepstakes, the Toronto Tempo will have the No. 1 pick in the 2027 WNBA draft. The Tempo won the draft lottery Sunday, with the Houston Comets picking second and the Washington Mystics third.

The Seattle Storm have the No. 4 pick, the Portland Fire got No. 5 and the Los Angeles Sparks have Nos. 6 and 7.

The Tempo, an expansion team in 2026, finished 11-33 last season, missing the playoffs. They were last in the league in defensive rating and won just one game after the All-Star break.

All of that could be much improved in 2027 with a player such as Watkins in Toronto. The national player of the year as a sophomore for the USC Trojans, Watkins missed last season after a knee injury suffered in the 2025 NCAA tournament. She has looked great so far this season and would fit in well with any WNBA team.

This is just Watkins' third college season, but age-wise, she is eligible for the draft. It is unknown if she will go pro or return to USC, but for now we are including her in the mock draft. If she decides Toronto is an unappealing destination or just wants to spend another season in college, she can wait until the 2028 draft.

That said, there is also uncertainty about the seniors who already have completed three seasons. Under the NCAA's new age-based eligibility model -- the five-seasons-in-five-years rule -- they could return for the 2027-28 season. So a lot about the draft pool remains speculative.

But now we know the lottery order.

USC | guard | 6-foot-2 | senior

Watkins and the Trojans are 3-1 after a close loss Sunday to No. 1 South Carolina in which she had 25 points. The March 2025 knee injury that forced Watkins to miss last season has not slowed her. She is averaging 24.5 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 3.3 steals. The Tempo's strength last season was at guard, led by Marina Mabrey. If Watkins doesn't declare for the draft, there should still be good players available for the Tempo. But perhaps not an immediate franchise-changer as Watkins is expected to be.

play 0:14 JuJu Watkins sinks a sweet reverse bucket

Texas | forward | 6-foot-1 | senior

Like several teams, Texas has not been tested yet. But Booker has displayed why she's a lottery pick in the three games she has played so far, including a 30-point, six-assist game against Northern Colorado. Booker's size, strength and confidence on offense and her versatility on defense should translate to the pro game. She took a hard fall in Wednesday's win over South Dakota State and did not play in Sunday's victory against Tarleton State, but she is not expected to miss much more time. The Comets -- the Connecticut Sun relocated as a revived franchise -- last played in the 2008 WNBA season. The Sun were tied for next to last with Toronto at 11-33 this year, and it's fair to say they could use help in all areas, which would make Booker appealing.

Notre Dame | guard | 5-foot-6 | senior

Hidalgo has carried a heavy load throughout her college career, and that continues her senior season. In four victories, she has averaged 28.3 points, 7.5 rebounds, 5.5 assists and 4.8 steals while shooting 59.4% from the field. Hidalgo is a huge threat on offense and defense and could really add to the young core already there if she goes to the Mystics. Washington could use more 3-point shooting. While Hidalgo wasn't great from beyond the arc last season (36 of 142, 25.4%), she shot 40% from 3-point range as a sophomore and is at 40% so far this season.

South Carolina | guard | 6-foot-1 | senior

Johnson's 3-point shooting is an impressive tool that will translate to the pro game. She was the top power-conference player in the country last season in 3-point percentage (44.8%, 90 of 201). So far this season, she is 9-for-18 (50%) from beyond the arc and is averaging 17.0 points. She had 28 points in Sunday's victory over USC. The Storm were last in the WNBA this past season at 8-36 and could benefit from another dynamic young guard to go along with the young post talent they have.

play 1:19 South Carolina takes down USC to improve to 4-0

LSU | guard | 6-foot | senior

The Tigers have cruised through four blowouts, and Williams' averages -- 19.0 points, 5.3 rebounds and 5.5 assists while shooting 58% from the field and 45.5% from beyond the arc -- don't tell us anything we didn't expect. She's a pro-ready player on the offensive end who can look to improve defensively in the WNBA. The expansion Fire had a solid season in 2025, going 17-27, and Williams could fit in offensively.

Virginia | guard | 5-foot-7 | senior

The Cavaliers are 5-0, and we will know more about them once they play their tougher nonconference foes, such as Oklahoma on Nov. 23. But so far, Johnson has looked very good, averaging 18.8 points, 5.2 rebounds, 5.4 assists and 2.2 steals while shooting 59.6% from the field and 61.3% from beyond the arc (13 of 21). With back-to-back picks, Los Angeles can address two of several needs with this draft. The Sparks were 16-28 this season and missed the playoffs for the sixth year in a row.

7. Los Angeles Sparks: Sarah Cissé

France | forward | 6-foot-2

There's so much we don't know now about the Sparks -- including who their coach will be for 2027 -- as they move on after future Hall of Famer Nneka Ogwumike's retirement. But Cissé is another talented player out of France who could make an impact on the WNBA. The MVP of the U20 European Championships this summer, she turns 20 in January. The Sparks were next to last in the WNBA in rebounding this past season, so Cissé might be able to help there.

8. New York Liberty: Ainhoa Risacher

France | forward | 6-foot-1

If you recognize the last name, Risacher is the younger sister of Zaccharie Risacher, the NBA's No. 1 draft pick in 2024. A good-sized wing player, Risacher competed alongside Cissé on France's winning U20 European Championships team this past summer. She will turn 20 in July. The Liberty had an up-and-down 2026 season, getting the No. 8 seed in the playoffs. They knocked off No. 1 Minnesota but then were swept by No. 4 Atlanta. New York fired Chris DeMarco after just one season, so we await their next coach. The Liberty already have a strong French/international presence. The question might be if Risacher impresses them enough defensively compared with other draft options.

South Carolina | forward | 6-foot-2 | senior

Kitts missed last season because of a knee injury but has looked great so far. A starter as a junior, she averaged 10.2 points and 7.7 rebounds in 2024-25. Through four games this season, she has three double-doubles and is averaging 13.0 points and 10.0 rebounds. In Sunday's victory over USC, Kitts had 15 points, 12 rebounds, three assists and four steals. If she continues to play this well, we could see her move up the draft board. Still, with Dallas having young guards such as Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd, Kitts could be a good addition for the Wings, who made the playoffs at 27-17 this season.

play 0:18 Chloe Kitts makes a great pass for a South Carolina bucket

Ole Miss | guard | 6-foot-0 | senior

The Fever are facing two huge offseason questions: Will free agent guard Kelsey Mitchell return, and who will be their general manager? Indiana could use help at the wing position with a player who can defend at a high level but also score. That could be Cooper, who is playing for her third SEC program and averaging 14.0 points while shooting 37% (10 of 27) from 3-point range. She showed progress from beyond the arc last season, and if that continues this season it will help her draft prospects. Cooper had her best defensive season as a sophomore at Tennessee, and a return to that level will boost her.

NC State | forward | 6-foot-2 | senior

Pierre doesn't shoot the 3 much, but she is relentless in the paint. After two strong years at Vanderbilt, she transferred to NC State and led the ACC in rebounding last season (11.9 RPG) while averaging 16.7 points and shooting 52.5% from the field. So far this season for the 4-1 Wolfpack, she is averaging 21.2 points and 8.4 rebounds while shooting 51.3%. The injury-plagued Sky went 16-28 and missed the playoffs for the third year in a row this past season. They were 13th in offensive rating and 10th in rebounding, and Pierre might help in both areas.

Kansas | guard | 6-foot | senior

Nichols is off to a little slower start than expected, averaging 12.5 points and 4.3 assists. (She averaged 17.4 and 4.6 last season.) That's why she has fallen from No. 6 in our two previous mock drafts. But to be fair, it's still early in the season. Nichols had 12 points and six assists in the Jayhawks' loss to Nebraska on Saturday. She and Kansas have another shot at a ranked team this week at Minnesota on Wednesday.

13. Dallas Wings: Kaylene Smikle

Tennessee | guard | 6-foot-0 | senior

Smikle started her career at Rutgers, then went to Maryland and is now at Tennessee. She played just seven games last year with the Terps, missing the rest of the season after knee surgery. So far this season, she is leading the 4-0 Lady Vols with 22.3 points per game, while also averaging 6.0 rebounds. She is also off to a hot start from beyond the arc at 50% (12 of 24). Smikle could add guard/wing depth for Dallas.

Maryland | guard | 5-foot-10 | senior

Okananwa is averaging 14.0 points and 6.3 rebounds, but the Terps have played just three games. She was first-team All-Big Ten and all-defense last season -- we know the WNBA champion Valkyries love defense -- but she probably will need to show improvement as a 3-point shooter to ensure being a first-round pick. So far this season she is 3-for-6 from beyond the arc.

Kentucky | center | 6-foot-5 | senior

Sunday was another big stats day for Strack, who had 29 points and 18 rebounds in a victory over Eastern Michigan. That included going 4-of-5 from beyond the arc, which is important: It's not easy for traditional centers to find their way in the WNBA, so having shooting range matters. Strack has shown that, making 42 3-pointers over the past two seasons. She is 8-of-21 from 3-point range so far this season. Strack, who was the SEC's defensive player of the year in 2025, is averaging 18.4 points, 9.6 rebounds and 3.8 blocks for the 5-0 Wildcats.

Sports.title: Buzz: Week 10's leading scorers through 'Sunday Night Football'
Sports.content:
Open Extended Reactions

Week 10 brought some huge fantasy performances around the NFL. Here's a look at the week's 10 leading scorers through Sunday's early games.

For the full list of leading scorers in Week 10, click here.

Does Emmett Johnson have RB1 upside while Kenneth Walker III sits?

Emmett Johnson takes over as Kansas City's lead back with Kenneth Walker III sidelined on Sunday. Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire

Kenneth Walker III will miss Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons because of a groin injury, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. The Kansas City Chiefs, in the words of a source, "want to give him a week."

Walker injured his groin during Thursday's practice, sat out Friday's session and was initially listed as questionable. It's a tough loss for managers, considering Walker ranks second in the league with 872 rushing yards and is tied for the league lead with 11 touchdowns from scrimmage.

Rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson is expected to take over as the Chiefs' lead back. Coach Andy Reid indicated Friday that Johnson would handle the bulk of the rushing attempts if Walker couldn't play, and Johnson has averaged 4.3 yards per carry and caught 14 of 16 targets for 237 yards and a touchdown this season.

Johnson scored 25.3 fantasy points against Denver in Week 8, catching five passes for 128 yards and a touchdown. He followed that up with 34 rushing yards and a touchdown on six carries against the New York Jets last week. Johnson has primarily been used on passing downs this season, but he should now see considerably more work on early downs. He also has a favorable matchup against a Falcons defense that's allowed the fifth-most fantasy points per game to running backs this season.

Johnson should be rostered in all formats and can be viewed as a low-end RB1 this week. If Johnson is already rostered in your league, there are two other running backs worth looking for in the free agent pool.

Corey Kiner (rostered in 41.7% of ESPN leagues) could lead the New England's backfield with TreVeyon Henderson ruled out and Rhamondre Stevenson expected to miss Sunday's game. Kiner has surpassed 50 rushing yards in three of his past five games despite playing a reserve role. The Detroit Lions have allowed the second-fewest fantasy points per game to running backs, but Kiner could see enough touches to be a viable flex option.

Kaelon Black (35.1%) is also worth considering in deeper leagues against a Dallas Cowboys defense that's allowed the fourth-most fantasy points per game to running backs. Christian McCaffrey remains the clear lead back, but Black has been more involved recently and should be rostered in more leagues given McCaffrey's workload over the past year.

-- Eric Moody

Nov. 13: Should you expect more big games from Likely and Skattebo?

Isaiah Likely scored 27.7 fantasy points on Thursday night, his fourth game this season with at least 20 points and his fifth in which he was targeted at least 10 times. AP Photo/Seth Wenig

The Giants might have lost the game on Thursday night, but we just might have gained a TE1 and a feature running back in the process. Both Isaiah Likely and Cam Skattebo had huge box scores, but here is the question to which fantasy managers would like to know the answer: which of the two performances is more sustainable?

Likely had been one of the standouts at tight end this season, but his production with J.J. McCarthy wasn't as prolific. Even last week, Likely scored a touchdown. But it happened when Jameis Winston was at quarterback. That all changed this week.

Likely was targeted 11 times which he turned into nine receptions for 127 yards and a touchdown -- which is a huge development. Brock Bowers and Trey McBride are clearly the two best tight ends going. But Likely is now just behind them as a must-start moving forward.

What about Skattebo? He was great in this game, rushing for 78 yards and a pair of touchdowns. I'm just not 100% sold on him being an every-down back -- and the Giants weren't either, having kicked the tires on Jonathan Taylor and Bijan Robinson. That would have been a pretty bold strategy. I mean, giving up a couple of draft picks to win the NFC East only to be eliminated in the first round by one of the NFC North teams?

This game felt more like a circumstance of matchup, weather and some good fortune. It's not something that can be sustainable for the rest of the season. The Giants have the Jaguars and 49ers in two of the next three weeks.

Here are a few more notes from Thursday night:

J.J. McCarthy did look pretty good in stretches, but what was he doing in that final drive? The Commanders brought the house and McCarthy heaved a ball that should have been intercepted but he got away with it. Then the Commanders ran the same defense and McCarthy launched another 50-50 ball that was intercepted, sealing the game. Again, two rough matchups in the next three weeks should leave him on the waiver wire.

Chig Okonkwo had eight targets, which was great. But he finished with under 10 points, which was not. I had high hopes for him, but the chemistry with Jayden Daniels just isn't there. You might need him during "Bye-mageddon" (check out my column on that), but his value is very limited.

Rachaad White had 47 yards on 11 carries -- but 18 came on one play. That's 29 yards on the 10 other attempts. I can't believe the Commanders have put so little around Daniels. Stefon Diggs is the only other Commander who needs to be started every week.

-- Adam Rank

Cowboys backup RB returns to action

Israel Abanikanda is set to get his first work in a regular season game since his rookie year in 2023 with the New York Jets (22 carries, 70 yards, seven catches, 43 yards) with Tyler Goodson out with a knee injury.

"I'm just ready to ball," he said. "Ready to ball out with my teammates and get this done."

Brian Schottenheimer has confidence in Abanikanda as the backup to Javonte Williams.

"This is a guy with explosive speed," he said. "When you get this guy into open space, he's a big man that can run really, really fast. And that was evident from our time with him in training camp, preseason and certainly going back to his Pitt film, but he has done a really good job and he's ready to go."

-- Todd Archer, NFL Nation Cowboys reporter

Ravens trot out new kicker

Riley Patterson will be the Ravens' kicker for their Monday night game against the Chargers, special teams coordinator Anthony Levine said. The Ravens signed Patterson to their 53-man roster on Wednesday, but they then added Harrison Mevis to the practice squad. Patterson has made 86.6% of his career field goal attempts, eighth best in NFL history (minimum 100 attempts).

-- Jamison Hensley, NFL Nation Ravens reporter

Nov 12: Still have trade deadline adrenaline? Check out these 12 players in fantasy

Broncos RB Jonah Coleman is a priority fantasy trade target as he has taken over the Broncos backfield. AP Photo/Scott Kinser

The NFL trade deadline is behind us, but fantasy managers have quite some time to make trades in their leagues. Here are some players to target before your deadline:

Jonah Coleman was listed as a trade target when I wrote this up a few weeks ago and is even more so one now. He has firmly taken over the Broncos' backfield, playing 82% of the snaps last week, and has topped 18 fantasy points in his last two. Denver being on bye creates a trading opportunity, as the Broncos have the second-best remaining fantasy RB schedule.

Chase Brown has been a big fantasy disappointment. He has averaged 11 carries per game since Week 3. In fact, the Bengals have scored 26 touchdowns since the start of Week 2, and none have gone to Brown! He has a tough matchup this week and his fantasy manager may be looking to get him out of their lineup. Offer to help by taking Brown off his hands. The Bengals have the fifth-best remaining RB schedule. The Bengals put up so many points that Brown is worth a second-half dice role.

Travis Etienne Jr. has not played since Week 3, meaning fantasy managers with him are either struggling to get by or have found a replacement option. Either way, it creates a trading opportunity. The Saints have the fourth-best remaining fantasy RB schedule and are very much so in the divisional race. Expect Etienne to handle a lot of volume once he is back.

Ollie Gordon II has scored less than eight fantasy points in two straight, making now the time to try and trade for him. He still has averaged 19.5 carries in his last four games and has the best remaining fantasy RB schedule, with a fantastic matchup this week against the Colts.

Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland have become the focal point of the Bears' passing attack since Caleb Williams returned in Week 6. Loveland leads the Bears with a 26% target share in that span, while Burden is second with 25%. Burden has averaged 20.1 fantasy PPG in that span, while Loveland has averaged 14.8 fantasy PPG. Plus, the Bears have the fourth-best receiver and second-best tight end fantasy schedule remaining. You're not getting a discount, but it's still worth it.

Parker Washington has been up and down for fantasy this season, but he is more a victim of circumstances than anything. He leads the Jaguars in target and air yard share, as well as red zone target share. The issue is, the Jags often do not have to throw much. That can still be a problem, but it is worth taking a shot on the talent given the upcoming schedule. The Jags have the best remaining fantasy WR schedule.

Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison have largely disappointed, but help is on the way in the form of both Kirk Cousins and a favorable schedule. The Vikings have the fifth-best remaining fantasy WR schedule. Jefferson averaged 98 receiving yards per game during his time with Cousins, while Addison was a WR3.

Carnell Tate has a 26% target share and 44% air yard share, both of which are team highs. He will always be a bit up and down due to his offense but he has been better as of late, with 9.9 fantasy points or more in four of his past five games. Plus, the Titans have the seventh-best remaining schedule for WRs.

Hunter Henry has been playing well with 11-plus points in four of six games. He has a fantastic matchup this week against the Lions, who have allowed the most yards, TDs and fantasy PPG to tight ends. He has the fourth-best remaining schedule for fantasy tight ends.

Dalton Kincaid has been up and down this season. Still, he is tied to a great QB and offense and has the 10th-best remaining fantasy schedule for TEs.

-- Michael F. Florio

Nov. 11: These are the five most-traded players in fantasy football

Parker Washington of the Jacksonville Jaguars caught this ball for a touchdown. AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough

The NFL's trade deadline is in the rearview, but we fantasy football managers are much more fortunate: Our deadline is still three weeks away, arriving at noon ET on Wednesday, Dec. 2.

As we evaluate prospective deals to improve our own teams, let's take a look at the players that ESPN fantasy managers are most frequently dealing to see what insights might be gleaned. Here are the five players involved in the most trades in ESPN leagues so far this Week 10, including all deals that were accepted or rejected.

1. Justin Jefferson, WR, Minnesota Vikings: By far the most-traded player, 54% more than the next-closest player, Jefferson's elevated trade interest probably has something to do with his new (old?) quarterback, Kirk Cousins. Cousins' familiarity with Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell's offensive scheme should allow him to reacclimate quickly, and bear in mind that Jefferson's most productive season (2022, 21.7 fantasy points per game) came with Cousins under center. Jefferson's favorable remaining schedule also supports a strong finish, and it should come as no surprise that trade offers including him have been met with a rejection nearly three-quarters of the time (even though he's the most-traded overall!). He's a go-get-him trade target.

2. Jonathan Taylor, RB, Indianapolis Colts: By not being traded before Tuesday's deadline, his fantasy stock plummeted to the point he's being frequently shopped. It's an understandable reaction, considering his Colts collapsed offensively over the final seven weeks of last season, during which time they had similar offensive efficiency and EPA metrics to what they've had so far in 2026 (if not slightly better than this year's). In those seven games, Taylor's fantasy production dropped by more than half (27.4 points per game the first 11 weeks, 12.6 the final seven) despite his averaging more rushing attempts and nearly as many touches per game, and he was the No. 18 running back. That seems like a fair barometer for hisrest-of-2026 value, meaning that if you can get better value in trade, make the deal.

3. Parker Washington, WR, Jacksonville Jaguars: Interesting ... are Washington's fantasy managers frustrated by both his inconsistency and the Jaguars' bevy of receivers? Granted, his next three games are ones in which his Jaguars could entirely control the game script, just as their past two, but on the whole they have the No. 1 remaining schedule for wide receivers. And let's not forget how thoroughly dominating this offense was over the second half of 2025, during which time Washington was the No. 12 fantasy wide receiver. I'd firmly want to be on the "trading for" side of any of his deals.

4. Ashton Jeanty, RB, Las Vegas Raiders: His declining usage the past two weeks has surely led to his being heavily shopped. Jeanty went from scoring 17.4 fantasy points per game with a 69% snap rate and 48% rushing share in the season's first seven weeks, to 8.7, 50% and 17% respectively in the past two. Now his Raiders will be breaking in a rookie quarterback -- granted, a plenty talented one in Fernando Mendoza -- but an untested one nonetheless. Considering we're probably at his seasonal valuation low point, Jeanty isn't someone I'd swiftly trade. Mendoza could prove competent or better, the Raiders have a generally favorable remaining running back schedule (13th, albeit with a bye remaining). Also, backup Mike Washington Jr. effectively flopped as Jeanty's stand-in the past two weeks. Any trade return would need to be a better-than-mid-range-RB2 valuation.

5. Chase Brown, RB, Cincinnati Bengals: He has been one of the most disappointing running backs thus far, as Brown's performance has led to the Bengals shifting to an all-out air attack in recent weeks. His yards after contact have plummeted, 1.79 per attempt, after 1.93 in 2024 and 2.12 in 2025, and his average speed at the line of scrimmage has dropped by nearly 2 mph. Any pro-Brown trade advice is a difficult case, but there's this: Brown averaged nearly eight more fantasy points per game in the second half of 2024-25 (20.4) than he did during the first half (12.9). That "second-half player" case makes him a worthwhile trade target, for the right valuation (mid-to-high-range RB2).

The next five: Derrick Henry, George Pickens, Nico Collins, Ollie Gordon II, Chris Olave.

-- Tristan H. Cockcroft

Nov. 10: Malik Willis placed on IR

Malik Willis of the Miami Dolphins will miss at least the next four weeks. Carmen Mandato/Getty Images

The Miami Dolphins placed Willis on the IR Tuesday due to a groin injury, and he will miss a minimum of four games.

Willis has averaged 13.1 fantasy PPG while throwing 1,396 yards, six touchdowns and six interceptions. He has run for 232 yards and three touchdowns. While he disappointed in fantasy last week against the Detroit Lions, he was trending upwards having thrown five of his six touchdown passes in the past four games.

With Willis out, that leaves Kyle McCord as the Dolphins starter. Not only will that be his first career start, McCord has not thrown a pass in the NFL. Willis was a potential streaming option due to the matchup, but that does not apply to McCord.

Additionally, fantasy managers should avoid the Dolphins pass catchers. Malik Washington had been a safe-floor flex option with Willis while Caleb Douglas has flashed his upside at times. Both could be benched -- or even dropped if you have a roster crunch -- until we see that they can produce with McCord. Ollie Gordon II is the only Dolphin that should be started in fantasy football for the time being. Gordon has averaged 13.2 fantasy PPG since Week 3 and the Dolphins have the second-best remaining fantasy RB schedule.

The Indianapolis Colts D/ST has struggled to find any sort of fantasy success this season, but are in play as a streaming option this week due to the matchup.

-- Michael F. Florio

Nov. 10: Cook helps Bills overcome tough Vikings defense

James Cook III got the ball 31 times on Monday night, which was enough volume to have a solid fantasy outing. Nick Wosika/Icon Sportswire

Despite a valiant effort by the Minnesota Vikings' defense, the Buffalo Bills' offense won out on Monday night. James Cook III was the lone standout performance, rushing 31 times for 107 yards and a touchdown. Only Jahmyr Gibbs has run for more yards against the Vikings this season. Cook finished with 16.7 fantasy points, enough to be the RB8 for the week. His 31 carries are the second most in any game in Cook's career.

Josh Allen had his worst fantasy night of the season, finishing with only 12.86 fantasy points. He threw for just 234 yards, with one touchdown and one interception. He also ran the ball six times for 15 yards. That was actually the most fantasy points any QB has scored against the Vikings since Jordan Love in Week 1 (19.48). Allen has a bounce-back opportunity next week against the New York Jets.

Other notes from Monday's game

Buffalo's pass catchers were largely held in check. DJ Moore saw only five targets, catching three for 25 yards. In his four full games this season he has a 26% target share and a 41% air-yard share, averaging 14.3 fantasy PPG.

Dalton Kincaid caught all three of his targets for 28 yards. He has a rebound opportunity next week against the Jets, who have allowed the fourth-most TE yards.

Khalil Shakir led the Bills with four catches for 58 yards. He's a "safe floor" option who can be used in deeper leagues or as an injury/bye week replacement.

Minnesota's offense was a slog all night. Carson Wentz struggled to make competitive throws all night long, finishing just 8-of-25 for 81 yards, no touchdowns and two interceptions. He also lost a fumble. Wentz was replaced by Max Brosmer for the Vikings' final drive, with the team down by three scores.

Justin Jefferson did see 11 targets, but was able to reel in only three of them for 58 yards. He has now finished with single-digit fantasy points in four of his last six games. He's averaging a career-low 56.1 receiving yards per game. It's not his fault, but the team's QB play has dragged him into "boom or bust" WR3 territory! Fantasy managers have to be hoping the Vikings trade for a quarterback.

Given the current state of the Vikings' passing attack, fantasy managers cannot trust either T.J. Hockenson or Jordan Addison . Hockenson finished with 33 yards, while Addison had 28.

Jordan Mason led the Vikings with 48% of the team's snaps, Aaron Jones saw 35%. Mason turned eight opportunities into 42 yards, while Jones had six touches for 21 yards. Neither has reached seven fantasy points in the three games since Mason's return. Both can be benched until we see them produce.

-- Michael F. Florio

Sports.title: Kansas City Current are in the NWSL Championship, just a year later than expected
Sports.content:
Open Extended Reactions

NEW YORK -- Sunday's NWSL semifinal was about revenge for the Kansas City Current, and they exacted it in the kind of cold-blooded efficient way that made them one of the best teams in league history last year.

Forward Haley Hopkins scored in the final minutes at Icahn Stadium to lift the Current to a 2-1 victory over Gotham FC, eliminating the defending champions and current NWSL Shield holders to advance to next Saturday's NWSL Championship against the Washington Spirit. The Current reversed last year's circumstances by knocking out the top-seeded Gotham.

Current defender Izzy Rodriguez told ESPN's Futbol W earlier this week that the rematch was "personal," echoing the words of teammate Michelle Cooper's rally cry throughout the week. Hopkins doubled down after the match, admitting "there was an element of vengeance."

- Pel: Spirit on verge of realizing Michele Kang's dream of dominance

- NWSL players demand more respect amid playoff venue issues

- USWNT, NWSL legend Naeher announces retirement after 16-year career

Rodriguez said that the team's "vendetta" wasn't just against Gotham; it was driven by their failure last year. Kansas City has one more game to win to finish their revenge tour.

Kansas City's appearance in the 2026 NWSL Championship is ironic following their shortcomings in 2025. A year ago, the Current entered the playoffs as the NWSL Shield winners who had amassed the most points in NWSL history. They won the league by 21 points last year, but they fell to the No. 8 seed Gotham in extra time.

The Current struggled to play their style in that quarterfinal a year ago, largely because they were missing star forward and two-time MVP and Golden Boot winner Temwa Chawinga due to injury.

Chawinga was on the field for Sunday's semifinal, and her presence was felt on the front line as Kansas City played their preferred style and struck on counterattacks. Both Kansas City goals were scored on set pieces on Sunday, including a direct free kick in the first half that midfielder Croix Bethune curled around Gotham's wall.

This year, Gotham entered the matchup as the top seed with a star player limited by injury: midfielder Rose Lavelle came off the bench at half-time due to ongoing injuries to her calf and neck. Lavelle provided an immediate spark when she entered the match, but for the second straight game, Gotham failed to produce a shot on goal and only scored on an own goal.

"It's not good enough," Gotham forward Midge Purce said of the team's offensive struggles. Purce's cross in the second half led to Gotham's goal. Purce added that "we lost today because we weren't the better team."

Kansas City now heads to the NWSL Championship a year later than expected and with plenty of momentum.

A year after playoff heartbreak, Kansas City gained an element of revenge. Elsa/NWSL

It didn't start out that way. The Current's 2026 season began on uncertain ground. Chris Armas had taken over as head coach after Vlatko Andonovski shifted into a sporting director role. Kansas City lost three straight games early in the season, underscoring questions around the appointment of Armas, who had not previously coached in the women's professional game.

Ghosts of Kansas City's past haunted the Current during those early-season woes: the Current led the league in set-piece goals conceded this season, a problem that hampered them during their 2024 season. But Kansas City also wasn't healthy. Chawinga and Cooper were both recovering from injuries in the spring.

Andonovski, a Kansas City native and beloved by players and fans, departed the club in August. It was a shocking development that suggested disagreements behind the scenes. Players like Cooper and captain Lo'eau LaBonta publicly expressed their disappointment with Andonovski's departure and the club's terse messaging around it.

STREAM FUTBOL W ON ESPN+ Ali Krieger, Cristina Alexander and Jeff Kassouf debate the biggest storylines and break down the best highlights from women's soccer in the Americas. Stream on ESPN+ (U.S. only)

But on the field, Kansas City began to surge, and that momentum continued in last week's quarterfinal win over Angel City, and again on Sunday against Gotham. Chawinga found her form and Hopkins supported with double-digit goals in a career year. Midfielder Vanessa DiBernardo came into full form and fitness after returning from maternity leave. Bethune remained the magician in midfield, breaking the league record for assists with 11 this season.

"I'm happy that we've played all year and stuck together, and we've become a real team," Armas said after Sunday's win. "And now, we're one of the two teams standing. That's what I'm most happy about and proud of a team that against odds, against -- maybe on the outside, [not what] people predicted, who knows -- against a lot of adversity this year, that they've really, really committed to becoming a real team. This, for a coach, is the greatest reward."

Sunday's performance was personal for Bethune, too, after falling short of an NWSL title the past two years with the Washington Spirit. That theme will continue in Saturday's final as she takes on her old team with a trophy on the line.

Kansas City's ownership group has frequently discussed its desire to be the best team in the world. They must first be the best team in the NWSL and win the league title for the first time. Doing so would give them a potential pathway to FIFA's first Women's Club World Cup.

On Sunday, everything came together how the Current hoped. They held just 35% of the possession but converted big chances to get their revenge on Gotham. They are one step away from finishing the job and winning a championship -- one year later than expected.

Sports.title: Kalajdzic scores late as Republic of Ireland taste defeat in Austria
Sports.content:
Sasa Kalajdzic dealt the Republic of Ireland a late blow in Linz with the only goal in Austria's 1-0 Nations League victory at the Raiffeisen Arena.

The result ensured that, no matter how the closing contests in Group B play out, Austria sealed promotion to League A.

Ireland enter Tuesday's critical home clash at the Aviva Stadium in third place, with one point fewer than their final opponents, Kosovo.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's men were not without chances, but only Kalajdzic made one count when he broke the deadlock in the 79th minute.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson urges UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in a behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; there were allegations of spitting by an Israeli player at half-time, while the Israeli government criticised the Irish players for bowing their heads during the national anthem

Republic of Ireland: Heimir Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future after tense draw

Ireland's head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has called for UEFA to keep his team and Israel separate in future

Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

The Ireland boss was speaking following his side's 1-1 UEFA Nations League draw with Israel behind closed doors in Serbia.

The games between the two nations this international break were overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

This continued in Serbia, as Ireland fitness coach Damien Doyle was allegedly spat on by an Israeli player at half-time, according to reports in the stadium.

Irish media reported that the incident took place as the teams went down the tunnel. Ireland boss Hallgrimsson confirmed there was an allegation, but he admitted he didn't see it and declined to comment further on it.

However, when asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Israeli Government accuses ROI of 'moral blindness'

The Israeli Government have accused the Ireland football team of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during their national anthem.

For the second time in a week, the Irish players, coaching team and FAI all bowed their heads while the Israeli national anthem was played pre-match.

Image: Republic of Ireland players bowed their heads during the national anthem

The official Israeli Government X account posted: "While some use the football field as their political theatre, for us this is personal.

"1939: Irish players raised their arms in salute to Nazi Germany.

"2026: Irish players bowed their heads during Israel's anthem.

"Different generations. The same moral blindness.

"Today, Israel's players wear black armbands to remember those brutally massacred by Hamas on October 7 - including former professional footballer Lior Asulin.

"Some of us have skin in the game. Others just make a show of it."

Sky Sports News has contacted the FAI for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged that a derogatory term had been used, which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. The term is not associated with antisemitic or anti-Israeli abuse.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying: "That's completely untrue," before bringing the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called following an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist, who said a microphone had been taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands that no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland draw with Israel in second Nations League meeting
Sports.content:
Match report and reaction as Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out after the break; sides clashed at half-time

Republic of Ireland 1-1 Israel: Troy Parrott scores again as sides draw second controversial Nations League meeting

The Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in the second controversial Nations League fixture between the sides.

Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out by Dor Peretz after the break in the behind-closed-doors game in Serbia.

The Republic's 'home' fixture was held on neutral territory at the 4,500-seat TSC arena in Backa Topola, due to "operational challenges that could impact on the delivery of the game on home soil" according to a June Football Association of Ireland (FAI) statement.

Both sides wore black armbands. The Republic's, the same as in Hungary to acknowledge - as the Football Association of Ireland chief David Courrell explained before that contest - "all lives lost" in the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict.

Israel's armbands - which read "7.10" - were to commemorate the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack on southern Israel, their official X account confirmed.

The pitch featured no sponsored content or branding, just UEFA graphics with slogans like "football for all", a decision taken by the FAI.

Image: The referee pleads with the benches in Serbia

Tensions rose at half-time after a fracas broke out in front of the tunnel and players from both sides engaged in a heated argument, with the Israeli Government later accusing Irish players of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during Israel's national anthem, as they did in Monday's first match.

Officials broke up a second altercation in three minutes of added time, and there were more heated words exchanged after the final whistle.

On the pitch Parrott, who has now scored 10 times in his last seven competitive internationals, fired the Republic in front from the spot in the 39th minute before Dor Peretz drew the sides level two minutes after the restart.

The result puts Ireland third in Nations League Group B3, level on points with second-placed Kosovo.

Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future

Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

Speaking after the 1-1 draw, Hallgrimsson also declined to comment on the half-time fracas between the two sides.

When asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

On the half-time incident, he said in his post-match press conference: "I was there. I'm not going to comment on it. It's something that a disciplinary committee is probably going to look at."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called due to an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist who had the microphone taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there was no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Ireland news conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland vs Israel is being played in Serbia as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott; protests briefly halted Ireland's draw with Austria on Thursday over opposition to Sunday's Israel fixture

Republic of Ireland vs Israel: Heimir Hallgrimsson's press conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media

Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson's pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday's match against Israel in Serbia ended abruptly after a tense exchange with Israeli media.

The media access was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed they were racially abused by Irish players during their match in Hungary last Sunday.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close as one of his colleagues remonstrated with the reporter.

Image: Ireland's players bowed their heads before facing Israel in the reverse fixture last week

Hallgrimsson later labelled the accusation a "verbal attack" during a separate briefing for members of the Irish press.

The exchange in the main press conference took place after Hallgrimsson was also asked a question about a co-pilot who attacked a pilot and tried to hijack a flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week.

The reporter's question was shut down by the FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there are no open UEFA investigations at this stage from the previous meeting between Israel and Ireland last weekend.

The FAI are conducting their own investigation into whether striker Adam Idah was racially abused by Israeli supporters during their 3-0 UEFA Nations League win but have yet to make an official complaint to UEFA.

Image: Protesters interrupted Ireland's draw with Austria by throwing tennis balls onto the pitch with Palestine flags on them

Despite the high-profile nature of the fixture, members of the Irish media later reported that there was no UEFA delegate present at the news conference.

Sky Sports News was told a UEFA match delegate does not have to attend press conferences. The duty is left to the venue media manager, whose job it is to report anything if there is an incident.

Sunday's match is being played in Backa Topola, Serbia, as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott.

Sky Sports News has approached the FAI for comment.

Sports.title: Ireland held by Austria despite Parrott double as protests interrupt game
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott scored twice but the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a "limited tennis ball protest", when - around the 20th minute - tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text '#StopTheGame' were launched onto the pitch.

The match paused a second time when an invader carrying what appeared to be a Palestine flag entered the pitch and was promptly tackled and carried off by security.

The protests came after Ireland's decision not to boycott their game against Israel last week - although goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu did make himself unavailable.

Ireland are due to face Israel again on Sunday.

Image: Tennis balls with Palestine flags were throw onto the pitch

Before the protests, Parrott scored a sensational 12th-minute opener, and then added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved Ireland's undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrimsson made three changes, including the reintroduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

Bazunu was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was a significant security and police presence outside the stadium, where a small group of protesters also gathered before kick-off.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhin Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before Ireland enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors' half.

Image: Parrott is congratulated after scoring his second goal against Austria

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah's glanced-on header from a goal kick.

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts, before nutmegging Philipp Lienhardt and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Image: A protestor was carried off the pitch during the game

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead.

Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a VAR check and blasted it past the Austria 'keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed after a VAR check.

The Brentford goalkeeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch's free-kick as Ralf Rangnick's side fought back for a point.

Ireland captain Dara O'Shea was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.
