Sports.title: The Antonelli you don't know: Inside the Mercedes garage with F1's new world champion
Sports.content:
Mercedes mechanics have learned to watch their backs. Not because of the dangers of a pitstop, but because of Kimi Antonelli. Formula 1's newly crowned world champion has a rather unusual habit. He approaches members of his crew, greets them and, when they least expect it, gives their nipples a pinch - so nobody appears to be safe!

It is just one of the many practical jokes through which the 20-year-old Italian has developed a special relationship with the people who work on his W17. But behind the mischief, seemingly so far removed from the image of a world champion, lies something much more significant.

Success has roots that are not always visible. To understand them, you sometimes have to look beyond what happens on the track. In Antonelli's case, that means listening to the people who share the work, pressure and emotions of a grand prix weekend with him.

Their accounts paint a picture of a young man who has earned something that even a world championship cannot guarantee: the trust and respect of those around him. It is a relationship that developed naturally, rooted in an attitude Antonelli learned long before reaching F1, when he accompanied his father Marco to races with his own team. Growing up around workshops and racing circuits taught him a valuable lesson: before becoming a racing driver, you have to learn how to be part of a team.

"When he comes into the garage, it's quite a show," said Nathan Tupper, who works on the power unit of Antonelli's car. "He grabs everyone, pinches people's nipples, slaps them all over and generally causes chaos. At the end of the day, he's 20 years old. That's just Kimi."

Ash Jones, the second senior mechanic on Antonelli's car, agrees: "There are so many practical jokes that it would be difficult to list them all. He comes over, says hello and then gives you a pinch. That's how he jokes around with us. He likes having a good relationship with everyone, laughing and having fun together."

The jokes do not even stop when the circumstances would seem to demand maximum concentration. Tom Mason, Antonelli's number one mechanic, has seen it countless times: "It always makes me laugh watching him getting ready to get into the car before qualifying. He's still joking around, grabbing the guys, tickling them. Even when the pressure is enormous, he's there having fun. He's incredibly relaxed."

The driver who has displayed such remarkable maturity on the track is the same young man who, the moment he walks into the garage, becomes a 20-year-old eager to have some fun. Birthdays are another occasion for the Mercedes mechanics to be on their guard, as Antonelli has introduced a tradition of celebrating his colleagues by covering their faces in whipped cream.

George Russell, Mercedes, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Hector Vivas / Formula 1 via Getty Images

Callum Wooldridge, who works on the front end of Antonelli's car, explained why the ritual has become so popular within the team. "When you work in Formula 1, you spend so much time away from home that sometimes you end up celebrating your birthday during a grand prix weekend,” he said.

"It's not always easy. Sometimes you really miss being at home. Kimi started this thing with whipped cream in people's faces, and I don't think there are many other garages in the paddock where something like that happens. It's funny. It happened to me on my birthday in September last year."

The practical jokes have helped create an environment in which the relationship between the driver and his crew has become unusually close. "It's one of the best atmospheres I've ever experienced working with a driver," said Jones. “With Kimi, you feel completely comfortable. It's like talking to one of the guys you work with every day. There's no awkwardness, no tension when you speak to him."

Antonelli's race engineer Peter Bonnington actively encourages that sense of familiarity. "Bono encourages us to interact with him, to have a laugh," Mason explained. "Kimi is very approachable and loves joking around with the guys. It's a really good environment to work in."

The early tests, the crashes and the kid in the blue cap

To discover another side of Antonelli, one must go back to 2024, when Mercedes began the testing programme designed to prepare him for his F1 debut. Franck Bougeard was one of the mechanics involved in those sessions and his first encounter with Antonelli came in the spring, during a test in Austria. Kimi was just 17, wearing a blue cap with a rather unruly head of hair sticking out from underneath.

"I remember all that hair coming out of his cap, looking a bit messy," said Bougeard with a smile. "He really looked like a little kid. And there he was, about to drive a Formula 1 car." Bougeard's memories also include Antonelli's early crashes, as the young Italian began exploring the limits of an F1 machine.

"At Abu Dhabi, he crashed and damaged the chassis. Luckily, we'd brought a spare one, which is something we hardly ever do at those tests,” he said. "I don't even know why we'd brought it, but thank goodness we had, because we needed it."

Antonelli crashed on his F1 session debut in Monza, 2024 Photo by: Zak Mauger / Motorsport Images

Then came Monza, and another accident: "At that point I was starting to think, ‘brilliant, every time this kid leaves the garage, we're going to end up changing a chassis!’ He was very quick, but sometimes he pushed too hard. He needed to learn where the limit of the car was, and a few crashes were part of that process. That's exactly why we were there, to give him the opportunity to learn."

After his accident at Monza, Antonelli returned to the garage visibly upset about the extra work he had caused. "He kept apologising," Bougeard recalled. "He was saying how sorry he was for having destroyed the car again. I told him it wasn't a problem and that the important thing was that he was OK. Then I asked him: 'What did your dad say?'"

Kimi's answer has stayed with the mechanic ever since.

"He gave me a telling-off for half an hour,” he said. Bougeard also wanted to know how Antonelli's mother had reacted. Kimi explained that she had been terribly frightened, to the point of tears. So here was a teenager already capable of driving an F1 car, yet still dealing with the sort of family situations familiar to countless young people.

His father telling him off, his mother worrying about him, and Kimi returning to the mechanics to apologise. But Marco Antonelli also features in another memorable episode, as during a test in Abu Dhabi, after learning that his son had crashed into the barriers, he rushed towards the scene of the accident, even crossing the circuit to reach him.

"Marco was on the other side of the track. When Kimi crashed, he immediately set off to get to him,” said Bougeard. "I had to speak to him afterwards. I said: 'Marco, there are professionals here, there are ambulances. The last thing I want is for you to get run over by an ambulance while you're crossing the circuit!'"

Marco admitted he had been wrong. But those early accidents are more than just amusing memories. Tom Mason recalled that when Antonelli joined the Mercedes race team at the beginning of 2025, one of the young driver's biggest concerns was creating too much work for his mechanics.

Antonelli endured many a tough lesson before becoming world champion Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

"Whenever he made a mistake, he felt incredibly bad about it,” said Mason. “He kept apologising for the damage to the car and for all the work he'd caused us. Eventually, I told him he needed to stop worrying about that."

Mason remembered exactly what he wanted the young driver to understand. "I told him: 'You don't need to apologise to us. If something goes wrong, you don't have to worry about the car or the work we have to do. We're happy to do our jobs. As long as you give everything you've got, we'll do exactly the same for you.'"

There had inevitably been some uncertainty before Antonelli arrived, as Mercedes was saying goodbye to Lewis Hamilton after a hugely successful partnership and handing his car to an 18-year-old rookie.

"We didn't really know what to expect," Mason admitted. "We'd worked with Lewis for so many years and knew his habits inside out. With Kimi, everything was going to be new. I wondered how many accidents he might have, how long it would take him to adapt and how much extra work he might create for us."

There were difficult moments, particularly during the 2025 season. But Mason stressed that even at his lowest points, Antonelli never brought tension into the garage. "Spa was particularly difficult for him,” he added. “But we weren't angry. If anything, we felt sorry for him because we could see how much he was suffering. He was so young and had an enormous amount of pressure on his shoulders."

But one quality has particularly impressed Antonelli's number one mechanic: his ability to move on quickly from disappointment. "He can have a terrible weekend, or a practice session where everything goes wrong,” he said. "When he gets out of the car, he's angry. You can clearly see it. But the next time you meet him, he's already completely different. He comes back into the garage full of enthusiasm, ready to start again. He doesn't carry that negativity around with him. It's almost as if he starts again from zero every time."

For Mason, that attitude makes a considerable difference to the way the team operates. "If a driver is constantly in a bad mood, the people working with him eventually end up feeling the same way,” he claimed. "With Kimi, it's the opposite. He's so positive that his enthusiasm rubs off on everyone. For me, having to coordinate the work of the guys, that's an ideal situation."

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Two days to learn everyone's name

There is another detail on which all five mechanics agree: Antonelli knows the people who work on his car personally, and he learned their names remarkably quickly. "That's one of the things that impressed me most," said Ash Jones. "He knows everyone in the garage. Not just their names, but details about their personal lives too. If you tell him something about yourself, he remembers it."

Tom Mason remembered an episode from the days before Antonelli officially joined the race team. "When we found out Kimi was coming, I spoke to Rosa, his press officer,” he said. “I suggested organising something so that we could all get to know him. Rosa told me Kimi was really enthusiastic about the idea, but first he wanted to do something with the guys who'd worked with him during testing."

Antonelli had no intention of forgetting the people who had accompanied him through the previous months. "He was very conscious of that," said Mason. "He wanted to make sure he met up with the people from the testing programme first, the guys who had been with him up to that point. Then he would get to know everyone else."

And when he finally arrived in the race team's garage, the introductions were remarkably quick. "After a couple of days, he already knew everyone's name,” added Mason. "And that's incredible when you think about how much he had to learn at the same time: a new car, how the team operated, all the procedures, working with the engineers. Yet he still found the time to get to know every single person."

It is an attitude that seems to run through the Antonelli family. Nathan Tupper explained that Marco had also developed a spontaneous, affectionate relationship with the mechanics. "You can be working away and suddenly someone comes up and gives you a hug from behind. You turn around and discover it's Marco,” he said. "That's just how he is. They're a very open, affectionate family. They make you feel part of their world."

Callum Wooldridge remembered the young driver he first met at the beginning of 2025: “He was still a little shy and needed time to settle in. As the months went by, he opened up more and more. Today he's not shy at all. He jokes with everyone.

"But really, he's still the same person. He's just learned to feel at home. He's part of the family now. He behaves exactly like the rest of us. And the nice thing is that his attitude doesn't change depending on the results. Whether he's had a good day or a bad one, he's always the same kid."

Antonelli's crash during FP3 in Melbourne Photo by: Mark Thompson / Getty Images

Melbourne: When the mechanics worked a miracle

Yet life in the Mercedes garage is not all jokes and laughter, as Jones recalled what happened in Melbourne at the start of the 2026 season. Antonelli had badly damaged his car during FP3, leaving the mechanics facing a race against time to get it ready for qualifying.

"After qualifying, I went to speak to him," Jones said. "He told me: 'I've no idea how you managed to get my car back on track.' He genuinely couldn't believe it!" So Antonelli's second place on the grid made the day even more special.

"He was incredibly grateful for what we'd done. He just kept thanking us,” he said. "That's something that has really stayed with me." It is an episode that helps explain just how personally the Mercedes mechanics have experienced Antonelli's journey to the world championship.

"When Kimi has a bad day, we feel bad too," said Wooldridge. "Whether the problem is down to him or the car doesn't really matter. We're so close that we all go through the same emotions together. It's like being on a rollercoaster."

For Jones, the turning point in believing Antonelli could genuinely win the world championship came at Monza, where the Italian sensationally fought his way to victory from 19th on the grid. Wooldridge, meanwhile, chose Austin, where Antonelli converted an unexpected pole position into a victory delivered with remarkable maturity.

Nathan Tupper's most vivid memory is the emotion of Antonelli's maiden grand prix win in China - the race after Australia - whereas Bougeard, who first met Antonelli when he was still a teenager taking his first steps in an F1 car, prefers to look at the entire journey.

"It's incredible to think how much he's grown in such a short space of time,” he said. "We knew he had talent, but I never imagined he'd come this far, this quickly."

Marco Antonelli talks with Simone Resta, Deputy Technical Director of Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

A world champion who is still a kid at heart

There is one remark from Bougeard that perhaps sums up Antonelli better than any other. "It's difficult not to like him,” he claimed. "Even if you woke up one morning thinking you really didn't want to put up with Kimi that day, the moment you see him, you change your mind. He's got a great sense of humour and loves teasing people. He gives you the feeling that he's genuinely enjoying what he does."

Antonelli's story is full of contrasts. The kid with the messy hair who turned up for his first F1 tests. The young driver that apologised profusely after destroying a chassis, while his father told him off and his mother worried about him. And the 20-year-old who is now the youngest world champion, but still wanders around the garage playing practical jokes on his mechanics.

Antonelli has grown up. He has learned to handle pressure and earned authority within the team, without losing the spontaneity that characterised him when he first joined the Mercedes programme. His mechanics have watched an extraordinary talent develop. They have rebuilt his cars after accidents, shared his disappointments, celebrated his first victories and experienced the tension of a championship battle that would have seemed impossible only a few months earlier.

Then, on Sunday evening in Mexico City, came the hugs and the tears. It was not simply the joy of a team celebrating a world championship. It was the emotion of people who had watched a young man grow up, got to know him and, somewhere along the way, become genuinely fond of him.

The world title is just the next step on that journey.

Sports.title: Tsolov lands reserve driver role for F1 2027
Sports.content:
Nikola Tsolov has been named as reserve driver for both Red Bull and Racing Bulls for the 2027 Formula 1 season having missed out on a full-time drive.

The 19-year-old Bulgarian had been linked to a step up from F2 to replace Liam Lawson at Racing Bulls in 2027, but after weeks of speculation the Faenza-based squad put rumours to rest by confirming the New Zealander would continue alongside Arvid Lindblad.

Tsolov has impressed in his first full F2 season, claiming six victories which include four feature races and a streak that saw him become the first in series history to claim three on the bounce.

Next year he will take on a reserve and development role that, alongside the potential to act as a substitute in case of emergency - as Yuki Tsunoda did at Racing Bulls when Lawson was called upon to replace the injured Isack Hadjar at Red Bull - Tsolov will undergo an extensive programme that will combine simulator work with on-track experience, gained through FP1 and TPC [Testing of Previous Car] sessions, as well as Pirelli tyre tests.

“Nikola is an exceptionally talented young driver, and we have been hugely impressed by his development and performances over the past few years," said Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies.

"To fight for the championship in F3 and now challenge for the F2 title in his first full season says a great deal about his ability and determination. What has impressed us just as much is his maturity, his approach to racing and his willingness to keep learning and improving.

"We have enormous belief in Nikola’s potential and see him as a driver with a very exciting future in F1.

Nikola Tsolov Photo by: Rudy Carezzevoli / Getty Images

“This appointment reflects our confidence in him and our commitment to his continued development. Our focus in 2027 will be on giving him the experience, tools and support he needs to be ready to race in F1 next.

"For now, Nikola still has an important job to finish in F2. We wish him every success in the final two rounds and will be supporting him all the way as he fights for the championship."

Tsolov sits second in the F2 standings and is seven points behind leader Rafael Camara with two rounds remaining, though the Brazilian could yet miss those if continuing with Haas - who he will race for next year - having stepped up to make his debut at Interlagos following Esteban Ocon's departure.

Read Also: Formula 1 Why Camara should take heart from a tough F1 debut in Brazil

Tsolov added: "I’m incredibly happy and grateful to Red Bull for giving me this opportunity. Since joining the junior team, I’ve received amazing support and have developed so much, both as a driver and as a person. My career has progressed incredibly quickly, and I owe a lot to everyone who has believed in me and helped me get to this point.

"My ambition is clear: I want to become an F1 driver. Having the opportunity to spend next year preparing for that next step is incredibly exciting. I’m confident that with the team’s support and experience, I’ll have the best possible preparation to make sure I’m fully ready to take the next step onto the F1 grid when the time comes.

"I know there is still a lot to learn, but I’m ready to work hard, make the most of every opportunity and give everything I have to the team. For now, my immediate focus is on finishing the F2 season as strongly as possible.”

Sports.title: Russell partners with BRDC to launch karting academy
Sports.content:
Formula 1 star George Russell has launched a karting academy in partnership with Silverstone to make motorsport more accessible and discover the next young superstar.

The eight-time grand prix winner launched his GR63 Karting Academy on Thursday with it open to boys and girls aged eight to nine, based at the kart track in Silverstone.

It features a “four stage path to the top” and will start in December with an open-access format inviting every eligible driver to Silverstone, where 80 will be selected for stage two.

That will see the 80 drivers compete in the “GR63 Shootout” on 31 January to determine the 25 slots for an eight-round championship at Silverstone from March to November in 2027.

The championship is fully-funded for each driver and the top five will go head-to-head in stage four next December, where the winner will receive a fully-funded karting campaign in 2028.

“Karting is where it all started for me,” said Russell, who won titles on a national and international level before progressing into single-seater competition.

“It taught me everything I’ve relied on throughout my career. I know how hard it is for talented young drivers to get that first opportunity, especially when budgets are tight.

George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Michael Potts / LAT images via Getty Images

“With the GR63 Karting Academy, I want to give something back by finding those hidden talents and giving them the support and platform they need to reach their potential.

“I'm really grateful to Silverstone and the British Racing Drivers’ Club for helping make this happen."

The academy is designed for those who “may not have the budget required to progress through the sport” with the costs in motorsport, both at grassroots level and at the top, increasing.

So costs to enter the academy’s opening stage are £25 with that rising to £75 for the “GR63 Shootout”, before everything is fully-funded from stage three onwards.

BRDC president David Coulthard said: “As owners of Silverstone and guardians of British motorsport, the BRDC has always been committed to reinvesting in the sport and nurturing home-grown talent.

“That commitment has played a big part in Britain’s long record of success in motorsport, and it is a great source of pride for the Club and its Members.

“The GR63 Academy captures that ethos perfectly, and we are delighted to work with George to support the next generation of drivers here at Silverstone."

All drivers must be a citizen of a commonwealth country and to book oneself for stage one, an arrive and drive session, click the link for the Silverstone website here.

Sports.title: Lawson to stay in F1 as Racing Bulls announces 2027 driver pairing
Sports.content:
Racing Bulls has confirmed Liam Lawson will stay with the team for the 2027 Formula 1 campaign, partnering Arvid Lindblad for a second, straight season.

They have formed a formidable duo this year having propelled Racing Bulls to fifth in the championship, which is set to be the Anglo-Italian team's best-ever result.

Despite sitting on 89 points, however, compared to 38 for rookie Lindblad, Lawson's future was in doubt thanks to junior driver Nikola Tsolov starring in F2 this year.

The 19-year-old Bulgarian is second in the standings and has been handed private testing opportunities and a rookie FP1 session in Mexico as part of his junior driver duties.

So Racing Bulls was weighing up its need for short-term performance against its explicit goal of training young drivers for parent team Red Bull.

But with Lawson rising to the occasion in recent weeks, performing some of his strongest races under constant pressure, the 24-year-old has effectively been too good for the team to ignore.

Nikola Tsolov Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Sources indicated to Autosport in Brazil last weekend that amid a big push for the company's top leadership to back Tsolov, the pendulum swung back towards Lawson's favour with his performances over the Americas triple-header.

Read Also: Formula 1 How the Racing Bulls pendulum is swinging back towards Lawson

So the Kiwi has now signed a fresh deal for 2027 with team boss Alan Permane saying he had "no doubt" that the squad will field the strongest possible line-up next season.

"We’re delighted to be continuing with Liam and Arvid for 2027," he said. "Both have demonstrated their ability and potential throughout the season, and we’ve seen the progress they’ve made, both individually and as a pairing.

“I have no doubt that this is the best driver line-up for us, bringing a strong combination of experience and ambition.

“Together, we have a solid foundation to build on the progress made this year, continue pushing ourselves forward and take the next step towards achieving our ambitions in 2027."

Next year is set to be Lawson’s third, full season in F1 having made his debut at Zandvoort towards the back end of the 2023 campaign - having another partial season in 2024.

Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Photo by: Rudy Carezzevoli / Getty Images

"I’m very happy to be continuing with Visa Cash App Racing Bulls next year,” he said. “We’ve had a brilliant season together and the team has worked very hard to produce a fast car, which I’ve loved driving.

“It feels great to be part of a historic season for the team as we continue our fight for P5 in the constructors' championship. It's a testament to the hard work of everyone both at track, and back at the factory.

"I’m looking forward to carrying this moment forward with Arvid through to 2027. We’re building something super positive and I’m excited by what we can achieve together.”

Lawson is currently eighth in the drivers’ standings with Lindblad in 11th ahead of the final three rounds: Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

"Looking back on my first season in Formula 1, it's been a truly special year, full of new experiences and learnings since the very first pre-season test," said 19-year-old Lindblad.

"I can't wait to get started next year, building on everything I've learned during my rookie season. It's set to be an exciting year, and I look forward to continuing to drive alongside Liam."

Sports.title: Fans Remind Vergil Ortiz That Zayas Actually Fought Ennis
Sports.content:
Vergil Ortiz Jr. called Xander Zayas arrogant and said he didn’t like him in a recent DAZN Boxing clip. Plenty of fans heard jealousy in those remarks. The fighter Ortiz singled out is four years younger, has already unified two world titles at 154 pounds, and took the Jaron “Boots” Ennis fight that Ortiz’s own team couldn’t close.

“Yeah the dude that stepped in and fought the fight you were suppose to take. Because what!?” wrote @boxing_eric in the replies. Another commenter, @DrBoxingTalk, pointed to the exact same two things missing from Ortiz’s resume: a unified championship and a bout with Ennis.

Beyond the belts, many fans view Zayas as a proactive go-getter who stays healthy, keeps an active schedule, and jumps at major opportunities without dragging his feet. Ortiz, by contrast, has lost long stretches of his prime to recurring illness, fight postponements, and promotional friction. While Ortiz was sidelined or stuck in legal disputes, Zayas kept showing up and moving forward.

Ortiz, 28, holds a spotless record and has good reason to rate his wins over Serhii Bohachuk, Israil Madrimov, and Erickson Lubin. He also had a legitimate interest in fighting Zayas. Golden Boy proposed a 50/50 split for a December 2025 bout in California or Nevada. Zayas considered the offer unfavorable, and the two sides never reached a deal.

The Ennis situation is where Ortiz’s own decisions deserve a closer look. Ortiz tried to make the fight without Golden Boy while disputing his promotional contract. The company secured a court order that blocked him from signing with a third party for the bout. Ennis moved on, and Zayas stepped up to defend both his WBA and WBO belts in Brooklyn.

Zayas was 23 when he took that risk. He won the vacant WBO title against Jorge García Pérez and added the WBA belt by edging Abass Baraou in San Juan. He could have spent years milking those titles against soft opposition before facing Ennis. Instead, he put both straps on the line in his very first fight as a unified champion and was stopped in seven rounds.

Calling Zayas arrogant is easy. The tougher question for Ortiz is how a fighter four years younger collected two belts, stayed active, and landed a date with Ennis while Ortiz is still waiting for his first full world title.

Sports.title: Will Shakur Stevenson Give Up His WBO Belt Over Muratalla Money?
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson faces a major financial crossroads ahead of Monday’s 3 p.m. ET WBO deadline, where the money on the table may not match the risk of fighting Raymond Muratalla. After earning massive purses in his last three outings, Stevenson has made it clear he is strictly chasing top dollar.

Without Saudi funding underwriting the event, traditional promoters must finance a mandatory defense carrying high danger and limited commercial upside. Facing Muratalla (25-0, 17 KOs) simply will not generate the revenue Stevenson could have commanded had he stayed with Zuffa Boxing and finalized a clash with Devin Haney.

Following the WBO’s October 27 order, both camps had 20 days to make a deal. With no agreement or extension announced as of Sunday night, Stevenson’s promotional free agency after leaving Zuffa leaves him exposed to a purse bid where Top Rank, Matchroom’s Eddie Hearn, and other promoters decide what the fight is worth.

The WBO’s auction rules offer little comfort to a fighter used to massive paydays. The sanctioning body sets a $150,000 minimum bid for light welterweight title fights, with a 75/25 split favoring the champion in his home country. Even when winning bids clear that floor, 75 percent of an unsubsidized bid is a steep drop from the Zuffa money Stevenson walked away from. Monday’s cutoff simply ends negotiations before the WBO sets a separate date for offers.

“Now is not the time to mess up the plan,” Hearn told BoxingScene about Stevenson’s next move. Hearn has pitched an undisputed run at 140 pounds featuring Gary Antuanne Russell and Dalton Smith, yet someone still has to fund the mandatory hurdle in front of them. A purse bid forces Hearn and rival promoters to show how much cash they will risk on one fight without locking Stevenson into a multi-fight deal.

That hesitation comes down to the opponent. Muratalla vacated his IBF lightweight belt to move up to 140 after beating Andy Cruz and Robson Conceicao. For Stevenson (25-0, 11 KOs), defending the WBO title he won from Teofimo Lopez in January against a heavy-handed former champion is genuinely dangerous. At the box office, however, Muratalla lacks the star power to drive pay-per-view buys or justify an eight-figure guarantee without outside funding from the Saudis.

It remains unclear whether Stevenson will keep his WBO strap or give it up. Vacating lets him bypass a tough matchup for less money, leaving the WBO to match Muratalla for the vacant belt. If Stevenson keeps the title and refuses the mandatory defense, the WBO can strip him. Either route costs him the championship leverage needed for unifications at 140, forcing him to weigh whether keeping the belt is worth a pay cut after leaving bigger Zuffa money behind.

Sports.title: Harlem Eubank Wants Devin Haney Next, Yet Books Greg Outlaw
Sports.content:
Harlem Eubank is talking about Devin Haney and Teofimo Lopez, which takes some nerve for a 32-year-old welterweight who has lost two of his last three fights and hit the canvas three times in his last outing. Instead of proving he belongs anywhere near that tier, Eubank is retreating to his comfort zone at the Brighton Centre on February 5, 2027, to face WBA No. 13 contender Greg Outlaw live on DAZN.

Calling this a fresh start for a world title run is a tough sell. Eubank lost to Jack Catterall, came home to Brighton to pick up a routine decision over Josh Wagner, and then dropped a 12-round decision to David Papot in July. Going back to the south coast for a fourth time looks less like a championship march and more like hitting the safety button between defeats. Even MF Pro didn’t bill the fight as a title eliminator.

Outlaw’s WBA ranking looks good on a promotional poster until you actually read his record. The 33-year-old from Maryland is riding a seven-fight win streak, yet he has spent a decade fighting almost exclusively on small club shows around Maryland and D.C. The only recognizable name on his 21-fight resume is Jonathan Montrel, whom he beat in 2022, while his two losses came against Andrew Rodgers (4-9-2 at the time) and Juan Meza Angulo. Worse still, Outlaw hasn’t fought since February 2026, meaning he walks into Brighton after a full year on the shelf.

“There’s a lot of guys in the States on the world scene that I am looking to fight. (Devin) Haney, (Teofimo) Lopez. This is the first step next year, and we are really looking to push on,” said Eubank in the fight announcement.

For Eubank (22-2, 9 KOs), beating Outlaw (19-2, 11 KOs) is the bare minimum after getting dropped three times by Papot and fading down the stretch. Haney and Lopez aren’t lining up to fight a guy rebuilding in Brighton against an inactive regional fighter. Eubank has won all three of his previous outings at the Brighton Centre, and anything less than a dominant win here should put the world title talk to rest.

Sports.title: Josh Kelly Is Begging for an Early Knockout Against Jaron Ennis
Sports.content:
Josh Kelly is begging for trouble if he actually wants Jaron “Boots” Ennis to jump on him early in their February 27, 2027, three-belt junior middleweight unification fight in Atlanta. Kelly believes he can catch Ennis coming in the same way Xander Zayas briefly did in the third round.

What he ignores is that Ennis walked straight through Zayas’ best shot and stopped him anyway, and Kelly lacks Zayas’ punching power to keep Boots off him.

“So, if he’s going to commit early like that, it’s good for me,” said Kelly to Fighthype after an interviewer told him Ennis was predicting an early stoppage. Asked what gave Zayas his opening, Kelly put it down to Ennis’ own success. “He was having so much success. He didn’t think about what was coming back. So, he’s going to have to be a little bit smarter with me, I guess.”

That sounds brave, but Kelly barely survived back-to-back grueling fights against Bakhram Murtazaliev and Caoimhín Agyarko that easily could have gone the other way, and neither fighter is in Ennis’ league.

Kelly pointed to his win over Murtazaliev as proof he can make Ennis respect what is coming back, recalling a second round shot that drew a nod before dropping Murtazaliev in the fourth. What Kelly leaves out is that it was a flash knockdown from a shot Murtazaliev never saw. Murtazaliev got right back up, chased Kelly around the ring, and dropped him in the ninth in a fight many felt Murtazaliev won.

Against Agyarko, Kelly suffered heavy nose damage and three facial cuts in a razor-close decision win over a lighter puncher than Ennis. Going back further, the last time Kelly faced a heavy-handed pressure fighter in David Avanesyan in 2021, he fell apart and got stopped in six rounds with his face a bloody mess.

Kelly said unseen shots do the most damage and claimed he can adjust from round to round. Based on how he has looked since Avanesyan, getting on his bike like he did against Murtazaliev will not save him. Ennis cuts off the ring too well, and Kelly will not last six rounds if he fights just to survive.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Refuses to Lose Money Signing Shakur Stevenson as Saudi Cash Dries Up
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn says Matchroom will not lose money to sign Shakur Stevenson, and that warning cuts straight to the financial reality of light welterweight boxing. Without Saudi backing or a massive check from DAZN, Hearn has every reason to ask how his company makes money on Shakur at 140.

“As much as I love Shakur, as much as I think he’s an unbelievable fighter, there’s no point doing a deal where you’re just losing money,” said Hearn to iFL TV after Saturday’s Diego Pacheco vs. Darius Fulghum card in Carson. “I might have done that when we started. We don’t need to do that now.”

Shakur appears spoiled by the inflated paydays he collected over his last three fights, all of which relied on Saudi bankrolling rather than standalone American box office strength. His bouts against Josh Padley in Riyadh, William Zepeda on the Ring III card in Queens, and Teofimo Lopez on The Ring 6 show at Madison Square Garden were all underwritten by Turki Alalshikh’s operation.

Even with a reported $3.78 million live gate at Madison Square Garden against Lopez, ticket sales covered only a fraction of the estimated combined purse pool. Collecting subsidized checks detached from traditional ticket and broadcast revenue has left Stevenson expecting the same massive guarantees in an open market that cannot sustain them. That disconnect already wrecked his brief stint with Dana White’s Zuffa Boxing, which ended last month without a single fight after the huge guarantees he wanted failed to materialize.

If Matchroom has to shoulder the purse guarantees and promotional overhead on its own, putting Stevenson in with Dalton Smith or Gary Antuanne Russell risks landing in the red, especially if Hearn opens with a belt unification.

Hearn floated starting with WBO mandatory challenger Raymond Muratalla or jumping straight into a unification bout. Neither path solves the commercial problem in the United States. Smith draws well in Britain and wants a stadium fight at Hillsborough in Sheffield, yet almost no casual American fans are paying to watch him box Stevenson. Russell is an American champion, though he remains far from a household name, and his flat outings against Andy Hiraoka and Alberto Puello did nothing to build stateside box office demand.

If Hearn brings Shakur on to the Matchroom roster, the fights worth putting together are Ryan Garcia, Devin Haney, Richardson Hitchins, Jaron Ennis, and Gervonta Davis. Davis is the matchup boxing fans have demanded for years. Ryan delivers a built-in audience, while Haney offers a grudge match between two of the best-known American fighters of their era. Hitchins would be a sharp technical test if either fighter is willing to meet at welterweight, and Ennis would present an even bigger physical challenge at 154. Given Shakur’s big deal about needing a 144-lb catchweight to face Haney, he’s not about to agree to fight Boots at 154 for any amount of money.

The problem is that Stevenson is going to expect massive money that would put Matchroom in a position to lose cash every time he steps into the ring. Landing Davis, Garcia, or Haney means paying huge eight-figure guarantees to both sides, pushing the total fighter payroll toward $30 million or more before arena and marketing expenses.

Even a fight with Ennis, who promotes under the Matchroom banner, or Hitchins, who left Matchroom to sign with Zuffa Boxing and moved up to 147, carries heavy financial and promotional hurdles. Ennis brings real East Coast ticket demand and will not take a small cut just to fund Shakur’s purse expectations, while dealing with Zuffa for Hitchins complicates negotiations even further for a bout that lacks massive casual pay-per-view appeal.

Still, if Hearn is worried about recouping his investment on Shakur, his first priority has to be finding opponents who actually sell tickets and subscriptions. Putting a second belt on the poster will not cover the losses on its own.

Sports.title: Zerafa Misreads Yoenli Hernandez Fight Tape Ahead Of WBO Title Clash
Sports.content:
Michael Zerafa is talking like a fighter who thinks home-court advantage in Melbourne will erase the memory of his two-round collapse against Erislandy Lara. He is right about one thing: the WBO title is suddenly within reach. Whether he can survive twelve rounds with Yoenli Hernandez to actually claim it is a completely different matter.

The situation already looks bleak for the 34-year-old Zerafa (35-5, 23 KOs), because he has not beaten any notable opposition in the last seven years since stopping Jeff Horn in August 2019. His four wins since being blown out by Lara in March 2024 have come against lesser opposition in Tommy Browne, Besir Ay, Mikey Dahlman, and Alejandro Ortiz. Now he is going up against a fighter viewed as a future star of the middleweight division, the Cuba-born Hernandez (11-0, 9 KOs).

Still, the Melbourne contender told DAZN Boxing he expects the vacant WBO middleweight title fight to land in Australia after the sanctioning body stripped Denzel Bentley on October 30 and ordered Hernandez and Zerafa into negotiations.

“The world title is there. I’m now the man to fight against [Yoenli] Hernandez. He’s very beatable, very strong, and tough,” Zerafa said, crediting Matchroom’s Eddie Hearn and Frank Smith with pushing to bring the bout to his backyard.

Melbourne is the target, though a date and venue remain unannounced. First, Matchroom has to clear a major hurdle at the negotiating table before the November 23 deadline.

WBO Purse Bid Threat

The WBO gave Hearn’s team and Leon Margules of Warriors Boxing, who represents Hernandez, until November 23 to reach an agreement. If talks stall, the fight goes to a purse bid with a $200,000 minimum.

For Hearn, beating that clock is everything. Warriors Boxing already stepped up once to put money behind Hernandez during the Bentley cycle, and letting this go to an open bid risks shipping Zerafa back overseas. Zerafa only landed this opportunity because No. 2 Vito Mielnicki Jr. declared himself unavailable and No. 3 Tim Tszyu is tied up with a December WBA title shot against Lara. Winning the negotiating battle to keep the fight in Melbourne is the only way Zerafa gets the exact terms he wants.

Where Zerafa Sees Openings And Where He Gets Hurt

Zerafa’s confidence comes straight from watching Francisco Daniel Veron push Hernandez to a majority decision on August 22 in Las Vegas. On paper, that result looks like a blueprint for beating the unbeaten Cuban. In reality, anyone who actually watched the fight saw Veron eat vicious power shots in every round.

Veron threw 809 punches across ten rounds, yet connected on only 105 while most of his work bounced off gloves or missed entirely. Hernandez landed roughly 200 punches out of 649 thrown, tearing into Veron with heavy right hands and punishing body work that distorted his face long before the final bell. That is why two judges scored it wide at 99-91 and 98-92 for Hernandez, making the lone 95-95 card look completely out of touch with the damage inflicted in the ring.

Veron did manage to wobble Hernandez toward the ropes in the fifth round with a sharp check hook, and he exposed brief moments where the Cuban loaded up on single right hands instead of chaining combinations together. The catch is that Veron had to absorb a beating just to create that one opening, and Hernandez immediately tightened his guard, took back control in the sixth, and hurt him again in the eighth.

Zerafa does not have the chin to absorb that kind of punishment while waiting for Hernandez to load up. Against Lara in March 2024, Zerafa was folded in two rounds the moment clean left hands started landing. Even his January 2026 bout against Nikita Tszyu ended in a third-round no contest after Zerafa told the ringside doctor he could not see.

Since that night in Las Vegas against Lara, Zerafa has rattled off those four stoppage wins in Australia, capped by an eighth-round TKO of Ortiz in August. He insists his past failures had nothing to do with his talent.

“It was never my ability. It was always the people I surrounded myself with in the past. It always made me look bad,” Zerafa said, praising the professionalism of Hearn and Smith.

Blaming old handlers for getting knocked out in two rounds by Lara is a tough sell for a 40-fight veteran, especially when nobody outside the ropes can take a punch for him once the bell rings. If Zerafa uses his feet, stays off the ropes, and forces Hernandez to adjust his stance for twelve rounds, he has a path to an upset in front of his home fans. If he gets dragged into eating the vicious shots Veron absorbed, his second world title shot will end just as quickly as his first.

Sports.title: Darius Fulghum Shuts Down Pacheco Rematch, Challenges Terence Crawford to Wrestle
Sports.content:
Darius Fulghum wrecked Eddie Hearn’s super middleweight plans in Carson on Saturday night, handing Diego Pacheco his first professional loss and immediately demanding the spotlight Hearn had been saving for his own fighter.

Fulghum walked out of Dignity Health Sports Park with a 12-round unanimous decision in a WBA final eliminator, then made it clear in his post-fight press conference that he has zero interest in giving Pacheco an immediate do-over.

“I think Diego will bounce back for sure,” Fulghum said when asked about a second fight. “I want to target some of the other big names.”

Canelo, Martínez, and the Rematch Clause Problem

Before Saturday, Pacheco was the name constantly floated for future fights against Canelo Álvarez and WBC interim champion Lester Martínez. Fulghum took that spot by taking away Pacheco’s reach and beating him up on the inside, and he made sure to remind Hearn of his pre-fight predictions.

“You heard what Eddie said in the press conference on how high he was on Diego. Diego is going to be the future in 168,” Fulghum said. “And I wanted to leave a message that, yeah, Eddie, you said that. So now you got to say the same thing about me.”

Hearn told reporters afterward that Pacheco’s contract includes a rematch clause, creating an immediate tug-of-war over what happens next. Matchroom needs Pacheco back in the win column to keep him in the Canelo sweepstakes, while Fulghum wants Golden Boy Promotions to cash in his WBA eliminator status for a shot at the division’s biggest names.

The WBA belt currently belongs to Jaime Munguía, who has 30 days to negotiate a mandatory defense against Bektemir Melikuziev. That timeline could force Fulghum to wait for the winner, leaving Golden Boy with a window to stage a major showcase fight in the meantime. Fulghum already picked the venue, lobbying for a homecoming card in Houston.

“We trying to bring big-time boxing back to Houston,” Fulghum said. “We need it bad. Houston wants it.”

Fulghum’s Wrestling Challenge to Terence Crawford

Fulghum also threw out an unexpected challenge to Terence Crawford during the post-fight media session, though he wasn’t asking the retired champion to put the gloves back on. Asked about the TNT broadcast, Fulghum joked about settling some Texas and Nebraska bragging rights on a wrestling mat.

“I ain’t going to call Bud to come out of retirement, but yeah, Bud, I got to see you in wrestling for sure,” Fulghum said. “First takedown wins.”

Fulghum actually has the credentials to back up the trash talk, and he holds a massive size edge over the retired former champion. While Crawford wrestled growing up in Omaha and uses that leverage in the clinch, he was never a decorated state tournament contender, leaving it to his son, Terence Crawford Jr., to capture a Nebraska Class A state championship earlier this year. Fulghum, meanwhile, qualified for the Texas state tournament as both a junior and senior at Ellison High School in Killeen, according to Killeen ISD records. He entered the 2015 Class 6A tournament with a 39-3 record at 195 pounds after placing third in his region, People Newspapers reported at the time.

Sports.title: Pacheco Exposed: Fulghum Hands Prospect First Loss in Carson
Sports.content:
Darius “DFG” Fulghum handed Diego Pacheco his first professional loss by unanimous decision Saturday at Dignity Health Sports Park in Carson, California. Two judges scored the 12-round main event 115–112, and the third had it 114–113 for Fulghum. On the same Matchroom Boxing card, Anthony Olascuaga retained his WBO flyweight title with a unanimous decision over Yuberjen Martinez.

Darius Fulghum vs. Diego Pacheco

Fulghum (16–1–1, 13 KOs), the WBA’s No. 4 contender from Houston, took the WBC Silver and WBO International super middleweight titles from Pacheco (26–1, 19 KOs) in a bout that also served as a WBA final eliminator.

Fulghum opened a cut under Pacheco’s right eye with a left hand midway through the third. His left hand gave Pacheco trouble throughout the first four rounds. Pacheco did better in the fifth until Fulghum caught him on the chin with a right in the final minute. They traded clean right hands midway through the sixth, by which time Pacheco also had swelling around his left eye.

Referee Ray Corona deducted a point from Fulghum in the ninth for hitting behind the head. Fulghum drew blood from Pacheco’s nose with a right hand late in the round. He outworked Pacheco in the 11th and rocked him with a right to the chin midway through the 12th.

Anthony Olascuaga vs. Yuberjen Martinez

Anthony “La Princesa” Olascuaga (13–1, 9 KOs) retained his WBO flyweight title by unanimous decision over Colombia’s Yuberjen Martinez (7–1, 7 KOs), a two-time Olympian and 2016 silver medalist. The judges scored it 115–112 twice and 114–113.

Martinez landed several punches with Olascuaga against the ropes in the second before the champion hurt him with a counter. Olascuaga caught him with a counter right early in the third, but Martinez rallied over the third and fourth and shook the champion twice with uppercuts in the sixth.

Olascuaga hurt Martinez with a body shot in the seventh and went back downstairs with a combination in the eighth. The two traded in the tenth, when Olascuaga went down after their feet caught. Referee Thomas Taylor ruled it a slip. With the fight still close in the final round, Olascuaga dropped Martinez with a short right to the chin in the closing seconds.

Undercard Results

Charlie Sheehy def. Jose Matias Romero, 10 rounds. Sheehy (14–0, 8 KOs) won the WBA Continental North American lightweight title by decision over Romero (31–5–1, 11 KOs). Sheehy rocked Romero with a right in the second, trapped him on the ropes with a flurry in the eighth, and buckled his knees with a right uppercut late in the ninth. Romero was still returning right hands in the tenth. Gerard White was the referee.

David Adeleye def. Alexander Flores, UD 10. Adeleye (15–2, 13 KOs) won the WBA International heavyweight title by scores of 100–89 on all three cards. He dropped Flores (21–7–1, 13 KOs) with a jab midway through the third. Adeleye controlled the middle rounds and repeatedly used his forearm against Flores at close range. Flores landed a right hand in the final exchange. Ray Corona was the referee.

Zaquin Moses def. Manuel Lerma, TKO 4. The southpaw Moses (9–0, 5 KOs) controlled the first three rounds of the scheduled eight-round super featherweight bout. Lerma’s corner called a halt between rounds, and referee Thomas Taylor stopped it at 0:01 of the fourth. Lerma fell to 5–4–1.

Nishant Dev def. Sona Akale, KO 3. Dev (8–0, 6 KOs) dropped Akale (10–6, 5 KOs) with a right hand in the third round of their scheduled eight-round junior middleweight bout. Referee Robert Hoyle counted Akale out at 2:52.

Federico Pacheco Jr. def. Jack May, KO 5. Pacheco (12–0, 9 KOs) dropped May (11–2, 8 KOs) in the fourth and again in the fifth of their scheduled eight-round heavyweight fight. Referee Thomas Taylor waved it off at 2:59 of the fifth.

Frank Espinoza def. Abisai Torres Diaz, TKO 2. Espinoza (6–0, 6 KOs) dropped Torres Diaz (5–3–2, 1 KO) with a right to the chin in their scheduled six-round middleweight bout. Referee Gerard White stopped it at 0:50 of the second.

David Diamante was the ring announcer.

Ghana News.title: AFCON 2027Q: Kofi Kyereh admits tough period during injury period
Ghana News.content:
Black Stars midfielder Daniel Kofi Kyereh says he had a difficult period during his recovery period from injury.

The 30-year-old had a tough period after returning to club football following his involvement in the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar.

Kofi Kyereh suffered an interior cruciate ligament injury that kept him out of action for almost four years, a time the midfielder admits was never easy.

“Yeah, of course, it was a long time. And I would be lying if I said it was easy or no problems for me coming back,” he said.

“There were ups and downs during my rehab. But at the end of the day, I always saw my goal to come back on the pitch and play and perform well.”

He also revealed he kept an eye on the performances of the national team as he continued to work out his recovery.

“I was following the Black Stars during that time. I had a lot of support, not only from my teammates, but from the whole staff and officials of the GFA,” he added.

“They were always reaching out to me and encouraging me. And of course, all the fans here in Ghana and the Ghanaians all over the world. Yeah, I got a lot of love and wishes that encouraged me to come back stronger, and I am happy to be back. So that, of course, gave me power and strength and motivation to come back. So, yeah, and now I'm here.”

The midfielder will be hoping to get more minutes when the Black Stars face Somalia once again at the Essipong Stadium on Monday, November 16.

Ghana News.title: Gideon Boako accuses Ato Forson of buying cedi stability with $10.6bn forex interventions
Ghana News.content:
Tano North MP Dr Gideon Boako has questioned the sustainability of Ghana’s recent currency appreciation, alleging that the Bank of Ghana spent about $10.6 billion on foreign exchange interventions in 2025 to support the cedi.

In a write-up issued on Monday, November 16, 2026, Dr Boako argued that the economic stability being credited to Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson came with high costs, including losses from the gold programme and unpaid obligations to public sector workers.

He said Bank of Ghana foreign exchange interventions, which averaged about $1 billion in 2023, increased to approximately $10.6 billion in 2025 as the cedi recorded an appreciation of about 41 per cent.

The MP described the intervention as an artificial means of supporting the currency rather than evidence of sustainable market-driven stability.

“He bought the cedi. BoG forex intervention was averaging $1 billion in 2023. This moved to about $10.6 billion in 2025 to support a 41% appreciation. That is not a market. That is a purchase,” he wrote.

Dr Boako further cited the IMF’s 2026 Article IV assessment, which he said reported losses of more than $1.7 billion, equivalent to 1.5 per cent of GDP, from the gold programme in 2025. He also referred to the Bank of Ghana’s negative equity position, which he put at 6.7 per cent of GDP.

Beyond the currency and gold transactions, the MP criticised the government’s fiscal management, arguing that its efforts to maintain a primary surplus had been accompanied by delays in paying public sector workers and scaling back development projects.

He cited 52,541 promoted teachers who, according to him, were yet to receive their associated payments, as well as concerns over newly recruited teachers who allegedly worked for 17 months without salaries.

Dr Boako also referred to IMF figures indicating that about 1,800 public projects had been cancelled, while approximately 2,000 others had been rephased or rescoped.

He argued that the government could not claim fiscal discipline while accumulating obligations to workers and contractors.

“A primary surplus built on unpaid salaries is not a surplus. It is arrears by another name,” he stated.

The Tano North MP also questioned the funding arrangements for the government's proposed $10 billion New Economy programme, arguing that the administration had yet to demonstrate how it would finance its ambitious plans while dealing with existing fiscal pressures.

He maintained that the current administration’s economic record should be judged not only by improvements in headline indicators but also by the cost of achieving them and the obligations left unsettled.

Ghana News.title: Bole-Bamboi MP congratulates new NDC Savannah executives, calls for unity ahead of 2028
Ghana News.content:
The Member of Parliament for Bole-Bamboi, Yusif Sulemana, has congratulated newly elected executives of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Savannah Region, urging party members to unite behind the new leadership ahead of the 2028 general elections.

In a statement issued through his spokesperson, Tahiru Iddisah Omega, the MP congratulated the executives following the party’s regional delegates conference held in Damongo on Sunday, November 15, 2026.

He described their election as an endorsement of their years of service to the party but urged them to celebrate modestly and recognise the importance of internal democracy.

The MP also encouraged unsuccessful aspirants not to regard their defeat as a rejection, but rather as an opportunity to continue contributing to the party. He said their willingness to contest had strengthened the NDC’s internal democratic process.

He called on all contestants and their supporters to put aside campaign differences and rally behind the elected executives, stressing that the party’s collective interest must take precedence over individual ambitions.

“The NDC remains bigger than any one of us,” he said, urging party members to work towards securing all seven parliamentary seats in the Savannah Region in 2028.

The MP further emphasised the need for unity in the region, describing it as the home region of President John Dramani Mahama and a stronghold of the NDC.

“The Savannah Region is the home region of H.E. President John Dramani Mahama. It is the heart of the NDC. We cannot afford division. We cannot afford factionalism. We cannot afford bitterness,” the statement said.

He urged members to close ranks from the branch and constituency levels through to the regional structure, strengthen the party’s grassroots base and work together to advance the government’s Resetting Ghana agenda.

The statement was signed by Tahiru Iddisah Omega, spokesperson for the Bole-Bamboi MP and Deputy Minister for Lands and Natural Resources.

Ghana News.title: Government plans GH¢28.8bn buyback of DDEP bonds due in February 2027
Ghana News.content:
Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson

The government is preparing to buy back up to GH¢28.8 billion worth of bonds issued under the Domestic Debt Exchange Programme (DDEP) and scheduled to mature in February 2027.

Information gathered by JOYBUSINESS indicates that the proposed transaction will involve the repurchase and cancellation of the four-year government bonds issued in February 2023 as part of the debt restructuring exercise.

The voluntary offer is expected to open on November 23 and close on November 25, 2026, with settlement scheduled for November 26. It will be conducted through a Dutch auction, allowing bondholders to decide whether to participate in the buyback.

The offer will be open to all eligible holders of the bonds, with Absa, CalBank, Fidelity Bank, GCB Bank, Standard Chartered Bank, ARB Apex Bank, Société Générale, Stanbic Bank and other financial institutions expected to act as dealers.

The bonds targeted under the programme were issued in February 2023, carried an annual coupon of 8.23 per cent and formed part of the government's domestic debt restructuring. Earlier Finance Ministry documents put the outstanding principal at approximately GH¢29 billion, with about GH¢11.1 billion in interest.

The planned transaction follows the government's announcement in its issuance calendar published on October 22, 2026, that it intended to undertake a buyback of DDEP bonds. The Ministry of Finance said the liability management exercise was linked to the full operationalisation of the sinking fund established to help prepare for the repayment of the restructured debt.

The issuance calendar also projected net domestic financing of GH¢15.38 billion between October and December 2026. However, that figure represents the expected difference between funds raised and repayments over the period, rather than the total value of securities to be issued or a dedicated allocation for the DDEP buyback.

Ghana launched the DDEP in December 2022, exchanging existing domestic bonds for new securities with longer repayment periods and lower interest rates as part of efforts to restructure public debt. The exercise affected several categories of investors, including banks, insurance companies and pension funds.

Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has previously disclosed that GH¢58 billion in DDEP bonds will mature in 2027, with a further GH¢53 billion falling due in 2028. Of the 2027 maturities, approximately GH¢30 billion is due in February.

The proposed voluntary buyback would give participating institutions an opportunity to receive payment ahead of the original maturity date, while allowing the government to manage its upcoming debt repayment obligations.

Ghana News.title: Gideon Boako: Ato Forson inherited debt restructuring gains, gold reserves and rising credit ratings
Ghana News.content:
Member of Parliament (MP) for Tano North, Dr Gideon Boako

Tano North MP Dr Gideon Boako has accused Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson of taking excessive credit for Ghana’s economic recovery, arguing that several of the gains recorded under the current administration were initiated before the NDC returned to power.

In a write-up issued on Monday, November 16, 2026, Dr Boako said the government inherited an economy that had already made significant progress in debt restructuring, credit rating improvements and gold accumulation.

He pointed to the $3 billion IMF Extended Credit Facility secured in May 2023, saying three programme reviews had been completed by the end of 2024 before Dr Forson assumed office.

The MP also cited the Finance Minister’s admission in the 2026 Budget that 93.5 per cent of Ghana’s total public debt had been restructured by December 2024.

According to Dr Boako, the exercise included $20.4 billion in domestic debt, $13.1 billion in Eurobonds and $5.2 billion in bilateral debt. He argued that the debt relief and improved sustainability resulting from the exercise should not be presented solely as achievements of the current administration.

He further traced Ghana’s credit rating improvements to decisions taken before January 2025, citing Fitch’s upgrade of the country’s long-term local currency rating from Restricted Default to CCC in March 2023 and subsequent upgrades by Moody’s and Fitch in October 2024 following the completion of the Eurobond exchange.

“Fitch even predicted in November 2024 that it would ‘move Ghana out of sovereign default by July 2025’ — before Ato had passed a single budget,” he wrote.

Dr Boako also questioned the extent to which the current government could claim credit for Ghana’s gold reserves, noting that the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme began in July 2021 under the NPP administration.

He said Ghana’s gold holdings had reached 30.53 tonnes by December 2024, before increasing to 38.04 tonnes in October 2025 under the current administration.

“Ato met gold in the vault and gold rising in London. NPP in 2017 met no gold and oil at $50,” he stated.

The MP acknowledged that Dr Forson had maintained the IMF programme and improved some economic outcomes, but argued that the current administration benefited from the foundations laid through the previous government's debt restructuring and gold purchase initiatives.

He maintained that the Finance Minister’s performance should be assessed by separating inherited gains from policies and outcomes directly attributable to his tenure.

Ghana News.title: Afenyo-Markin accuses Mahama of sidelining Big Six in new currency design
Ghana News.content:
Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin

Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin has taken aim at the Mahama administration over the exclusion of five members of the Big Six from Ghana’s newly unveiled banknotes, arguing that the decision overlooks their historic role in the country’s independence struggle.

In a Facebook post on Sunday, November 15, he questioned the decision to feature only Ghana’s first President, Kwame Nkrumah, among the six nationalist leaders, particularly as the country prepares to mark its 70th Independence Anniversary.

Mr Afenyo-Markin recalled that the Big Six gained national prominence through their leadership in the United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC) and their subsequent detention following the 1948 disturbances.

He stressed that their contributions predated the formation of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) and the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

He also pointed to the 2007 redenomination of the cedi under former President John Agyekum Kufuor, when the collective portraits of the six leaders featured on Ghana’s banknotes. The introduction of the GH¢2 note bearing Nkrumah’s image under the late President John Evans Atta Mills, he noted, did not result in the removal of the other five from the currency.

The Minority Leader argued that the government could have recognised other prominent Ghanaians on the new notes without excluding historical figures whose contributions to the independence movement were already acknowledged.

He specifically mentioned nationalist J.B. Danquah and Chief Simon Diedong Dombo, saying their contributions to Ghana’s political development and independence deserved recognition. He criticised what he described as the government’s reluctance to acknowledge Danquah’s role in advocating for the adoption of the name Ghana.

“We can celebrate the designer of our flag and the composer of ‘Yɛn Ara Asaase Ni’, but are unwilling to recognise the man who proposed the name Ghana for an independent Gold Coast. It is sad that the Mahama-led NDC government does not want to acknowledge J. B. Danquah, whose research and advocacy helped advance the adoption of the name Ghana,” he said.

He added that Danquah’s campaign had persuaded colleagues within the UGCC and the wider nationalist movement, and that Nkrumah’s government eventually adopted the name despite their political differences. He urged current leaders to demonstrate a similar willingness to recognise contributions across political divides.

“Your government can remove the Big Six from the currency, but can never withdraw them from history,” Mr Afenyo-Markin stated, urging President Mahama to put national history above partisan considerations in decisions involving national symbols.

His comments follow the Bank of Ghana’s unveiling of its new Heritage Series banknotes on Thursday, November 12. The redesigned notes feature Agnes Oforiwa Tagoe-Quarcoopome on the GH¢1, Cardinal Peter Poreku Dery on GH¢2, Dr J.E.K. Aggrey on GH¢5, Justice Annie Jiagge on GH¢10, Dr Ephraim Amu on GH¢20, Theodosia Salome Okoh on GH¢50, Kofi Annan on GH¢100 and Kwame Nkrumah on GH¢200.

The new banknotes are scheduled to enter circulation on December 1, 2026.

Ghana News.title: Advertisers Association rejects political claims over crackdown on illegal billboards
Ghana News.content:
The Advertising Association of Ghana (AAG) has rejected suggestions that the ongoing demolition of unauthorised billboards and advertising structures is politically motivated, saying the exercise is intended to protect the public interest and improve urban spaces.

Chairman of the AAG Outdoor Committee, Mukaila Ahmed Akuamoah, said the association’s collaboration with the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs was focused on ensuring orderly advertising practices and a cleaner environment, rather than targeting individuals based on their political affiliations.

“Once we’re here, it’s not about being political from any other party. It’s about Ghana, it’s about you, it’s about me, it’s about making things happen,” he said.

He made the remarks during a joint billboard inspection and enforcement exercise organised by the Ministry and the AAG in Accra.

Mr Akuamoah said the partnership would help authorities identify and remove advertising structures erected without the required authorisation, noting that some had contributed to environmental problems and obstructed drainage systems.

He also criticised the indiscriminate installation of billboards by some operators, including members and non-members of the association.

“Some of them have mounted boards indiscriminately all over the place, and it doesn’t go down well with us. Some of them are causing drains and headaches all over the place,” he said.

The enforcement exercise follows a directive requiring billboard owners and advertising companies to display their names and company details prominently on their structures to make identification easier and support regulatory action against non-compliant operators.

Ghana News.title: Assemblies to face sanctions over illegal billboards – Deputy Minister
Ghana News.content:
The Deputy Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Rita Naa Odoley Sowah, has warned Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs) that they will be held responsible for unauthorised billboards and advertising structures erected within their jurisdictions.

She said the various assemblies must take ownership of enforcement efforts and ensure that advertisers comply with regulations governing the installation of outdoor advertising structures.

Madam Sowah issued the warning during a joint billboard inspection and enforcement exercise organised by the Ministry, in collaboration with the Advertising Association of Ghana (AAG), in Accra on Sunday, November 15, 2026.

She stressed that no individual or advertising company may erect a billboard or advertising sign without first securing approval from the relevant assembly.

“As the MMDCEs have spoken, we are looking forward to them taking charge of their various jurisdictions from today onwards. As we have started, we want them to take full charge so that, wherever they see any illegal billboards or advertising signs, they will take the necessary action,” she stated.

The Deputy Minister also cautioned landowners against independently granting permission to advertisers to mount structures on their properties, explaining that the relevant assemblies have the authority to issue permits.

The exercise follows a deadline issued to billboard owners and advertising companies to display their names and company details prominently on their structures to facilitate identification and regulatory enforcement.

Inspection teams visited selected roads and areas in Accra with high concentrations of billboards, identified structures that breach applicable standards and regulatory requirements, and removed them through established procedures.

Madam Sowah urged operators with unauthorised structures to dismantle them voluntarily to avoid enforcement action and additional financial penalties.

“If you do not do that, the assemblies are going to surcharge you, and you pay something to them for pulling down your billboards,” she warned.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
