World.title: ‘I was mentally down’ – Benjamin Fredrick opens up about missing 2025 AFCON
World.content:
Super Eagles defender Benjamin Fredrick has revealed the emotional toll of missing the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco, admitting that his injury setback came at the worst possible time in his career.

The Brentford centre-back had been enjoying an impressive rise and was emerging as one of Nigeria’s promising defensive options after making a strong impression during the 2026 FIFA World Cup qualifying campaign under head coach Eric Chelle.

However, his growing momentum was halted in November 2025 when he suffered a knee injury during training with Belgian side FCV Dender. The setback brought his loan spell to an abrupt end and ruled him out of Nigeria’s AFCON campaign.

Speaking to 54Footballx, Fredrick admitted that missing the tournament was particularly painful because he believed he was playing the best football of his career and had been looking forward to making his AFCON debut at a young age.

“To be honest, at that time, I was playing well and was in the best shape of my life to play football. I was happy there before I got injured. When I got injured, I was really down. I was mentally down because I planned to go to the AFCON at such a young age,” he said.

The defender described the opportunity to feature at the continental showpiece as a major ambition for any young footballer, making his untimely injury even more difficult to accept.

“It is like a dream for every young player to reach that stage at such a young age. So, getting injured during that period left me feeling down and sad. But I am happy to be back playing again. I am so happy,” he added.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Having worked his way back to fitness, Fredrick has returned to competitive action and the Super Eagles setup, featuring in Nigeria’s recent fixtures against Russia and Tanzania.

The youngster now has an opportunity to reclaim his place in Chelle’s plans as Nigeria continue their push for qualification for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations.

With the disappointment of missing out on the last AFCON behind him, Fredrick is focused on making the most of his return and helping the Super Eagles finish their qualifying campaign strongly.

“I want to play, and I am happy I am here. I am playing, and I want to assure everyone that we will try to give our best. We will get the victory in every game from the next game to the end of qualifiers,” he said.

World.title: South Africa’s SABC speaks on livestream controversy after Nigeria’s complaint
World.content:
The South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC) has spoken out on the controversy surrounding the livestream of the diplomatic ceremony which allegedly left out Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode.

In a statement on Sunday, the public broadcaster said it covered the ceremony and broadcast it on its LIVE channel on SABC+.

The statement came after a heated exchange between the South African and Nigerian governments, in which the Nigerian High Commission called the South African presidential spokesperson, Vincent Magwenya, a “disgrace” and a “liar.”

The diplomatic spat began after Mr Fani-Kayode protested the omission of his speech from the live stream of the event in which he presented his credentials to Mr Ramaphosa. He accused the South African station of cutting off the live stream when the Nigerian envoy took the stage.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that Mr Fani-Kayode, also accredited to Lesotho and Eswatini, insisted that he was the only one of the 15 Ambassadors given the stage to speak whose live stream was cut off.

But the South African presidential spokesperson responded, saying the SABC live-streamed the event and that the presidential team had no influence on its editorial process.

In its statement, the broadcaster said Mr Fani-Kayode’s arrival was shown during a “live crossing on its SABC News channel on DStv Channel 404.”

It also said it published a clip of the Nigerian envoy speaking with Mr Ramaphosa on its official X account.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The media organisation, however, did not respond to Mr Fani-Kayode’s allegation or explain why the live stream went off during the event.

Instead, it said it had sought an interview with him after he made his complaint to President Ramaphosa, but the request was declined.

It said, “Two points need clarifying. First, the SABC is a public service media, not a state broadcaster. Our mandate is to serve the public interest through independent, impartial and credible journalism.

“The Presidency’s livestream arrangements and SABC News’ editorial coverage are separate matters.”

World.title: Tanzania vs Nigeria: Super Eagles arrive in Zanzibar for crucial clash
World.content:
Nigeria’s Super Eagles have arrived in Zanzibar ahead of Tuesday’s crucial 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying encounter against Tanzania.

The Nigerian delegation included 23 players, coaches, backroom staff, representatives of the National Sports Commission (NSC) and Nigeria Football Federation (NFF), selected journalists and members of the supporters club.

The team travelled to the East African island on Sunday, two days after securing a 3-1 victory over Tanzania in the first leg at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State.

A second-half brace from substitute Tolu Arokodare helped the Super Eagles claim all three points after Alhassan Yusuf had given Nigeria an early lead in the encounter played on Friday.

Yusuf opened the scoring in the second minute, but Tanzania drew level through Alphonce Msanga in the 32nd minute.

Arokodare, introduced at the start of the second half, restored Nigeria’s advantage in the 52nd minute before completing his brace eight minutes later to secure the victory.

The Super Eagles will now seek another win when both teams meet at the Amaan Stadium in Zanzibar on Tuesday.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The return fixture is particularly important for Nigeria, who are chasing the only available qualification ticket from Group L, with Tanzania already assured of a place at the tournament as co-hosts alongside Kenya and Uganda.

Nigeria currently have six points from three matches and occupy second position in the group, one point behind leaders Guinea-Bissau, who have seven points.

The Super Eagles began their campaign with a 2-1 victory over Madagascar in Uyo before suffering a disappointing 3-0 defeat away to Guinea-Bissau.

The victory over Tanzania restored some confidence in Eric Chelle’s team, but another positive result on Tuesday would be important to their qualification ambitions.

Nigeria will, however, be without Ademola Lookman, who has been ruled out of the return fixture after sustaining a knee ligament sprain during Friday’s encounter.

The forward was instrumental in Nigeria’s opening goal in Uyo before being substituted in the first half.

With Guinea-Bissau also competing for the group’s remaining qualification place, the Super Eagles cannot afford another slip-up as the race for the 2027 AFCON ticket intensifies.

World.title: NAF to hold memorial for victims of October 5 aircraft crash
World.content:
The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has announced plans to hold a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony for victims of its NAF 931 aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ondo State, on 26 November,

The ceremony, scheduled to take place at the National Military Cemetery in Abuja, will honour those who lost their lives in the 5 October accident, as the air force continues investigations into the circumstances surrounding the crash.

In a statement on Sunday, the NAF spokesperson, Ehimen Ejodame, said the ceremony would bring together bereaved families, colleagues, friends and members of the military community to pay their last respects to the deceased and recognise their service and sacrifice.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that NAF announced it had recovered the aircraft’s Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR), alongside other wreckage and relevant evidence from the crash site.

Mr Ejodame reiterated these recoveries, saying data retrieved from the recorder was being analysed and would contribute significantly to the ongoing investigation.

He added that recovery operations had yielded several human remains and aircraft fragments, while the identification of the recovered remains was still ongoing.

The air force spokesperson attributed the difficulties encountered during the exercise to the swampy nature of the terrain and the depth to which some of the wreckage had penetrated the ground.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the investigation was progressing in collaboration with the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) and the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA).

Mr Ejodame noted that NAF was engaging relevant agencies to address environmental concerns arising from the recovery exercise and ensure appropriate remediation after the operation.

This newspaper reported that the traditional ruler of Igbokoda raised an alarm over water and air pollution following the crash, warning that the community faces a public health and economic crisis.

Background

The accident occurred when the ATR-42 aircraft, designated NAF 931, crashed in a swampy area near the Naval Base in Igbokoda, Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State, while travelling from Benin City to Lagos on a routine mission.

Air traffic controllers reportedly lost contact with the aircraft at about 9:13 am, after which the wreckage was located near the Naval Base. All 25 people aboard, comprising five crew members and 20 passengers, died in the accident, according to the air force.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that the casualty figure was initially disputed after Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo announced that 32 people, comprising 25 passengers and seven crew members, were aboard.

However, the NAF subsequently clarified that 25 people were on the aircraft, explaining that the discrepancy resulted from differences in the interpretation of aviation terminology.

It said the final figure comprised five active crew members and 20 passengers, including two military officials classified as non-active crew members but travelling as passengers.

Following the crash, the Chief of the Air Staff, Sunday Aneke, ordered a comprehensive investigation and search-and-rescue operations. The NAF confirmed that no survivors were found and subsequently released the names of all 25 victims. Mr Aneke, an air marshal, also expressed condolences to their families and assured them of the Service’s support.

On 13 October, the air force announced the constitution of a 12-member specialist aircraft accident investigation board to establish the circumstances and causes of the crash and recommend measures to prevent a recurrence.

World.title: How Tinubu’s reforms averted Nigeria’s economic collapse – Gov Mbah
World.content:
Governor of Enugu State, Peter Mbah, says Nigeria would have suffered total economic collapse but for President Bola Tinubu’s courageous reforms, arguing that the removal of fuel subsidy and floating of the naira only waited until the President’s assumption of office in 2023 because the nation delayed the ‘evil day’ and lived on borrowed time.

He gave the insights at the weekend during the launch of “As Tinubu Mbah Moves” (ATM), a support group convened by the Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Dr. Kingsley Udeh (SAN), and dedicated to the re-election of President Tinubu and Governor Mbah in Enugu.

Speaking to the mammoth crowd, he said, “It would have been a lot easier for any leader to just continue with the status quo and carry on on the basis of business as usual. But for Bola Ahmed Tinubu, it was business unusual that led to the bold initiatives.

“As a person who had played very actively in the oil and gas sector, I had written quite a lot of features and articles arguing against the fuel subsidy regime long before now, for it was clear to me, even from the point of a major player in that sector, that the subsidy regime was not sustainable because of the economic devastation it was causing to us as Nigerians. We were just basically postponing the evil day.

“We were just digging our poverty pits continually. We were actually digging deeper into that pit of poverty. And it would have taken a very courageous leader in his first term to say, ‘Look, if we have to build for the future, if we have to think about our children, then we must take out the subsidy and we must also unify the exchange rate regime.’”

Mbah took a swipe at the foreign exchange regime before the floating of the naira by Tinubu, describing it as a cesspool of corruption.

“We got to a point in this country where even salary earners, once they get paid, would run to the bureau de change to change it rather than hold their salary in naira. Confidence was completely eroded in the naira. Nobody wanted to touch it with the tip of their finger. And that was the recipe for a failed nation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“If you wanted to do a study or research of any failed nation, it is when the country, the citizens themselves, begin to lose confidence in their currency. And that was the environment that this President inherited.

“It was a major cesspool of corruption. The arbitrage was obvious and people were being taken advantage of. What was happening between the official and the parallel market was terrible. And some people were benefiting from that arbitrage at the expense of the economy. But it took this President’s understanding of the economy to be able to make those bold decisions,” he explained.

Continuing, he said that the stabilisation of the nation’s macroeconomic indicators by the Tinubu administration had encouraged Foreign Direct Investments (FDIs) necessary for improving Nigeria’s microeconomic indices, such as household incomes and employment.

“This essentially is something that is largely driven by private capital. But government enables it by policies because I can tell you that private capital does not go to where you do not have stability.

“If your macro indicators are under pressure; if you have not addressed your foreign reserve, your foreign exchange regime, your inflationary rates, and all that, you do not have any chance of attracting private capital because private capital is blind. It is not emotional. It goes to where it makes return on investment, where it can be guaranteed some high level of security.

“Because we did not have all those before now, private capital was not coming. So, what the bold policies and initiatives this President took have done is that those macro pressures have largely been eased. And what you are now witnessing in our economy is a growth trajectory.

“So, private capital is now looking towards our country. You can see quite a number of FDI deals being closed – not MoA (Memorandum of Agreement) or MoU (Memorandum of Understanding). These are final investment decisions being made across different sectors, particularly in the oil and gas sector. You can see billions of dollars coming towards this direction today.

“People who have dollars are now going back to exchange their dollars because that confidence has been restored.

“So, now that we have stabilised our macro indicators, we have now started witnessing growth, albeit not to the level we aspire.

“The next thing is going to be shared prosperity because you are going to see that growth cascade. You are going to see it get to the households. You are going to see it create employment. So, our unemployed youths would be gainfully employed. That is the way it works,” he explained.

Citing Enugu State as an example, Mbah also credited the President with freeing funds that could have been sunk into subsidy, thus arming states with resources to embark on massive development projects that impact the lives of the people.

The Governor, therefore, urged Nigerians to vote en masse for the President to complete the job he started, saying it was the only realistic option.

“Nations are not built by abandoning challenges halfway through. If we have gone through this whole process of difficult periods when it appeared as if all was doomed to a point where we are beginning to see the light at the end of the tunnel, we cannot abandon what has been started. No great sailor abandons his ship because of a rough sea, mid-sea. You have to sail to get to your destination,” he said.

He urged ATM members to take the message of the successes of Tinubu’s reforms and the President’s various infrastructural and policy interventions in the South East to the electorate.

Meanwhile, Dr Udeh (SAN) said the support group would focus its mobilisation efforts on non-members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) across the 4,145 polling units of Enugu State ahead of the 2027 general elections, deploying technology to register members, track their participation and monitor its mobilisation activities through an online registration portal.

World.title: Tinubu prepares five-year plan to end Boko Haram insurgency, tackle insecurity
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu’s five-year plan to end the 17-year Boko Haram insurgency and tackle other security threats across Nigeria is ready, the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has said.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that Nigeria’s multidimensional security threats have triggered Mr Tinubu’s security reforms, including a recruitment drive, expansion of commands, plans for the creation of state police and investment in military hardware and infrastructure.

Boko Haram insurgency has entered its 17th year, spreading from the North-east to the North-central and South-west, where Boko Haram kidnapped schoolchildren in two separate attacks, as documented here and here.

The military has attributed Boko Haram’s expansion to its sustained offensive against terrorists, vowing to maintain the pressure. However, terrorist groups continue to exploit security vacuums and local grievances in poorly governed areas, consolidating their presence, winning over sections of local communities while continuing to kill and abduct their targets.

The five-year plan

The plan is designed to strengthen the country’s security architecture, improve military effectiveness and provide a coordinated response to terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other forms of criminality.

Dele Alake, spokesperson for the APC Presidential Campaign Council, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, saying the framework would align defence priorities, operational requirements, military capability development and expenditure with Nigeria’s current and anticipated security challenges.

Mr Alake, who doubles as the Minister of Solid Minerals, stated that the Tinubu administration has recorded the elimination of more than 15,000 Boko Haram insurgents and bandits in the last three years, while over 130,000 Boko Haram fighters and their dependents have surrendered through Operation Safe Corridor, a controversial federal government rehabilitation programme for repentant insurgents.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

National Security Adviser (NSA) Nuhu Ribadu had shared similar figures at an APC summit.

Mr Alake said the recent figures reflected the administration’s “two-phase” approach to insecurity, combining sustained military operations with non-kinetic interventions.

As part of efforts to expand the military’s operational capacity, Mr Tinubu has created four new Nigerian Army divisions and restructured existing military formations to improve operational coverage and enable troops to respond more swiftly to security threats.

The president has also approved the establishment of two additional army depots in Osogbo, Osun State, and Amasiri-Edda, Ebonyi State, to expand recruitment and training capacity.

The two facilities are designed to accommodate 6,000 recruits each, bringing their combined training capacity to 12,000 soldiers at a time.

The Osogbo facility currently has 5,210 recruits undergoing training, said Mr Alake.

The administration has also approved the recruitment of an additional 28,000 soldiers and 50,000 police officers to strengthen military manpower, internal security and the country’s response to criminal activities.

On military infrastructure and personnel welfare, Mr Alake highlighted a 700-unit military barracks project in Ikere-Ekiti, Ekiti State, which is intended to provide accommodation and operational support for military personnel in the area.

He said the five-year defence plan would also prioritise intelligence, surveillance and coordination, with government investments guided by identified security threats, operational requirements and national priorities.

He added that the framework was expected to improve combat readiness, address critical capability gaps, optimise available resources and minimise unnecessary expenditure and wastage.

However, Mr Alake did not provide a specific implementation date for the plan, its projected cost or details of its funding arrangements.

World.title: 2027: Jigawa ADC backs Atiku, passes vote of confidence in state leadership
World.content:
Candidates of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Jigawa State have declared their support for former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and his running mate, Rotimi Amaechi, for the 2027 presidential election.

They announced the commitment in Dutse on Sunday at a meeting of the party’s flagbearers in the state.

The gathering was led by the governorship candidate and state party leader, Sabo Nakudu—who recently received his Certificate of Return after clinching the party’s governorship ticket—and brought together 45 legislative candidates across the state.

The candidates pledged their loyalty to the ADC and vowed to work toward the electoral victory of their presidential candidate and other candidates contesting across Jigawa’s constituencies.

The flagbearers also passed a vote of confidence in both the current and legacy leadership of the party at the state and local government levels, led by Sani Gumel.

“We call on all party members, stakeholders, and supporters to remain united and work diligently for the victory of the ADC in Jigawa State,” the party leadership stated at the event as political activities intensify ahead of the 2027 polls.

The candidates committed to conducting peaceful, issue-based campaigns throughout the electoral cycle.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The party’s chairperson, Mr Gumel, commended the governorship candidate, Mr Nakudu, for his leadership and urged all flagbearers to remain focused and disciplined in their grassroots mobilisation.

Certificate of return

The meeting in Dutse followed Mr Nakudu’s formal receipt of his certificate of return following his victory in the party’s primary election held in May.

“I have received the certificate of return as the ADC governorship candidate for Jigawa State, following the primary election conducted in recent months.

“The ceremony took place at the national headquarters of the party located in the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja”, Mr Nakudu stated

The event showed Mr Nakudu displaying the certificate alongside the Jigawa State ADC chairperson, Mr Gumel and other state party chieftains.

The presentation of the certificate of return follows months of internal friction that fractured the Jigawa State chapter of the ADC following the May 2026 gubernatorial primary.

In the 28 May primary, Mr Nakudu defeated former federal lawmaker, Bashir Adamu.

Mr Adamu rejected the primary results, petitioned the party’s appeal committee, and accused Mr Nakudu’s camp of hijacking the party machinery.

World.title: TAJBank Wins Best Non-Interest Bank Award
World.content:
TAJBank Limited, Nigeria’s largest non-interest bank, has, for the fifth consecutive time, won the Non-Interest Bank of the Year Award at the BusinessDay Banks and Other Financial Institutions (BAFI) Awards 2026.

The Founder and Managing Director of TAJBank, Mr. Hamid Joda, said the recognition reinforced the bank’s responsibility to widen access to non-interest banking and deliver transparent and customer-focused financial services that meet the needs of individuals, businesses and underserved communities.

Joda, according to a statement issued at the weekend by the bank’s Head of Marketing Communications, Isiaka Wakili, thanked the management of BusinessDay Media Ltd for recognising TAJBank’s contributions to the nation’s non-interest banking industry.

“We are deeply honoured to receive the Non-Interest Bank of the Year Award at the 2026 BAFI Awards. This recognition belongs to our Board of Directors, management, dedicated staff and most importantly, our valued customers, whose confidence continues to inspire us.

“We see this award not merely as a celebration of our achievements, but as a renewed call to deepen financial inclusion, strengthen our commitment to ethical banking and develop innovative solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers,” Joda said.

In his remarks, the Co-ounder/Executive Director of TAJBank, Mr. Sheriff Idi, said the award reflected the bank’s progress in building a distinctive identity in Nigeria’s financial services industry.

He noted that TAJBank had continued to strengthen its market position through customer-focused solutions, operational innovation and a business model designed to meet the diverse financial needs of its growing clientele.

He said the award would spur the bank to consolidate its gains, explore new growth opportunities and deliver greater value to customers while reinforcing its position in the nation’s non-interest banking sector.

World.title: Airline operators, customs agents, others back Tax Ombud, seek fairer tax system
World.content:
Dr. Allen Onyema, Vice President of the Airline Operators of Nigeria (AON), has applauded the establishment of the Office of the Tax Ombud, describing it as a significant institutional intervention that provides the aviation sector and taxpayers generally with an impartial platform for resolving complaints and addressing grievances.

Delivering a goodwill message at a Town Hall Meeting organised by the Office of the Tax Ombud in Lagos last weekend Onyema highlighted the association’s persistent efforts to draw attention to its grievances at various levels of government, including security and legislative institutions.

Onyema made a strong case for the harmonisation of tax regimes to promote fair competition and sustainability, particularly for private and charter airline operators.

The Tax Ombud/Chief Executive, Dr. John Nwabueze, said the mandate of his Office includes promoting fairness, transparency and accountability in Nigeria’s tax administration system.

He commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, for pioneering the establishment of the Office of the Tax Ombud, which is mandated to address operational, administrative and procedural grievances relating to taxes, levies, regulatory fees and customs duties.

Nwabueze emphasised that the services of the Office are free of charge to Nigerians, providing an impartial platform for resolving disputes through mediation rather than adversarial proceedings.

He further explained that the Office does not determine substantive tax liabilities but focuses on addressing gaps in complaint management and promoting voluntary compliance by building trust between taxpayers and revenue authorities.

Underscoring the importance of stakeholder collaboration involving taxpayers, professional associations, business organisations, civil society and the media, he encouraged participants to share their experiences candidly and offer constructive recommendations.

Nwabueze, who commended the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of Economy, Mr. Taiwo Oyedele, for his leadership in tax reforms, reassured participants of the Office’s independence and commitment to resolving complaints promptly, reiterating its guiding principle of “bridging differences and building trust.”

Engr. Olusola Obadimu, Director-General of the Nigerian Association of Chambers of Commerce, Industry, Mines and Agriculture (NACCIMA), described the Town Hall Meeting as a vital platform for addressing the persistent challenges confronting businesses and industries, ranging from inadequate infrastructure and rising energy costs to the increasing burden of taxation.

Obadimu expressed support for the role of the Tax Ombud and commended Dr. Nwabueze for facilitating open dialogue between government and private-sector stakeholders.

He called on policymakers to prioritise expanding the business landscape and supporting entire economic ecosystems, pledging NACCIMA’s collaboration with the Tax Ombud in promoting an equitable business environment conducive to enterprise growth and national development.

Speaking on behalf of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (ICAN), Mr. Adewale Taju Olayinka emphasised that a fair and trustworthy tax system is fundamental to voluntary compliance and sustainable national revenue generation.

Olayinka welcomed the establishment of the Office of the Tax Ombud as an important step towards strengthening accountability in tax administration and reaffirmed ICAN’s commitment to collaborating with the Office on professional capacity-building and taxpayer education.

Delivering a goodwill message on behalf of the Association of National Accountants of Nigeria (ANAN), Mr. Bernard Akinnola underscored the importance of an equitable and predictable tax system, particularly amid ongoing reforms aimed at strengthening transparency and fiscal sustainability.

He outlined five core principles that ANAN believes should underpin Nigeria’s tax administration system: transparency, equity, respect for taxpayer rights, professionalism and stakeholder collaboration.

Dr. Titilayo Fowokan, speaking on behalf of the President of the Chartered Institute of Taxation of Nigeria (CITN), described the Tax Ombud as a landmark institutional innovation in Nigeria’s tax administration framework, with the potential to strengthen accountability, protect taxpayer rights and promote transparent grievance resolution.

She noted that CITN considers the independent platform essential to building taxpayer confidence and fostering constructive relationships between taxpayers and revenue authorities.

Fowokan reaffirmed CITN’s commitment to supporting the Tax Ombud’s mandate and promoting high professional standards in tax administration.

Speaking on behalf of the Executive Director of the Nigerian Export Promotion Council (NEPC), Arc. Benedict Itegbe commended the Office of the Tax Ombud for extending its stakeholder engagement to Lagos.

He noted that free and impartial mechanisms for seeking redress are crucial to promoting a competitive non-oil export sector.

Itegbe urged exporters to maintain comprehensive records and take advantage of the avenues provided by the Tax Ombud to address complaints relating to unfair treatment and complex tax-compliance challenges.

He assured the Office of NEPC’s readiness to promote awareness of its services, support systemic improvements and sustain collaboration in bridging gaps between taxpayers and revenue authorities.

Mr. Olufemi Adewole, representing the Depot and Petroleum Products Marketers Association of Nigeria (DAPPMAN), highlighted the significant operational and fiscal challenges confronting oil and gas marketers, particularly delays in VAT refunds and high working-capital costs.

He acknowledged the government’s revenue-generation needs but stressed that taxation should not contribute to escalating the cost of living. He therefore advocated regular reviews of fiscal policies affecting petroleum marketers to assess their impact on downstream operations.

Prince Olusegun Oduntan, National Vice President, Association of Nigerian Licensed Customs Agents (ANLCA) highlighted concerns over personal taxes, local government levies for various amenities, and the method of taxing based on total turnover rather than actual profit margins.

He emphasized the association’s intention to submit a detailed position paper to the Office of the Tax Ombud, seeking redress and more equitable tax assessment practices tailored to the realities of their business model.

The Town Hall Meeting was attended by representatives of the Nigerian Association of Small and Medium Enterprises (NASME), National Union of Road Transport Workers (NURTW), Nigerian Association of Small Scale Industrialists (NASSI), Nigeria Network of NGOs (NNNGO), Nigeria Employers’ Consultative Association (NECA), Lagos Hotel Owners and Managers Association, Association of Nigerian Licensed Customs Agents, Petroleum and Natural Gas Senior Staff Association of Nigeria (PENGASSAN), and Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN) among others.

World.title: Without manufacturing $1tr economy is an illusion
World.content:
File image.

By Dele Sobowale

Japan in fact offers a relevant historical example of what can happen to an economy which falls behind in the global manufacturing race. Even in Africa, the Giant of Africa is lagging behind at least three other economies in the scale and scope of manufacturing. Consequently, the politically-motivated promise to make Nigeria a one trillion dollar economy by 2030 is only one of the many illusions of the Tinubu administration. Desirable as it is, a $1 trillion economy is unachievable for reasons too numerous to discuss now, but, the cardinal reason is Nigeria’s weak manufacturing base – forcing us to import thousands of products which we can, with little effort, produce locally.

I was a Senior Lecturer/Consultant working with the Nigerian Institute of Management, NIM, in 1992, when Morita wrote the article in which that statement was made. The NIM Library was my second home and office. When not busy teaching courses in Sales, Marketing and General Management, I was in the Library reading and gathering materials for my lectures, as well as my book of quotations, VBQ – which was published in 2007. Japan was the world’s second largest manufacturing economy as well as the second largest economy; and was threatening the American leadership in that regard. Several books were written on the Art of Japanese Management; leading American Business Schools included courses in Japanese business methods in their curricula as compulsory subjects. The Japanese economy was growing at 7 to 10 per cent annually; and projections were made regarding when it would overtake the US as the largest economy globally. China and India were nowhere in sight. Then, something happened.

Science and technology brought new products which called for new and modern factories. Western investors, scared by Japan’s growing economic prowess, diverted investments to other Asian economies – South Korea, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and China. Gradually, several South East Asian nations started challenging Japan in sectors such as electronics and ship building. Unnoticeable at first, but the steady erosion of Japanese share of global manufacturing eventually took its toll. Today, the second and third leading manufacturers are China and India. China is now the largest manufacturer; hotly pursued by China. Japan has dropped to the fifth position in global ranking measured in terms of Gross Domestic Productivity, GDP. China, not Japan, is now threatening the US leadership. Manufacturing is the primary reason for that change in the fortunes of nations.

Nigeria Is Missing The Boat Once Again

“Those who do not remember the past are condemned to repeat it.”

George Santayana, 1863-1952, VBQ p 93.

It might be difficult for the Generation Z youths to believe that Nigeria once embarked on rapid industrialization. The Gowon administration sent delegations to the United States in 1974 to appeal to young and well-educated Nigerians to return home and fill vacant positions opening up in manufacturing in several industrial layouts in Lagos, Ibadan, Kaduna, Kano, Portharcourt and Aba. I was one of those who responded to the call to return home and help Nigeria’s transformation to a manufacturing giant. On arrival in August 1974, my first working experience was at the Ilupeju Industrial Layout in Lagos. I soon discovered there were others in Lagos State – Ikeja, Iganmu and Apapa. My first trip to Portharcourt and Aba revealed the Trans Amadi and Ogbor Hill layouts respectively; the Northern legs of the national familiarization tour took me to Kano’s Bompai, Kaduna and Anglo Jos in Plateau state. Granted, everything I saw could not have been more than a few establishments on Route 128, Massachusetts, USA – where I gained industrial experience. But it was a promising start. Construction of new factories and expansion of old factories was going on at feverish pace. Jobs were available everywhere. I left manufacturing enterprises in 1990 after working in five different industrial layouts. The last was in Kalambina, Sokoto State.

Unfortunately, the 16 years between 1974 and 1990 represented the period of the rise and decline of manufacturing in Nigeria. Instead of building on what we started, gradual decline set in. SPARS, a retail outlet, has replaced our factory for analgesics and cough syrup. The brewery in Bompai lies in ruins; and the rice mill in Sokoto remains shut since 1991. Right now, the current reforms embarked upon by President Tinubu threaten to again set in motion the process which made manufacturing extremely difficult in Nigeria.

Current Situation: No Power; Expensive Credit

“Power supply plunges as gas shortage, water level worsen.”

VANGUARD, November 6, 2026

Manufacturing became very attractive in the 1970s when the Kainji Hydro Power Station was established. None of the industrial estates could have been started without relatively reliable public power supply. Definitely, Nigerian Paper Mill, Jeba; Nigerian Sugar Company, NISUCO and the Nigerian Yeast and Alcohol Manufacturing Company, both at Bacita, Kwara State could not have been started if they had to operate on generators. I was a consultant for the three; and I recall the discussions with their Chief Executive Officers. Without exception, they were certain their companies could not survive on generators. They were absolutely correct. On November 5, 2026, Nigeria was able to supply only 2,926MW to the entire nation. That is deeply concerning for two reasons. One, we achieved capacity to generate 4,000MW per day as far back as 2012. Fourteen years later, the Federal Government is still offering the same excuses for remaining stuck at 4,000MW on a good day. No $1 trillion economy generates less than 45,000MW. South Africa is Africa’s largest economy, far less than the $1 trillion economy. But, it already provides more than 45,000MW.

“Banks’ loan to manufacturers slumps 26.8% to N5.19trn.”

VANGUARD, October 26, 2026.

Credit is the soul of business and has been an axiom for several hundred years. Banks and financial institutions were established primarily to promote businesses; not to finance government deficits. The Great Depression in the last century, as well as the rise of Keynesianism, gave rise to governments invading banks to borrow funds for their operations. Deficit spending, once proposed as a short-term measure, has hardened into a permanent feature of fiscal policy. Very few governments now attempt to balance their budgets. Reliance on deficit spending and perpetual borrowing is the new normal. In the process, banks are increasingly called upon to extend credits to the government. Private sector borrowers, especially manufacturers are bearing the brunt of the new situation.

Nigerian manufacturers are being hammered three ways. First, they don’t receive as much as they would want. Second, the interest rates are exorbitant. Third, they compete against foreign producers whose governments provide support across the board and whose banks charge single digit interest rates. How we expect Nigerian manufacturers paying 30 per cent to compete with Chinese paying 2 per cent remains a mystery to me.

Follow me on Facebook @ J Israel Biola

World.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 16, 2026
World.content:
The Nigerian naira opened Monday, November 16, 2026, under mild pressure across the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) while maintaining relative stability in the parallel market.

At the official window, data published by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) shows the NFEM rate referencing ₦1,353.97 per dollar. This follows a ₦7.18 depreciation in the preceding session as corporate foreign exchange obligations and seasonal end-of-year import demand weighed on liquidity. Meanwhile, spot interbank indicators in early morning trading hovered around ₦1,343.35 per dollar as dealers awaited fresh intraday price discovery.

In the parallel market, also known as the black market, Bureau De Change (BDC) operators and street dealers in Lagos and Abuja quoted the US dollar at a buying rate of ₦1,380 and a selling rate of ₦1,390.

With the official rate standing at ₦1,353.97 and the parallel market selling at ₦1,390, the exchange rate spread between both markets sits at approximately ₦36.03 per dollar. Market analysts note that steady foreign reserve buffers and ongoing CBN market interventions continue to keep the disparity between the official and unofficial segments within a narrow band compared to historical volatility.

World.title: Stock market rebounds as investors reap N2.2trn amid decline in oil price
World.content:
By Peter Egwuatu

The Nigerian stock market rebounded last week after weeks of sustained pressure from profit taking led to decline in stock value.

Equity investors on the Nigerian Exchange Limited, NGX, last week, reaped over N2.2 trillion in capital gains leading the NGX market capitalisation, to close last week at N163.795 trillion, up from N161.593 trillion the previous week.

Similarly, another major market performance indicator, NGX All Share Index, ASI, surged by 1.4 % to close at 252,269.16 points from 248,877.22 points the previous week, indicating renewed demand for selected heavyweight stocks, which dominated the market.

Analysts noted that although buying interests remained evident in major banking and industrial stocks , the broader market reflected a mixed trading pattern, with investors maintaining selective positions amid intermittent profit-taking in several stocks

The positive performance, according to analysts, highlights the continued resilience of the domestic stock market, which has maintained substantial gains since the beginning of the year.

Reacting to market performance and outlook analysts at InvestData Consulting Limited, said : “ The immediate market outlook remains cautiously positive, supported by the strong year-to-date return and continued interest in selected large-cap stocks. Nevertheless, investors are likely to maintain a selective approach, considering corporate earnings, dividend expectations, valuation levels and prevailing macroeconomic conditions before increasing their exposure. The possibility of further profit-taking cannot be ruled out, particularly in stocks that have recorded significant gains in recent sessions.

Overall, the market appears to be consolidating its recent advances while maintaining an underlying bullish bias. The ability of the index to break above the 255,000-point resistance level, alongside improved market participation, will be important in determining whether the current upward movement can extend into another phase of appreciation.” They further noted that the political outcome of the US midterm elections introduced additional uncertainty into the market adding that the developments have placed renewed attention on the possibility of diplomatic negotiations and their implications for global crude supply.

“For Nigeria, the movement in international crude prices remains particularly important given the country’s dependence on oil exports for foreign exchange earnings and government revenue. A sustained decline in crude prices could place additional pressure on projected oil receipts, especially if production levels remain below expectations. Conversely, elevated prices could support external earnings, although the benefits would depend on domestic production performance, export volumes and fiscal management” the analysts added.

World.title: Imposing Tinubu in 2027 will trigger crisis — Ex-APC spokesman
World.content:
Timi Frank

ABUJA — FORMER Deputy National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Mr Timi Frank, yesterday, warned that any attempt to force President Bola Tinubu back into office in 2027 could plunge the country into crisis.

Read Also: ‘How Tinubu will end insecurity ready’

Frank, who is the Ambassador to East Africa and the Middle East of the United Liberation Movement for West Papua, ULMWP, said Nigerians would not accept an outcome that contradicts their votes.

“Nigerians will not accept a situation in which someone is declared the winner when the people know they did not vote for him. They should not push the country into a crisis by attempting to impose him on the people,” he warned.

Urging the president to abandon his re-election ambition and guarantee a transparent electoral process, he said: “Whoever wins should be allowed to emerge as the choice of the people.”

Frank also expressed concern over alleged attempts by some political actors to manipulate the electoral process.

He described the public protest against Tinubu after prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in Area 1, Garki, Abuja, last Friday as evidence of growing dissatisfaction with the administration.

Tinubu reportedly faced boos from some Hausa protesters who chanted “Ba ma yi” (we don’t want you) after the prayers. In a viral video, some protesters were seen removing and destroying his campaign posters and billboards in parts of Area 1.

Frank condemned the protesters for choosing a religious occasion to vent their displeasure and commended the President’s security detail for ensuring his safety and de-escalating the situation.

He nevertheless urged the President to recognise the significance of the public reaction.

“The rejection was total and unmistakable. No Nigerian president has been embarrassed like this publicly. The way Nigerians rejected him speaks volumes but should he decide to go ahead and he loses, he should be prepared to accept defeat just like former President Goodluck Jonathan did,” he said.

The former APC spokesman said he was worried by what he called a growing gap between the assurances given to the President by political associates and the mood of the people.

“I have seen the confidence with which some people are assuring President Tinubu that he will win the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, and that he is firmly in control. But the reported embarrassment he suffered during a prayer session in Abuja tells a different story.

“What happened in the FCT last Friday showed that political assurances and promises are not necessarily a reflection of the reality on the ground. The public reaction reflects the anger and dissatisfaction of Nigerians, which those around the President may not be telling him about.

“What happened in FCT and Jos after the APC rally has shown that people like the FCT minister, Nyesom Wike promising him 80 percent of votes in Abuja and the Governor of Edo State, Monday Okpebholo vowing to give him 2.5 million votes in Edo State, would disappoint him due to the reality on ground.

“Those telling him to continue and assuring him that he will win the next election are merely deceiving him. Even some people within his political circle, including those involved in his campaign, know that selling his candidacy to Nigerians will be difficult,” Frank said.

He alleged that financial considerations were influencing the positions of some political associates, and said the President needed honest assessments of his performance and popularity.

“I am giving him this advice because I genuinely want him to listen to the truth. Those around him may not be telling him that he has become very unpopular and that continuing in the presidential race may be a difficult undertaking. My advice is that he should take a bow and leave the race. He should take this advice seriously,” he said.

Frank urged Tinubu to take a cue from opposition figures, including former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and former Anambra State governor, Peter Obi, whom he said draw large crowds without financial inducements.

“Wherever these opposition leaders go, Nigerians come out in large numbers to receive them without being induced with rice or money. Their reception should tell the President something about the mood of the country,” he said.

He listed hunger, unemployment, rising living costs and insecurity among the factors fuelling public anger.

“If the President had performed well, there would be no need for the desperation we are witnessing today,” he said.

Frank also questioned the credibility of endorsements for the President, alleging that some individuals and groups were motivated by anticipated financial benefits rather than genuine public sentiment.

“President Tinubu still has an opportunity to make history and have his name written in gold. He can achieve this by ensuring that the country conducts a free, fair and credible election,” he said.

Vanguard News

World.title: Fani-Kayode refused interview after live-stream ‘exclusion’ — SABC
World.content:
The South African Broadcasting Corporation, SABC, has said Nigeria’s High Commissioner to the country, Femi Fani-Kayode, declined an interview invitation, following his protest over the exclusion of his speech from a livestream of a diplomatic ceremony hosted by President Cyril Ramaphosa.

Read Also: South Africa releases Fani-Kayode’s speech after protest

The SABC, in a statement issued yesterday, said it regretted the envoy’s decision but remained open to engaging with him and the Nigerian High Commission.

The response followed Fani-Kayode’s complaint that his introduction and speech were omitted from the broadcaster’s livestream of the presentation of letters of credence ceremony held at the Sefako Makgatho Presidential Guest House in Pretoria on Friday.

“We regret that the High Commissioner declined an interview with SABC News, reportedly because of his dissatisfaction with the livestream of the ceremony. We respect his decision and remain open to engaging with him and the Nigerian High Commission,” the statement said.

Notably, the SABC did not address the specific allegation that Fani-Kayode’s presentation was excluded from the livestream of the ceremony.

It, however, rejected the description of it as a state broadcaster, insisting that it was a public service media organisation committed to independent, impartial and credible journalism.

“Two points need clarifying. First, the SABC is a public service media, not a state broadcaster. Our mandate is to serve the public interest through independent, impartial and credible journalism. The Presidency’s livestream arrangements and SABC News’ editorial coverage are separate matters.

“Secondly, SABC News did cover the ceremony. It was carried on the SABC News LIVE channel on SABC+, and the High Commissioner’s arrival was shown during a live crossing on the SABC News Channel (DStv Channel 404). We also published a clip on our official X account of the High Commissioner speaking to President Cyril Ramaphosa.

“The SABC remains committed to upholding the principles of fairness, impartiality and editorial independence in its coverage, as well as value our longstanding relationship with Nigeria,” the statement read.

Recall that Fani-Kayode had earlier accused the South African Presidency of deliberately excluding Nigeria’s delegation from the livestream of the ceremony, which involved 15 ambassadors presenting their letters of credence to Ramaphosa.

The envoy said the introductions and speeches of 14 other ambassadors were broadcast, while Nigeria’s segment was omitted, with the livestream resuming after he had concluded his address.

He also disclosed that he declined an interview offered by SABC News at the venue, saying he had been displeased with the treatment of the Nigerian delegation.

However, the South African Presidency later released the full video of the ceremony, including Fani-Kayode’s speech, on its YouTube channel.

The controversy subsequently sparked a public exchange between the Nigerian High Commission and Vincent Magwenya, spokesperson for Ramaphosa.

World.title: Economy Palava: Traders decry rising waybill ‘store keep’ charges
World.content:
By Elizabeth Adegbesan

Small-scale traders operating across major markets in the country have raised the alarm over arbitrary and escalating storage fees, locally known as “store keep money”, charged by transport operators and motor park agents on delayed waybills, warning that the practice is eroding their capital and threatening their livelihoods.

For many market women who rely on interstate commercial buses and trucks to restock goods such as foodstuffs, textiles, and household provisions, waybill logistics are the lifeline of daily commerce.

However, traders said the shrinking grace periods before daily demurrage charges kick in have turned routine restocking into a financial burden.

Economy&Lifestyle visits to some markets revealed a widespread frustration among traders, many of whom operate on thin profit margins and depend on daily turnover or microfinance loans to sustain their stalls.

Mrs. Grace Okafor, a wholesale dealer in dried seafood and condiments, recounted how a 24-hour delay caused by heavy rainfall cost her nearly half of her expected profit on a recent consignment.

“My goods arrived at the park late in the evening when no one could go out.

“By the time I got there the next afternoon with a tricycle to carry my sacks, the park officials insisted I had exceeded their grace period and demanded N6,000 for ‘store keep’.

“We cannot increase our selling prices because customers are already struggling to buy. That money came straight out of my capital.”

Other traders noted that the lack of standardized billing across motor parks leaves them vulnerable to exploitation, particularly when unforeseen emergencies delay pickup.

Mrs. Comfort Momoh, who trades in fabrics and wrappers, stated that arbitrary fee hikes are discouraging traders from ordering goods in bulk.

“There is no fixed rate or clear receipt for this store keep money; it depends on the mood of whoever is on duty at the park store,” she said.

“Sometimes a driver does not call on time to inform you that the vehicle has arrived, yet the park starts counting storage days against you. By the time you clear your bale, the profit is already gone.”

Similarly, Alhaja Rasheedat Suleiman, a palm oil and grain merchant, called on market associations and transport unions to intervene and establish fair, transparent guidelines.

“We understand that parks have limited space, but giving traders at least 48 hours of grace after proper notification is only fair,” Alhaja Suleiman said.

“Most of us are breadwinners supporting our families from these stalls. If transport companies and park unions do not regulate these charges, many women will be forced out of business.”

When contacted, a park supervisor at an interstate loading bay in, who declined to be named, defended the charges, stating that limited warehouse space and the risk of theft or damage make it necessary to compel traders to clear their goods promptly.

This growing extortion racket is more than a minor transport nuisance; it is an informal tax suffocating Nigeria’s micro and small enterprises.

Individuals are not left out of this ordeal

Mrs. Chidinma Okafor, a tailor, recounted her ordeal saying: “My sister sent me a small carton of clothes from Lagos and paid N4,000 at the park.

“When the driver called me, I was already waiting at the terminal. Yet, he refused to bring the bag down from the roof rack until I paid N3,500 for store room and park settlement.

“The bag never even touched the ground, let alone entered a store room.”

Ibrahim Jato, a baker, said: “I ordered baking ingredients from Onitsha for a weekend wedding cake, and the supplier already cleared the transport fare.”

“When I got to the park, three men surrounded the boot and demanded N8,000 for ‘store room security’ before releasing my items.

“ When I protested, the driver threatened to lock the boot and return with the goods the next day.

“I had no choice but to pay.”

Vanguard News

World.title: 2027: Can INEC, Security Agencies Save Nigeria from Political Violence?
World.content:
Iyobosa Uwugiaren writes that as Nigeria moves towards the 2027 general elections, the Independent National Electoral Commission cannot afford another credibility crisis. Its preparations must be guided by transparency, consistency and strict adherence to the Electoral Act and the Constitution

I have followed recent reports of violence accompanying political events in different parts of the country. Every form of violence stands condemned. Violence should never have a place in our political campaigns as we move towards the 2027 general elections.”

These were the words of President Bola Tinubu in a personally signed statement titled ‘Let’s Shun Violence: Our Campaigns Must Be About Issues That Promote the Welfare of Our People”, issued on Friday.

The President, apparently concerned about the growing incidents of political violence across the country, called on political leaders and their supporters to embrace peaceful campaigns, insisting that political competition should be about ideas and national development rather than hostility and confrontation.

“Our campaigns should be about issues, a contestation of ideas that promote the welfare of our people and the progress of our country,” he said.

Tinubu, who reiterated his commitment to a peaceful, free and fair election, reminded political actors that belonging to different parties or pursuing different political ambitions did not make Nigerians enemies. He also reiterated his directive to security agencies to be firm against anyone attempting to undermine public order.

Political analysts said the President’s intervention underscores growing concerns that the 2027 general election could become one of the most antagonistic electoral contests in Nigeria’s democratic history.

To be sure, across several states, including Delta, Edo, Borno, Ekiti, Kaduna, Ebonyi, Enugu, Kano and Lagos, reports of political intimidation, attacks on opponents and inflammatory statements by political actors have raised serious questions about the safety of citizens and the future of the country’s democracy. Perhaps more disturbing is the emergence of the slogan, “Rig and Die”, among some political supporters and actors.

There are suggestions from many stakeholders that rather than dismissing the expression as ordinary campaign rhetoric, it should be treated as a dangerous warning about the direction of Nigeria’s political culture. According to them, it reflects an increasingly disturbing mindset in which electoral victory is regarded as a matter of life and death, while democratic competition is reduced to a struggle for political survival.

The implications are frightening. If political actors and their supporters are already threatening violence months before the general election, what should Nigerians and the international community expect when voting, counting and declaration of results begin?

Recent developments have reinforced these concerns. The General Abdulsalami Abubakar-led National Peace Committee, in its monitoring report covering August 19 to October 27, 2026, recorded 109 breaches of the National Peace Accord across 26 states and the Federal Capital Territory. Political violence and thuggery accounted for 33 incidents, while misinformation, deepfakes and disinformation accounted for another 29.

These figures suggest that the threat to peaceful elections is neither imaginary nor confined to isolated political disagreements.

INEC and other stakeholders have consequently warned against the “Rig and Die” rhetoric, describing it as a threat to innocent citizens, electoral officials, party agents and observers. While the warning is necessary, it raises a fundamental question: Can INEC and security agencies prevent Nigeria from descending into electoral violence?

One of the greatest challenges confronting Nigeria’s democracy has always been the growing perception among politicians that political power is worth acquiring at virtually any cost. Elections should provide citizens with an opportunity to choose their leaders through peaceful competition.

From media reports, the problem is not restricted to one political party. Across the political divide, there are individuals whose actions and utterances suggest a willingness to undermine democratic principles to secure electoral advantage. This is why the temptation to blame only the ruling party or opposition for the present political atmosphere is not flying.

Political violence has no party colour. Whoever instigates, finances, encourages or participates in electoral violence, regardless of political affiliation, should be seen as an enemy of democracy.

It is particularly disturbing that some political leaders, who should be preaching peace and responsible political engagement, sometimes employ language capable of encouraging their supporters to resort to violence.

The consequences, however, are often borne by innocent citizens. Young people are recruited as political thugs, communities are divided, businesses are disrupted and lives are lost.

Ironically, politicians who instigate these confrontations are rarely the first victims. They are often protected by security personnel, while vulnerable young people bear the consequences. The recent incidents in Asaba, Delta State, and Lagos, where some thugs reportedly lost their lives, illustrate the dangers. All stakeholders must therefore confront the dangerous political belief that winning an election is more important than preserving human life.

Many political analysts believe INEC remains one of the most important institutions capable of preventing electoral violence through the organisation of free, fair, transparent and credible elections. Their argument is straightforward: when voters are confident that their votes will count and that declared results genuinely reflect their choices, the likelihood of post-election violence diminishes.

There is considerable merit in this position. A credible electoral process reduces suspicion, discourages confrontation and strengthens public confidence in democratic institutions. On the other hand, elections characterised by manipulation, irregularities, dubious result management and unexplained discrepancies create fertile ground for protests and instability. INEC must therefore understand that its responsibility goes beyond organising elections. It must establish public confidence in the integrity of the entire electoral process.

The experience of the 2023 general election remains instructive. Controversies surrounding electronic transmission and uploading of results, particularly the performance of the INEC Result Viewing Portal, generated widespread dissatisfaction and weakened confidence in the process.

Whatever explanations were subsequently offered by INEC, the controversy demonstrated that technological innovations must be supported by reliable implementation, clear communication and institutional accountability.

For 2027, INEC cannot afford another credibility crisis. Its preparations must be guided by transparency, consistency and strict adherence to the Electoral Act and the Constitution.

The commission must ensure credible voter registration, equal treatment of political parties, timely distribution of electoral materials, proper accreditation of voters and accurate recording, transmission and collation of results in accordance with the law. It must also communicate effectively with Nigerians.

However, many INEC officials have consistently argued that it would be misleading to suggest that credible elections conducted by the commission alone can eliminate political violence.

Although INEC has the constitutional responsibility to organise and supervise elections, it does not possess the mandate to maintain public order, arrest armed political thugs or prosecute individuals threatening political opponents. These responsibilities fall primarily within the jurisdiction of security agencies and other relevant institutions.

The Nigeria Police Force, Department of State Services, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps and other security organisations must therefore demonstrate professionalism, impartiality and preparedness before, during and after the elections. They must not wait until violence erupts before taking action. Intelligence gathering, early-warning mechanisms, identification of political flashpoints and prosecution of electoral offenders should begin well ahead of Election Day.

More importantly, security personnel must not become instruments of political intimidation. Nothing undermines public confidence more than the perception that law enforcement agencies are protecting one political interest while persecuting another.

The judiciary also has an important responsibility. Electoral disputes must be resolved promptly, impartially and in accordance with the law. Political actors should be encouraged to pursue legitimate grievances through established judicial institutions rather than mobilising supporters for confrontation. Credible judicial remedies can discourage political self-help, but the courts must also inspire public confidence through timely adjudication and consistent application of the law.

Perhaps the most neglected aspect of the debate is the responsibility of political parties and their candidates. It is convenient for political parties to condemn violence when their members become victims while remaining silent when their supporters are implicated. Such selective condemnation is hypocritical and dangerous. Every political party must publicly commit itself to peaceful campaigns and demonstrate that commitment through the conduct of its members.

The National Peace Accord, which all parties are signatories to must not be treated as a ceremonial document signed merely to satisfy public expectations. It must become a genuine moral commitment demonstrated through the actions of political parties and their candidates.

Former INEC Resident Electoral Commissioner, Mike Igini, has also warned that the credibility of the 2027 elections will depend on INEC, the judiciary, politicians and Nigerians themselves.

“The 2027 general elections will be more than a test. It will be a verdict on whether we, as a people, can learn from what has happened,” he stated.

Igini argued that INEC officials, judicial officers and politicians seeking public office would all be judged by their conduct, cautioning Nigerians against concentrating their attention exclusively on the electoral commission.

He also criticised the recruitment of unemployed youths as political enforcers, noting that they are often deployed to intimidate opponents, disrupt political gatherings and manipulate electoral processes, only to be abandoned after elections to face arrest, prosecution, injury or death.

Ultimately, Nigeria must confront the political values that make electoral victory appear more important than human life. Political parties must stop treating unemployed youths as disposable instruments of political warfare. Young Nigerians must also reject the temptation to exchange their democratic rights for money, political appointments or temporary material benefits.

President Tinubu’s warning should therefore be more than another political statement. It should translate into concrete action by the government, security agencies, INEC and political parties.

The 2027 general elections must not become a contest over who can intimidate, manipulate or eliminate opponents. It must be a contest of ideas, competence, character and public trust.

World.title: Sanwo-Olu Showers Flamingos with ₦10m Each, iPhone 18 Pro Max
World.content:
Duro Ikhazuagbe

More rewards have continued to pour in for Nigeria’s victorious Flamingos who won the FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup penultimate weekend in Rabat, Morocco.

Yesterday, Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu gifted the cadet World Cup winners ₦10 million each plus an iPhone 18 Pro Max for emerging the first African women’s teams win a FIFA Women’s World Cup

The reward is coming shortly after President Bola Tinubu had last week announced a ₦100 million donation to each of the players and the chief coach Akeem Busari. The other coaches were also gifted ₦50 million each. The gift was announced at the Presidency by the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu when playing host to the triumphant girls in Abuja.

Also, the Senate President, Senator Godswill Akpabio announced a donation of

₦100 million to the entire team shortly on arrival from Morocco.

Like the gift from the Presidency, Gov Sanwo-Olu also announced that the under aged players will not be able to access the cash until they reach adulthood at 18 years.

The gesture from the Lagos State Government further adds to the growing recognition and celebrations surrounding the Flamingos’ historic achievement, as the young champions continue to receive support and appreciation for bringing honour to Nigeria.

The rewards also underline the importance of recognising and encouraging young athletes whose achievements continue to inspire the next generation of Nigerian footballers.

The Flamingos’ historic World Cup victory remains a defining moment in Nigerian football, with the players continuing to enjoy recognition for their outstanding contribution to the country’s sporting success.

The Coach Busari’s wards defeated Japan 2-1 in the final to become the first African nation to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, marking a landmark achievement for Nigerian and African women’s football.

After a sluggish start in the group stage, losing to Poland, Flamingos regained their composure to beat beat Puerto Rico 2-0 and shocked defending champions North Korea 3-1 to reach the knockout stage. Flamingos Knocked out Mexico 2-1 in the Round of 16 before sending home Venezuela with 1-0 scoreline in the quarterfinal. Brazil also fell 3-1 before defeating Japan 2-1 in the epic final.

World.title: NOC Rewards Three Youth Olympic Gold Medalists with  $1,000 Each
World.content:
*The world champions also expecting Presidential largesse after victories in Senegal

The Nigeria Olympic Committee (NOC) has announced the reward of $1,000 (one thousand dollars) to each of the three athletes that won gold medals for Nigeria at the recently concluded Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal.

President of the NOC, Engr. Habu Ahmed Gumel, announced the reward to the gold medalists at the reception for the Nigerian contingent on arrival at the Lagos airport at the weekend.

In announcing the award, the NOC President said there was no better way to appreciate the athletes than to put smiles on their faces to reciprocate their excellent performance at the Games.

Speaking further at the reception, Engr. Gumel stressed that the athletes sacrificed all they had to put smiles on the faces of Nigerians by registering the country’s name on the world map.

“They put smiles on our faces as our worthy ambassadors of this great country.

“You went to the Games, saw and conquered to register Nigeria’s name on the world map and put smiles on our faces. This reward is just to reciprocate your excellent performance as our good ambassadors of this great country,”observed the elated NOC president.

Secretary General of the Nigeria Olympic Committee, Hon. Babatunde Popoola, also congratulated the young athletes for their excellent performances at the first ever Olympic Games on African soil.

Meanwhile, sources close to the team, hinted yesterday that the young athletes are also expecting to receive similar compensation as other sports that have also done the country proud in continental and global sports fiestas.

Super Falcons, Super Eagles and D’Tigresses have been rewarded by the Presidency for bringing honours to Nigeria.

World.title: Okoko Wins CIO Golf Classics with Record Score
World.content:
Nigeria’s 19-year-old golf sensation, Godwin Okoko, has stormed to a historic victory at the seventh CIO Golf Classic, posting a record-breaking 22-under-par total at the Python Golf Club in Port Harcourt, Rivers State.

The rising star delivered a commanding performance across the four-day championship, carding rounds of 67, 63, 65 and 71 for a remarkable 266 total, shattering the three-year-old course record by four strokes.

Okoko’s triumph represents another significant milestone in his rapidly advancing professional career and further underscores the potential of Nigerian professional golf talent on the continent.

“I have been looking forward to moments like this since my career started, and I am very delighted that things are coming together for me,” an elated Okoko said after his victory.

His exceptional performance was highlighted by a stunning nine-under-par 63 in the second round, which laid the foundation for his record-breaking achievement.

He subsequently maintained his advantage against a strong international field to claim one of the most prestigious titles on Nigeria’s professional golf calendar.

Chairman of Keeves Global Leasing, sponsors of the championship, Chief Ikenna Okafor, described the youngster’s achievement as impressive and a fitting climax to an event that continues to raise the standard of professional golf in Nigeria.

“Okoko’s record score puts the icing on the effort and growth this seventh CIO Classic has offered. He is an ambitious and talented player who is bold enough to carry the hopes and aspirations of Nigeria golf supporters and investors who are thinking of how to support golf in Nigeria,” Okafor said.

The victory also carries significant implications beyond the championship’s ₦100 million total prize purse, placing Okoko in pole position on the Safari Tour rankings and strengthening his prospects of qualifying for the 2027 Magical Kenya Open.

Ghana’s Vincent Torgah mounted a spirited challenge but finished two strokes behind the champion at 20-under par, while Zambia’s Sydney Wemba secured third place at 15-under par.

Nigeria’s Gift Willy and Uganda’s Ronald Rugumayo shared fourth place at 10-under par, while Samuel Emmanuel Odey, Sunday Olapade and Zimbabwe’s Samuel Njoroge tied for sixth at nine-under par.

Kenya’s Nuru Mollel and Nigeria’s Francis Epe completed the top ten, sharing ninth position at seven-under par.
