4. Gift Willy (Nigeria) – 10-under par

5. Ronald Rugumayo (Uganda) – 10-under par

6. Samuel Emmanuel Odey (Nigeria) – 9-under par

7. Sunday Olapade (Nigeria) – 9-under par

8. Samuel Njoroge (Zimbabwe) – 9-under par

9. Nuru Mollel (Kenya) – 7-under par

10. Francis Epe (Nigeria) – 7-under par

World.title: AS FAR Retain CAF Women’s Champions League Title
World.content:
Moroccan club AS FAR became the first team to retain the Women’s African Champions League title with a hard-fought 3-1 win over Mamelodi Sundowns.

Imane Touriss put the North Africans ahead in the 23rd minute in Ismaila, Egypt, when her early shot from outside the box caught out Sundowns goalkeeper Andile Dlamini.

But the South African side levelled two minutes later through a stunning effort from Refilwe Tholakele, who flashed a right-footed shot from a narrow angle across goal and inside the right-hand post.

Seventeen-year-old right-back Hiba Youssoufi restored the lead eight minutes before half-time when her shot from 12 yards was deflected in off Sundowns defender Asanda Hadebe.

And, as the Brazilians pushed forward in search of an equaliser, an unmarked Touriss made it 3-1 with 13 minutes remaining with a low first-time finish from the middle of the area after fine work down the right flank by Fatima Tagnaout.

Ronnel Donnelly had scored a hat-trick for Sundowns in their semi-final victory over Kawempe Muslim Ladies but was largely kept quiet by the AS FAR defence.

The closest the Brazilians came to an equaliser in the second half was when substitute Nthabiseng Majiya had an effort deflected wide, and they failed to test AS FAR goalkeeper Khadija Er-Rmichi after going two goals down.

AS FAR, who had surprisingly lost their opening game at the finals to Ugandan outfit Kawempe Muslim Ladies, are the first side to win the Women’s African Champions League title three times and also take home $600,000 (£449,000) in prize money.

World.title: White Tigers FC  Retain Spires 5-Aside Title for the Third Successive Year
World.content:
Lagos Island-based side White Tigers FC have emerged champions of the Spires 5-Aside Naija Street Soccer Tournament 2026.

The coach Emmanuel Olom tutored side who won the past two editions of the tournament in 2024 and 2025 defeated Oworonshoki’s Wasola football club 4-2 in Saturday’s final at the Stables sports ground in Surulere Lagos.

White Tigers received a prize money of N5 million as champions. Wasola FC pocketed the sum of N3 million as runner-up, while Agege’s ASDI Academy went home with N1 million after beating All Saints Football Club of Badagry 2-0 in the third place match.

Moses Henry emerged as the tournament Most Valuable Player and top

scorer with 17 goals. He went home with the sum of N500,000 for both honors.

Head Coach of White Tigers FC, Emmanuel Olom, won the coach of the tournament and received N250,000, while his goalkeeper Azeez Shittu won the best goalkeeper of the campaign He received the sum of N250,000 and a Golden Glove trophy.

As part of the closing ceremony, 52 laptops computers were presented free to selected participants of the Spires Sports Meet-tech programme, an initiative that trained over 200 youth in various tech skills such as Microsoft Word, Cybersecurity, Machine learning, Coding amongst others.

The initiator of the tournament, Dr. Bankole Allibay, believes that the tournament will only get better as they continue to build on the successes recorded to make the next edition an even greater success.

” This year’s event is very special because we expanded other initiatives around the tournament, we trained more participants in our Sports Meet-tech 2.0 programme, and we initiated the Spires Media Award to honour those who have supported us in the journey thus far. It was truly a successful campaign and I am so excited,” Allibay concluded with excitement.

World.title: Grassroots Sports Summit: Organisers Announce One-day Adjustment on Schedule
World.content:
The Main Organising Committee (MOC) of the National Grassroots Sports Development Summit 2026 has announced a slight adjustment to the dates of the much-anticipated national gathering, following unforeseen technical challenges and an emergency situation.

The summit, earlier scheduled to hold on Wednesday, November 18 and Thursday, November 19, 2026, will now take place on Thursday, November 19 and Friday, November 20, 2026, at the State House Banquet Hall, Presidential Villa, Abuja.

Announcing the development, the Chairman of the Main Organising Committee and Senior Special Assistant to the President on Grassroots Sports Development, Hon. Adeyinka Anthony Adeboye, explained that the one-day adjustment became necessary due to circumstances requiring urgent attention by the organisers.

He assured invited dignitaries, government officials, development partners, sports administrators, private-sector stakeholders and other participants that preparations for the summit remain firmly on course.

“The Main Organising Committee sincerely regrets any inconvenience this adjustment may cause our esteemed stakeholders and participants. The decision became necessary because of unforeseen technical challenges and an emergency situation.

“We deeply appreciate the understanding, patience and continued support of everyone who has committed to making this summit a success,” Adeboye stated.

The MOC Chairman emphasised that the change affects only the dates, as the venue, theme and overall objectives of the summit remain unchanged.

The summit, which has received the endorsement of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, is being organised to address critical issues confronting grassroots sports development in Nigeria, including talent discovery, school and community sports, infrastructure, sustainable financing and private-sector investment.

With the Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG) providing technical support, the two-day gathering is expected to generate practical recommendations towards creating a sustainable framework for grassroots sports development across the country.

Adeboye further appealed to all invited guests, speakers, panellists, partners and registered participants to update their schedules accordingly.

He reaffirmed the committee’s commitment to delivering a productive and impactful summit that will contribute meaningfully to the future of Nigerian sports.

“Members of the public interested in participating virtually can register at www.grassrootssportssummit.ng,” observes the convener of the summit.

The Main Organising Committee appreciates the understanding and cooperation of all stakeholders as preparations continue for the rescheduled summit.

World.title: APC-PCC: President Readies 5-year Security Plan as Military Eliminates 15,000 Terrorists
World.content:
*Cites recruitment of 28,000 soldiers, 50,000 policemen as key achievements

Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja

The federal government yesterday disclosed that its five-year security plan is now ready, setting out a new framework for strengthening the country’s defence architecture and tackling terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other security threats.

The announcement comes as the administration announced that military operations in the last three years had eliminated more than 15,000 Boko Haram terrorists and bandits that were terrorising parts of the country.



Similarly, the federal government stated over 130,000 Boko Haram fighters and their dependents had surrendered through Operation Safe Corridor, the government’s rehabilitation programme for repentant insurgents.

The figures and details of the plan were contained in a statement yesterday by the spokesperson of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), Dele Alake.



The five-year strategic defence operations plan is designed to align defence priorities, military capabilities, operational requirements and expenditure with Nigeria’s current and anticipated security challenges.

It is expected to provide a more coordinated approach to national defence, with greater emphasis on intelligence, technology, surveillance and prevention.



The Bola Tinubu administration said the surrender of the insurgents, alongside the reported casualties inflicted on armed groups, reflected its combination of sustained military operations and non-kinetic interventions.

“President Bola Tinubu is determined to end the 17-year scourge of insecurity ravaging parts of Nigeria through a comprehensive five-year strategic defence operations plan designed to strengthen the country’s security architecture, improve military effectiveness, and ensure a coordinated response to emerging threats.



“The plan provides a long-term framework for aligning defence priorities, operational requirements, capability development, and expenditure with Nigeria’s current and anticipated security challenges.

“The initiative is a major component of President Tinubu’s determination to reposition the nation’s security architecture toward a more coordinated, intelligence-led, technology-enabled, and prevention-oriented system capable of addressing terrorism, banditry, kidnapping, and other forms of criminality,” the statement added.



As part of efforts to increase the military’s operational capacity, Alake recalled that Tinubu had created four new army divisions and restructured existing formations. The changes, he said, are intended to expand the military’s coverage, decentralise operations and enable troops to respond more quickly to security threats.

The president, the statement explained, has also approved two additional army depots in Osogbo, Osun State, and Amasiri-Edda, Ebonyi State, to expand the training of new soldiers. Each facility can accommodate 6,000 recruits at a time, giving the two depots a combined capacity of 12,000.



According to Alake, the Osogbo depot currently has 5,210 recruits undergoing training, with the expansion expected to reduce training turnaround time and increase the number of soldiers available for deployment.

Tinubu, he emphasised, has separately approved the recruitment of 28,000 additional soldiers to reinforce the military’s presence on the ground and improve its operational effectiveness.



Besides, the APC PCC explained that the government is planning to recruit 50,000 additional police officers to strengthen internal security, expand policing capacity and improve the response to criminal activities.

“To further the manpower expansion drive, President Tinubu also approved recruiting an additional 28,000 soldiers to strengthen the military’s presence on the ground and enhance its operational effectiveness.



“The President also approved recruiting 50,000 additional police officers as part of broader efforts to reinforce internal security, improve policing capacity, and strengthen the country’s response to criminal activities.

“Beyond investments in equipment, technology and training, the administration is also investing in military accommodation and operational infrastructure to improve personnel welfare and effectiveness,” Alake stressed.



Beyond manpower, the administration cited investments in military accommodation and operational infrastructure as part of its efforts to improve personnel welfare and effectiveness.

Among the projects, it pointed out, is a 700-unit military barracks in Ikere-Ekiti, Ekiti State, designed to provide accommodation and supporting facilities for military personnel.



Under the five-year plan, defence investments are expected to be guided by clearly identified threats, operational requirements and national priorities. The government said the framework would strengthen combat readiness, address critical capability gaps, improve the use of available resources and minimise unnecessary expenditure and wastage.



Nigeria has battled the Boko Haram insurgency for over a decade, with the conflict causing widespread deaths and displacement, particularly in the North-east. Banditry and kidnapping have also expanded the security burden across several parts of the country.

World.title: Tragedy off Yzerfontein as 60-year-old paddler dies
World.content:
A 60-year-old Cape Town man has died after getting into difficulty while surf-skiing off the coast of Yzerfontein on Saturday, 14 November. Image: NSRI website

A 60-year-old Cape Town man has died after getting into difficulty while surf-skiing off the coast of Yzerfontein on Saturday, 14 November.

The National Sea Rescue Institute (NSRI) Yzerfontein crew was activated at approximately 16:20 after receiving multiple reports of a surf-skier in distress offshore of Schaap Eiland.

READ | NASA looks to NSRI for future astronaut rescue operations



One of the man’s fellow paddlers had reportedly made his way into Yzerfontein Harbour to raise the alarm after becoming concerned about his friend.

The group of eight surf-skiers had launched earlier from the Oceana Power Boat Club (OPBC) for an organised paddle to Yzerfontein.

Search launched for missing surf-skier

NSRI Yzerfontein launched its rescue craft, Janine, and began searching the area where the man was last seen.

Another member of the group, who was assisting with a shoreline search, spotted a surf-ski offshore and alerted the rescue team.

The NSRI rescue craft diverted to the location and found the surf-ski.

During the ongoing search, the missing man was located in the water north-west of Yzerfontein Harbour.



He was recovered onto the rescue craft, where rescuers immediately began cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR).

A local doctor and West Coast Medical Service were also activated to respond at Yzerfontein Harbour.

Man declared dead despite CPR efforts

Despite extensive efforts to resuscitate the man, the doctor sadly declared him deceased after all attempts had been exhausted.

The South African Police Service attended the scene, and the man’s body was handed over to police and the Government Health Forensic Pathology Service.

Police have opened an inquest docket.

The circumstances surrounding the incident are being investigated, including the possibility that the man suffered a medical condition while paddling.

Condolences to family and surf-skiing community

NSRI Yzerfontein station commander Junre Marais conveyed condolences to the man’s family, friends and the wider surf-skiing community.

The incident serves as a tragic reminder of the dangers that can arise during ocean activities, even when paddling as part of an organised group.

World.title: MTN makes fresh bid to buy Telkom
World.content:
MTN has revived its plans to acquire Telkom after abandoning its initial takeover bid in 2022. Images: X

Telecommunications giant MTN has launched a fresh bid to acquire Telkom, four years after abandoning its previous takeover attempt.

Both companies confirmed the negotiations in Stock Exchange News Service (SENS) announcements on Monday, 16 November.

In its cautionary announcement, MTN outlined plans to acquire Telkom’s entire issued share capital should negotiations succeed.



MTN EYES TELKOM TAKEOVER

MTN intends to fund the acquisition through cash, with the option for Telkom shareholders to receive MTN shares.

However, the companies have yet to finalise the terms or disclose the value of the proposed transaction.

In a separate announcement, Telkom confirmed that MTN had approached the company.

Both operators cautioned that discussions remained at an early stage and might not result in a deal.

They urged shareholders to exercise caution when trading their shares until further notice.

WHY MTN’S PREVIOUS BID FAILED

MTN first entered into takeover talks with Telkom in July 2022.



However, the mobile operator abandoned negotiations in October that year after Telkom failed to provide assurances over the exclusivity of the discussions.

In September 2025, MTN Group CEO Ralph Mupita dismissed speculation that the companies had resumed talks.

However, he maintained that South Africa’s telecommunications industry needed consolidation.

WHAT DOES THIS MEAN FOR CUSTOMERS?

A successful acquisition could change the competitive landscape of South Africa’s telecommunications industry.

Neither operator has announced changes to existing mobile contracts, data prices or customer services.

World.title: BUSINESS INSIGHTS: The accidental landlord dilemma
World.content:
Becoming a landlord by accident is easier than you think, but is renting out your property really worth it? Image: Unsplash

Picture this. You buy a flat in Durban, get transferred to Joburg two years later, meet someone in the city, move in with them, decide to put the Durban flat on the market and watch two sales fall through. Someone eventually says the obvious: why don’t you just rent it out?

Congratulations. You’re now a landlord.

Not because you spent months researching rental yields or deliberately building an investment property portfolio, but because your circumstances changed and offloading in a buyer’s market no longer made the most financial sense.



And while the above relocation in a “down” market scenario is more common than most people realise, there are plenty of ways to become an “accidental landlord.” Divorce, inheritance, moving in with a partner, or simply deciding to buy another home before you’ve managed to sell the first can all leave you with a property you no longer need, or want, to live in.

In many of these cases, renting the property out can absolutely make the most financial sense. But an attitude of “I’ll just get a tenant” is neither strategic nor sustainable.

Rent doesn’t equal automatic profit

Contrary to popular belief, if someone wants to rent your property for R20,000 a month, you are not making R20,000 a month.



Rates, levies, insurance, letting and management fees, maintenance and repairs all come off that figure. You also need to budget for the property sitting empty between tenants and the inevitable expense that arrives at the least convenient time.

And then there is tax. Rental income needs to be declared to South African Revenue Services (SARS), although certain expenses incurred in earning that income may be deductible.

My point isn’t that being a landlord isn’t profitable. It has been a hugely successful wealth-building strategy for many. But that profit isn’t a given. You need to calculate the actual return after costs rather than simply looking at the advertised rental price and convincing yourself the tenant is paying your bond.



You’ve also accidentally started a small business

What this requires in practice is something many first-time landlords underestimate. Once somebody is paying to live in your property, you have responsibilities to them – responsibilities that could cost you a lot in legal fees should you fail to meet them.

First and foremost, you need a proper, lawyer-vetted lease. Deposits must be handled correctly. Incoming and outgoing inspections matter. Maintenance requests cannot simply sit unanswered because you are busy.

And if a tenant stops paying, changing the locks and putting their belongings on the pavement is a fast way to rack up those aforementioned legal fees. Even entering your own property requires reasonable notice once somebody else is renting it.



While these are necessary warnings, my intention is not to scare away would-be landlords. I’m simply trying to kill the fantasy that rental income is passive from day one.

Distance changes the calculation

As I said at the start, many accidental landlords become landlords because of relocation – a factor that adds another layer of complexity.

A burst geyser is an irritation if you live ten minutes away from your rental property. But if you’re sitting in Joburg and it happens in Durban, it becomes a much bigger problem, especially if you’ve decided to save money by not using a local property management company.



A good management partner may come with a fee, but so does trying to coordinate contractors, inspections, late payments and tenant queries from another province or country.

Would you buy this property as an investment today?

This is probably the most useful question an accidental landlord can ask themselves. Forget for a moment that you already own it – if you viewed the property today, at its current market value, with its realistic rental income and running costs, would you choose to buy it as an investment?

If the answer is no, why choose to keep it, regardless of the state of the market?



Look at how much equity is tied up in the property, what return that equity is actually producing and what else you could do with the money if you sold. On the flip side, a low-maintenance property in an area with strong rental demand and reasonable running costs may be well worth keeping.

But keeping it because selling feels like a hassle is not the same thing as deciding it is a good investment. Becoming a landlord by accident is easy. Staying one should be a deliberate decision.

World.title: ‘Most of my criticism is in Arabic’: Rulani Mokwena feels under pressure despite winning
World.content:
Pyramids FC head coach Rulani Mokwena feels like he’s still under immense pressure despite enjoying an impressive start to the 2026/27 season with the Egyptian giants.

The former Mamelodi Sundowns coach has guided Pyramids to eight consecutive league victories, putting them at the top of the Egyptian Premier League standings with a four-point advantage over Al Ahly.

With his side enjoying such a strong run, Pyramids are firmly in the title conversation but Mokwena believes expectations remain high at a club of their stature.



Rulani Mokwena enjoying a good start with new club

Speaking to Radio Mars, the South African tactician admitted that he does not fully understand all the criticism directed at him because much of it is written in Arabic.

“The amount of pressure and criticism I face? Most of the criticism is written in Arabic, so I only understand a little of it.

“This is football, isn’t it? We are always under pressure when we work at big clubs. I faced immense pressure when I was at Wydad, and I am still facing great pressure now.

“At big clubs, there is always pressure, and the same applies to Pyramids FC; the pressure is present to the same extent, but it is certainly not like the pressure at Al Ahly FC,” Mokwena told Radio Mars.

Rulani Mokwena enjoying a strong run in Egypt

Mokwena’s latest spell comes after a challenging period since his departure from Sundowns in 2024.

The 39-year-old has coached several clubs, including Wydad Athletic Club, before taking charge of Pyramids FC.



His time in Morocco came with considerable expectations, but he is now enjoying a positive run in Egyptian football.

Eight consecutive league victories have put Pyramids in a strong position as they chase the Egyptian Premier League title.

Rulani Mokwena knows that maintaining that momentum will be crucial, particularly with Al Ahly among the clubs competing for domestic honours.

Can Rulani win the league?

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs news and injury update: Phili, Mayo, Abrahams
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs head into the Carling Knockout Cup semi-final against Mamelodi Sundowns amid uncertainty surrounding winger Faiz Abrahams.

The 21-year-old has reportedly gone AWOL after failing to report for duty ahead of the team’s mini-camp in Polokwane.

Abrahams was expected to join his teammates on Thursday as Amakhosi prepared for this weekend’s highly anticipated encounter against Masandawana.



Kaizer Chiefs star goes AWOL

Following reports of his absence, the winger’s father, Muneer, opened up about his son’s behaviour in an interview with KickOff.

He revealed that Abrahams has become increasingly withdrawn, often isolating himself from family and friends.

“He doesn’t talk to us or anyone for that matter. Even his close friends are left in the dark and don’t know what is going on with him. If he’s not visiting a friend who lives nearby, he’s locked up in his room the whole day.

“During his time in Israel, we noticed similar behaviour. He just went into his shell. He stopped calling us the way he normally would, but we can’t say exactly what caused it.

“As parents, it’s extremely worrying. We are clueless and don’t know what to do. At the same time, we don’t want to put too much pressure on him because we don’t know how it could affect him. But naturally we’re concerned,” Muneer told KickOff.

The father of the Kaizer Chiefs star also defended the upbringing of his son, insisting that he comes from a good family despite growing up in a challenging area of Cape Town.



“People will probably have their opinions, but the reality is that Faiz comes from a good home. My wife and I raised him with good morals and values.

“Yes, we live in a tough area in Cape Town, but that doesn’t mean he wasn’t brought up with respect, discipline and good standards. We also asked ‘Boere’ (Luke Baartman) but even he doesn’t know.”

Meanwhile, Kaizer Chiefs could receive a timely boost with Langelihle Phili and Khanyisa Mayo potentially returning from injury.

Phili last featured against Sundowns in August, while Mayo is yet to make an appearance for the Soweto giants.

Their possible returns would provide head coach Fernando Da Cruz with additional attacking options as Kaizer Chiefs look to overcome their Tshwane rivals and secure a place in the Carling Knockout Cup final.

With silverware on the line, the semi-final presents Da Cruz with a valuable opportunity to make a statement and move closer to delivering a trophy for Amakhosi.

Will Amakhosi beat Downs?

World.title: Fake Eskom technicians demand CASH for prepaid reconnections
World.content:
Residents in this metro allege that prepaid reconnections scammers are posing as Eskom staff. New-generation smart prepaid electricity meters are supposed to give households safety and control. But in Ekurhuleni, skelms are allegedly posing as staff, working on meters, sometimes disconnecting/altering them. They then return some while later to ask for a fee to reconnect.

PREPAID RECONNECTIONS SCAM

The South African reader, Maele, is an Ekurhuleni pensioner and left this comment on a story: “ My new smart prepaid meter was supplied in September. Since then I’ve had to buy tokens worth more than R2 500. My consumption is too high. I run a geyser only from 3am to 6am, a stove for about two hours in the late afternoon, and lights, a fridge and a kettle. I suspect the meters are made to run and consume the electricity very high,” she said.

After an ‘inspection’ from someone posing as a technician, the modus operandi is to then demand a fee to return consumption back to normal. In Ekurhuleni, the minimum charge for removing and reinstating a tampered connection is R5 566, doubling on a second offence and tripling on a third. Eskom warns of fines of up to R12 000.



ESKOM TARIFF INCREASES IN 2026

Smart meters have opened the door for skelms to pose as fake technicians and extort poor households. Image: File

The timing of such prepaid reconnections is cruel on the metro’s poor. Eskom’s direct tariffs rose 8.7% in April. And municipal increases averaging 9% followed in July. Despite qualifying, many households also don’t apply for free basic electricity, which the City provides to qualifying indigent households. They don’t do this because they may already be benefitting from illegal connections.

Tampering is a separate problem. It’s risky, as offenders face fines and disconnection, and it strains the grid. But Maele’s not alone. In Wattville, residents protested Eskom’s smart meter rollout last year, saying, “these meters are consuming too much electricity.” So, what can you do to check your meter and spot a potential prepaid reconnections scam?

DOES YOUR CONSUMPTION ADD UP?

Monitor your consumption and compare your spending before and after the new meter was installed.

Switch everything off at the DB board and see whether the meter still shows consumption.

Ask in writing for a meter accuracy test from the Eskom technician and keep a copy.

Photograph your meter and token receipts.

Check any staff’s ID. Don’t pay cash. Legitimate fees go on your municipal account only.

Buy tokens only from the City, Eskom or registered vendors.

Report suspected scams to the City and SAPS

If your meter seems to be running fast, consuming power, don’t tamper with it. Ask for a test from a city technician.

But what do you think? Do you suspect your meter is using too much energy? Have you see anyone fall for the prepaid reconnections scam? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: Nabeelah Shaikh: Tributes pour in for SA journalist
World.content:
Tributes have poured in for Nabeelah Shaikh, whose fearless reporting earned her several journalism accolades. Image: Facebook/Nabeelah Shaikh

eMedia Holdings, the South African National Editors’ Forum (SANEF) and political parties have paid tribute to award-winning eNCA Investigative Reporter Nabeelah Shaikh following her death on Saturday, 14 November.

Shaikh, 34, died following a short illness. She was seven months pregnant with her second child.

The journalist’s family laid her to rest alongside her unborn baby on Saturday evening.



eMEDIA MOURNS NABEELAH SHAIKH

In a statement on Sunday, eMedia Holdings described Shaikh as a “no-nonsense journalist who was never afraid to go anywhere or ask the toughest questions”.

Shaikh had recently joined the broadcaster’s newly launched investigations unit.

The company highlighted her achievements in journalism, the respect she earned among her peers and her devotion to her family.



“Nabeelah’s loss will be felt not only within the eMedia family but across the country she loved dearly,” the company said.

eMedia mourns the loss of eNCA Investigative Reporter, Nabeelah Shaikh. pic.twitter.com/oS3XLgBeGG — eNCA (@eNCA) November 15, 2026

SANEF PAYS TRIBUTE

The South African National Editors’ Forum described Shaikh as a rising star in South African journalism.



Editor-in-chief Nisa Allie highlighted Shaikh’s coverage of the murders of women in Ekurhuleni, which reached a wide audience across digital platforms.

“She was agile, a new-age reporter, a unicorn in our space,” Allie said.

Allie added that Shaikh had looked forward to her new role and had already started planning her investigative stories.



Eyewitness News journalist and close friend Karinda Jagmohan remembered Shaikh for her generosity towards fellow reporters.

“She pulled everyone up the ladder with her,” Jagmohan said.

DA AND IFP MOURN SHAIKH’S DEATH

The Democratic Alliance (DA) also extended its condolences to Shaikh’s loved ones.



“Her contribution to journalism will always be remembered.

“Our heartfelt condolences go out to her family, friends and colleagues. May her soul rest in peace,” the party said.

🕊️ | The DA mourns the passing of eNCA journalist Nabeelah Shaikh. Her contribution to journalism will always be remembered. Our heartfelt condolences go out to her family, friends and colleagues. May her soul rest in peace. pic.twitter.com/fubJF7uvPx  November 15, 2026

Meanwhile, the Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) said Shaikh had inspired many young women who aspired to pursue careers in journalism.

“It is particularly heartbreaking that a life so full of promise, talent and potential has been cut short at such a young age,” IFP national spokesperson Mkhuleko Hlengwa said.

AWARD-WINNING JOURNALIST

Shaikh began her career at the Sunday Tribune in Durban in 2013.



She earned several accolades throughout her career, including recognition at the Vodacom Journalist of the Year Awards.

Shaikh leaves behind her husband, young daughter, parents and brothers.

World.title: Tshwane implements Level 2 water restrictions
World.content:
PRETORIA - The City of Tshwane has implemented Level 2 water restrictions, effective Monday, in a bid to curb high water consumption and ease pressure on Rand Water’s supply systems.

The restrictions follow a directive from the Gauteng Department of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs to all water services authorities.

The City says the measures will remain in place for 30 days, during which water consumption will be closely monitored.

Residents are warned that those who fail to comply with the restrictions face fines of R5,000.

Households that exceed their allocated water usage could also face additional charges for overconsumption.

Residents are urged to use water sparingly and adhere to the restrictions to help protect the province’s water supply.

World.title: Andreeva defeats Svitolina to win WTA Finals
World.content:
LOS ANGELES - Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva battled past Elina Svitolina in straight sets to win the season-ending WTA Finals crown on Sunday.

Andreeva powered to a 7-5, 6-3 victory in a hard-fought duel in Indian Wells to complete a superb week in California.

Reigning French Open champion Andreeva, 19, clinched the title without dropping a set in the tournament.

She is only the third teenager after Chris Evert and Maria Sharapova to win the WTA Finals on their debut.

"It feels amazing, of course I'm super-privileged to put my name in that group," said Andreeva.

The teenager thanked friends, family and support staff in a victory speech, before light-heartedly thanking herself for her success.

"I want to thank myself for always doing the hard work, for never quitting, for always believing in myself, for not taking the days off, for working every day, and for committing to what I have to do," said Andreeva, wearing a track-suit top with the slogan "I want to thank myself."

A gruelling 1 hr 48 min duel saw Andreeva secure a break in the opening game of the first set before holding for a 2-0 lead.

Ukrainian veteran Svitolina broke back in the fourth game, conjuring a sublime angled volley to level at 2-2.

Svitolina was soon back under pressure though, conceding another break to go 4-3 down before Andreeva held for a 5-3 lead.

There was more drama to follow when Andreeva served for the first set at 5-4 up.

She opened with back-to-back double faults to go 0-30 down, and then yanked a wild forehand wide to give Svitolina two break points at 15-40.

World.title: 'Godfather' of Mexico's modern drug trade Felix Gallardo dies at 80
World.content:
MEXICO CITY - Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, the architect of modern Mexican drug trafficking known as "the boss of bosses," who transformed the global cocaine trade and orchestrated the murder of a US agent, died Sunday at age 80, officials said.

The notorious drug kingpin, a former police officer who played a key role in forging alliances with Colombian traffickers, died in a hospital where he had been transferred from prison two days earlier.

"After remaining under observation with a guarded prognosis, he died on November 15 at the medical facility" after "he suffered multiple organ failure," according to a statement from the security ministry of the state of Jalisco, where he was being held.

Felix Gallardo's health had deteriorated markedly in recent years, with conditions including high blood pressure, diabetes and deafness.

In 2022, then-president Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador said he was "in very poor health." A judge granted him house arrest, but technical problems with electronic ankle monitoring prevented his transfer.

One of the founders of the Guadalajara cartel, from which the Sinaloa cartel would later emerge, Felix Gallardo had been incarcerated since 1989 and was serving a 40-year sentence.

He was convicted for the 1985 murder of an undercover US Drug Enforcement Agency officer, Enrique "Kiki" Camarena Salazar, which outraged the United States.

- Rise of the cartels -

Felix Gallardo was a native of Sinaloa state, where he was born on January 8, 1946, according to public records.

His involvement in crime went virtually hand in hand with his career in the state and federal police.

World.title: US Treasury chief wants answers soon from Nvidia
World.content:
WASHINGTON - US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called on Nvidia Sunday to explain whether it knowingly allowed its most advanced AI chips to reach China, saying this was more important than ex-CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged spy for Beijing.

Speaking on "Fox News Sunday Morning Futures" three days after Huang resigned, Bessent said he wants to know if Nvidia used shell companies to dodge US restrictions and sell its most powerful chips to China.

But late Sunday, tech tycoon Elon Musk and several other Silicon Valley leaders added their signatures to more than 165,000 others on an open letter demanding that the company's board members "bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts."

The United States forbids sales to China of the most cutting-edge AI chips, hoping to stay ahead of the Chinese in the race to dominate artificial intelligence.

In late 2025, President Donald Trump did authorise sales of Nvidia chips called H200s to the Chinese -- but not the most advanced chips used to run AI models reshaping modern society.

"Nothing above the H200s can be sold to the Chinese," Bessent said.

"What's more important here," he said, "is to examine whether Nvidia had a culture of compliance around the US export restrictions."

Bessent alluded to companies linked to Megaspeed, the Singapore-based data centre company that Huang's alleged lover Alice Huang once worked for.

"And who knew? Because I mean, these shell companies were obvious. They were being investigated. And did Nvidia use them as a workaround to sell chips to the Chinese?"

Of Alice Huang he said: "It doesn't matter to me whether she's a spy or not. You know, Jensen's foibles are his foibles."

- Investigation deadline -

Bessent said he wanted answers from Nvidia and its internal investigation of Jensen Huang's behavior within the next 10 days, and said the company needed "a dramatic shake-up," which should include looking "outside" for its next chief.

World.title: Pope Leo wraps up South America homecoming that tested health
World.content:
LIMA - Pope Leo XIV wraps up a 12-day homecoming tour of South America on Monday that eased doubts about his recovery from cancer surgery and highlighted the social justice priorities shaping his early papacy.

The 71-year-old pontiff travelled through Uruguay, Argentina and Peru -- a demanding itinerary many doubted he could complete a month after lung surgery.

From the high Andes to the sweltering Amazon, US-born Leo crisscrossed a continent where he spent nearly two decades as a missionary, and picked up Peruvian citizenship along the way.

Visiting care homes and prisons, the leader of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics delivered hard-hitting speeches and browbeat political leaders like Argentina's Javier Milei, insisting growth must benefit all, and speaking in defense of the poor, the elderly and disabled people.

Pulling it off has proved Leo's "incredible strength and determination," which people had largely "underestimated," said Vatican expert Elise Ann Allen, who has written a biography of Chicago-born Leo.

"We're also seeing the missionary pope in a way that we've never seen him before," she told AFP.

In wealthy, secular Uruguay, the pontiff ventured into the most dangerous neighbourhood in the capital Montevideo to highlight the deaths of children caught up in drug violence.

He urged greater solidarity with the lonely and suffering, describing the country's high suicide rates as "painful" and demanding greater respect for women, a theme that would return throughout his trip.

World.title: 14-year-old arrested for allegedly killing domestic worker on Barberton farm
World.content:
MBOMBELA - A 14-year-old boy has been arrested on a charge of murder after he allegedly shot and killed a 51-year-old domestic worker at a farm in Barberton, Mpumalanga on Saturday.

The teenager was later released into the custody of his parent in accordance with the Child Justice Act.

According to police, the firearm allegedly used in the incident was a shotgun belonging to the boy’s uncle.

It is alleged that the victim was asleep in an outside room when the teenager knocked on the door. When she opened it, he allegedly shot her. The woman was certified dead at the scene.

Police said the teenager reportedly informed them about the incident.

ALSO READ | Four killed in Bellville taxi rank shooting

“A murder case was opened; hence the suspect was arrested. However, in terms of the Child Justice Act, the minor was released into the custody of his parents,” police Mpumalanga police spokesperson Colonel Mavela Masondo said in a statement.

The firearm suspected to have been used in the shooting has been seized and will form part of the police investigation.

Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident, while the motive remains unknown at this stage.

Meanwhile, a separate case of negligent handling of a firearm has been opened against the suspect’s uncle, who is reportedly the owner of the shotgun.

World.title: 8 men shot dead inside vehicle in Sweetwaters, KZN
World.content:
PIETERAMARITZBURG – KwaZulu-Natal police have launched a manhunt after eight men were found shot dead inside a vehicle in Sweetwaters, outside Pietermaritzburg, on Sunday night.

According to police, the men were allegedly shot and killed inside a vehicle along a road in the Mabane Section.

Police responded to reports of a shooting and, upon arriving at the scene, found a white seven-seater vehicle riddled with bullet holes. Inside, they found eight men with multiple gunshot wounds.

READ | Four killed in Bellville taxi rank shooting

All eight were certified dead at the scene.

The circumstances surrounding the shooting remain unclear. The deceased had not yet been identified at the time of reporting.

Police said further details would be provided once the scene had been processed.

World.title: UN to debate rules for 'killer robots'
World.content:
GENEVA - Countries will debate whether to start talks on binding rules for autonomous weapons systems, dubbed "killer robots" by critics, at the UN from Monday, as concerns grow about their increasing use on the battlefield.

Warfare is undergoing a radical transformation as armies seek to capitalise on the boom in artificial intelligence to boost their fighting abilities by identifying and striking targets more quickly and more accurately.

But a chorus of voices, from campaigners to UN chief Antonio Guterres and Pope Leo XIV, have warned against the dangers of handing the power of life and death to fully autonomous machines.

"The need to regulate autonomous weapons has taken on new urgency" with developments in artificial intelligence, said Laurent Gisel, head of the Weapons and Conduct of Hostilities Unit at the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC).

Russia has reportedly used fully autonomous drones to deadly effect in its war on Ukraine, while Ukraine's own defence industry is pushing to develop autonomous "drone swarms".

Human Rights Watch said the meeting in Geneva this week of the UN's Review Conference of the Convention on Conventional Weapons (CCW) would leave civilians "dangerously exposed" if it failed to act decisively.

The meeting will bring together 128 countries to decide whether to open negotiations on legally binding rules.

- 'Carefully cultivated ambiguity' -

But while many states are in favour of tighter rules, as with other advanced military capabilities such as nuclear weapons, countries that have acquired the technology are reluctant to have their hands tied.

At the UN General Assembly last month, 163 states adopted a resolution calling for negotiations on rules governing autonomous weapons.

Five countries voted against, the United States, Russia, Belarus, Israel and North Korea, which last week boasted of a new AI-enabled torpedo system.

Nine abstained, including Iran, Saudi Arabia and China, which has maintained a "carefully cultivated ambiguity", said Laure de Roucy-Rochegonde of the French Institute of International Relations.

Washington has proposed a five‑year process to develop a non‑binding instrument, while NGOs and the ICRC are advocating for a one‑year timeline.

In 2023, Guterres and ICRC President Mirjana Spoljaric Egger called on states to ban autonomous weapons before 2026.

The ICRC is calling for a ban on two categories of autonomous weapons: so‑called "unpredictable autonomous weapons" and those designed or used to directly target humans.

Given the opposition from leading international powers, observers say it looks unlikely agreement will be reached this week to start talks on binding rules.

By Agnès Pedrero

World.title: Thwake Dam project reaches 94pc completion
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Thwake Multipurpose Dam, which is 94.2 per cent complete, with the government targeting April 2027 for water impoundment.[File,Standard]

Thwake Dam is 94.2 per cent complete, with the government targeting April 2027 for water impoundment as residents seek a review of alleged construction-related damage claims.

Principal Secretary for Water and Sanitation Julius Korir told the National Assembly Departmental Committee on Blue Economy, Water and Irrigation that construction had reached 94.2 per cent.

The dam is being built at the confluence of the Athi and Thwake rivers along the Makueni-Kitui border. It is designed to provide water for domestic use, irrigation and electricity generation.

Martin Kimeu, a resident of Wote, said the project would improve access to water for farming in the region.

“Ukambani is fertile. Water has been the biggest impediment to the realization of our agricultural potential. Thwake Dam water is the clear solution to this,” he said.

Kimeu also defended the compensation process, saying he had followed the project since its inception and believed the exercise had been conducted properly.

Jacob Mwanzia, a resident of Madangi Village, said households in his area had been assessed and compensated. He argued that outstanding complaints should be addressed without delaying the project.

Mariam Mwikali, another resident, said assessments had been conducted on affected properties and residents given an opportunity to raise concerns.

However, some households have complained that construction-related blasting damaged their homes. Residents have reported cracks in walls, windows and foundations as well as dust, noise and ground vibrations.

In August 2026, residents from villages in Mavindini Ward, organised under the Thwake Dam Blasting-Affected Community Committee, sought an independent review by the African Development Bank (AfDB).

The residents alleged that some properties had been left out of assessments and compensation. They also sought access to assessment reports, photographs, measurements, valuation records and estimates for repairs or reconstruction.

A project official said the dam's safety department invited competitive bids for an independent assessment of properties potentially affected by blasting. Agile Consulting was selected to conduct the exercise.

The official said the consultant assessed 330 households within a two-kilometre radius of the construction site and submitted its report to the project implementation team. A large proportion of those assessed were satisfied with the exercise, the official added, without giving a breakdown.

Ben Mwongela, a director at Agile Consulting, said the assessment reviewed blasting records, vibration data and compliance with regulatory standards.

The exercise also involved documenting households, classifying structural defects and preparing bills of quantities and cost estimates for repairs or reconstruction, he said.

The AfDB conducted a field mission to the project between September 21 and 25, with its report published on October 21, 2026.

The bank's team, led by project task manager Nancy Ogal, met residents whose homes had been affected by blasting and identified outstanding health, safety, environmental and social issues, including homeowner grievances.

The bank called for timely compensation and continued monitoring of the project's environmental and social performance.

During a stakeholder engagement visit to Mavindini in October, Korir said the government had secured additional funding after the project experienced cash-flow constraints.

“When we ran short of cash, we engaged with our development partners, and they allocated additional funding, and this money will now go towards total completion of the project,” he said.

In June 2026, the AfDB approved additional financing of €68.39 million to support completion of the first phase, alongside funding from the Kenyan government.

The bank said the financing would support engineering refinements and safety works, including strengthening foundations, raising the dam and constructing two additional saddle dams.

The project has four phases. The first involves construction of the dam, while the subsequent phases cover hydropower generation, water supply and sanitation infrastructure, and irrigation.

The dam is approximately 80.5 metres high and has a planned storage capacity of 688 million cubic metres.

Once the water supply component is operational, the project is expected to provide 150,000 cubic metres of treated water daily to an estimated 1.3 million people in Makueni and Kitui counties and Konza Technopolis in Machakos County.

The irrigation scheme is designed to cover 40,000 hectares, equivalent to about 100,000 acres of agricultural land.

The project is also designed to generate 20 megawatts of hydropower.

The water supply, irrigation and hydropower components require infrastructure beyond the dam structure, including treatment and distribution networks and power generation facilities.

World.title: Love under watch: How technology is fuelling intimate partner abuse
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Your enemy is closer than you think. For many Kenyan women, the person who demands a phone password, reads private messages and tracks their movements through a screen is not a faceless troll. He is the man they live with, or the one they used to.

That is the uncomfortable picture painted by the recently released 2025–2626 Kenya Mini Demographic and Health Survey (KMDHS), which measured technology-facilitated gender-based violence, abuse committed, assisted, aggravated or amplified through digital tools.

The most common form of abuse is online control, reported by 19 per cent of women, followed by hacking at 5 per cent and online sexual harassment or cyber sexual abuse at 3 per cent. Most of it happens on platforms women use every day.

“Sixty-seven per cent of women who experienced digital gender violence say it happened on social media, with Facebook cited by 59 per cent. Messaging apps follow at 47 per cent, with WhatsApp at 26 per cent. Among girls aged 15–19, 77 per cent reported abuse on social media.”

The report shows how widespread the abuse is. “Twenty-six percent of women age 15–49 have ever experienced technology-facilitated violence from any perpetrator,” the report says, and 21 per cent experienced it often or sometimes in the 12 months before the survey. Among women who have ever had a husband or intimate partner, 27 per cent have experienced it at the hands of a current, most recent or previous partner.

The burden is not spread evenly, the report states that Nairobi City records the highest lifetime experience from any perpetrator at 33 per cent, followed by Murang’a and Baringo at 32 per cent each.

“For abuse by an intimate partner, Homa Bay 36 per cent and Baringo 35 per cent lead, while in the 12 months before the survey Trans Nzoia topped the list at 31 per cent. At the other end, Mandera and Wajir report just 3 per cent, a figure that may say as much about silence as about safety,” the report says

The picture is similar among young people. A 2024 rapid study by the Collaborative Centre for Gender and Development, working with the UNFPA and Women Economic Empowerment, found that nearly 90 per cent of young adults enrolled in three Nairobi tertiary institutions had witnessed TFGBV, and 39 per cent had experienced it personally.

Among women who have ever had a husband or intimate partner, 27 per cent have experienced gender violence committed by a current, most recent or previous partner, and 22 per cent did so in the past year. When women were asked who was responsible, the answer was blunt. Current husbands or intimate partners accounted for 61 per cent of perpetrators, former partners for 22 per cent and strangers for just 13 per cent.

Women who have never been married or had a partner face a different threat. For them, the most common perpetrators are strangers at 45 per cent, online attackers at 23 per cent and friends or acquaintances at 20 per cent.

Warning signs

Control is the common thread. The report describes such behaviours by a male partner as “important early warning signs that may escalate into violence within a relationship.”

Sixty-one per cent of ever-partnered women say their current or most recent partner has shown at least one controlling behaviour, and 27 per cent report three or more. Half say he has been jealous or angry when they spoke to other men, and 36 per cent say he insists on knowing where they are at all times. Others describe partners who demand passwords or read messages without consent.

Age and marital status matter. Technology-based gender violence is lowest among girls aged 15–19 at 10 per cent and highest among women aged 20–24 at 37 per cent. Forty-one per cent of divorced, separated or widowed women have experienced it, compared with 27 per cent of married women and 19 per cent of the never married.

Yet the digital rights advocate Cherie Oyier, a programmes officer at the Kenya ICT Action Network (KICTANet), says the low figures in some places should not be read as safety. Much of the abuse happens where nobody can see it.

“Closed applications, meaning like WhatsApp, those are the ones that most people, intimate partners will usually use,” she says. “Even as you are scrolling the internet to look for these instances, we may not be able to catch it. But it does not mean that it is not happening or that it is at a lower level.”

Culture also silences women. “Most women are told just endure, this is what marriage is about,” Oyier says. “Sometimes they don’t know, it’s so overt, like it doesn’t come out clearly that this is abuse. So most of the times, it is not reported.”

Online, abuse has been turned into entertainment. “It has become banter,” she says. “Even the people who are experiencing it have trivialised it. It’s now ingrained to you, like this is something that happens, you should expect it actually. If you post a picture, one of the things that you are thinking about is what kind of comments am I going to get.”

A 2023 report by KICTANet found that more than 30 per cent of Kenyans have experienced some form of TFGBV, while 90 per cent have witnessed it. In 2025, KICTANet and Equality Now released survivor testimonies showing how deceptive online job offers, grooming and image-based abuse leave women exposed, and how many had never received counselling despite years of trauma.

The stakes are not only digital. The 2025 Report of the Technical Working Group on GBV Including Femicide, cited in the KMDHS, indicated that many cases of homicide of women and girls, and of sexual and physical harm directed towards them, “are preceded by online and offline harassment using digital tools.”

For survivors, the law offers little comfort. “The technology is moving at a very fast pace compared to the laws,” Oyier says. In an attempt to bolster the gaps, Kenya has many fragmented laws. “You’ll have the Data Protection Act, the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, the Children’s Act, that to some extent touch on online issues, but they don’t really cohesively cover the different instances of TFGBV.”

The police, she says, often do not know either. “Just imagine you’re a woman who is in a village, for example, a village in Siaya, and you encounter violence. For you to even understand which law apply is very stressful.”

“You’re going through psychological stress and depression, and you’re also supposed to figure out which law applies in your situation. It causes even more problems for victims and survivors.”

Flagging abusive language

Artificial intelligence is adding a new layer. Even so, Oyier cautions against writing it off. “We should not vilify AI completely,” she says. KICTANet has built a lexicon to help flag abusive language and runs a tracker for online gender-based violence. “One person cannot sit down and look at everything on social media. When AI is able to pull every post that has this word, a human content moderator is able to look through it with local context and see is this TFGBV or not.”

The KMDHS findings further show that exposure to TFGBV varies across age groups and digital platforms.

“Younger women are particularly exposed on social media, with 77 per cent of women aged 15–19 and 72 per cent of those aged 20–24 who experienced TFGBV reporting abuse on social media platforms, compared with 50 per cent of women aged 40–49.”

However, messaging applications tell a different story. Women aged 40–49 reported the highest exposure through these platforms at 54 per cent, compared with 30 per cent among teenagers aged 15–19.

Wealth also influences where women encounter online abuse. Exposure on social media increases from 45 per cent among women in the lowest wealth quintile to 74 per cent among those in the highest. Conversely, women in the lowest wealth quintile report greater exposure through messaging applications, at 62 per cent, compared with 39 per cent among those in the highest wealth quintile.

These differences suggest that TFGBV cuts across age and economic backgrounds, although the platforms through which women experience it vary.

World.title: Not so fast: Court slams brake on ARA over wealth forfeiture
World.content:
Felix Mecha Nyakundi could not provide a plausible explanation for how he amassed his wealth.

The Court of Appeal has ruled that the government cannot go after a person’s wealth without prior investigations to establish reasonable grounds for suspecting that the property constitutes proceeds of crime.

In a landmark judgment, Justices Patrick Kiage, Jamila Mohammed and Nduma Nderi said that although it does not require a person to be charged for a crime for the Asset Recovery Agency (ARA) to come knocking, it bears the responsibility to link the wealth or cash to a crime.

World.title: Back to sender: Aisha Jumwa returns to UDA
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto welcome former Cabinet Secretary Aisha Jumwa back to the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA) on November 12, 2026. [PCS]

Former Cabinet Secretary Aisha Jumwa has returned to President William Ruto’s United Democratic Alliance (UDA), ending a three-month political fallout with the ruling party that saw her join opposition outfit Wiper Patriotic Front and declare support for the one-term movement ahead of the 2027 General Election.

President Ruto welcomed Jumwa back into UDA at State House, Mombasa, on Thursday, November 12, 2026, in a political reunion that could reshape alignments in Kilifi County and the wider Coast region as parties position themselves for next year's elections.

The reunion comes barely three months after Jumwa dramatically announced her departure from UDA, accusing the party leadership of frustrating her political ambitions and failing to support her quest for the Kilifi gubernatorial seat.

On July 30, 2026, Jumwa announced her resignation during a press conference at her Kakuyuni home in Malindi, saying her attempts to have her grievances addressed by the President had repeatedly been unsuccessful.

Among her concerns was what she described as humiliation and rejection within the ruling party, including an alleged incident in which she was chased out of State House during a meeting between Ruto and Coast leaders.

She also accused sections of the ruling coalition of undermining her gubernatorial ambitions, claiming that the political arrangements being pursued in Kilifi were designed to deny her an opportunity to contest for the county's top seat.

President William Ruto recieve former Cabinet Secretary Aisha Jumwa back to the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA) on November 12, 2026. [PCS]

Jumwa, who was among UDA's founding members and one of Ruto's most vocal mobilisers at the Coast during the 2022 elections, said her loyalty to the people of Kilifi outweighed her allegiance to any political party.

"My loyalty to the people of Kilifi will always be greater than my loyalty to any political party. The voice of the people of Kilifi is louder than the voice of UDA," she declared during her exit announcement.

Her departure marked a significant political shift, particularly given her central role in mobilising support for Ruto in the Coast region.

In August, Jumwa turned to the opposition, where she was warmly received by Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka, who visited her at her Kakuyuni residence on August 14 alongside a delegation of party leaders, including Nyali MP Mohamed Ali, Kitui Senator Enoch Wambua and Wundanyi MP Danson Mwashako.

Kalonzo subsequently proposed Jumwa for the position of Wiper Deputy Party Leader, citing her political experience and influence, while also backing her ambition to contest the Kilifi governorship on a Wiper ticket.

Jumwa embraced the new political alliance, declaring support for the one-term movement and threatening to mobilise UDA supporters in Kilifi to deregister from the ruling party and join Wiper.

"We are the ones who registered UDA members in Kilifi, and we are embarking on a grassroots campaign to deregister them from UDA and join Wiper," she said at the time.

On September 8, she attended a meeting involving Wiper leaders and Coast gubernatorial aspirants, including Mohammed Ali and Danson Mwashako, as the party intensified efforts to expand its influence in the region.

However, the political alliance has now taken another turn, with Jumwa returning to the party she had accused of frustrating her ambitions.

Announcing her return, President Ruto welcomed the former Cabinet Secretary back into UDA, signalling renewed efforts to consolidate the ruling party's support in the Coast region.

"I look forward to working with her to advance the party’s transformation agenda at the Coast and across the country. We remain committed to uniting leaders and Kenyans around our shared vision of a united, inclusive and prosperous Kenya," the President said.

Her return comes as Ruto steps up political mobilisation in the Coast region ahead of the 2027 elections, with Kilifi emerging as an important battleground for competing political formations.

Jumwa's political journey has been characterised by shifting alliances. She previously served under the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM), representing Malindi in Parliament before becoming Kilifi's first Woman Representative between 2013 and 2017.

She later became one of Ruto's key political allies and served in his Cabinet.

World.title: Buxton estate tensions escalate after county officials attacked
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

At the heart of the dispute is a joint venture agreement between the county and the developer, which provides for the county to receive 10 per cent of all housing units. [Robert Menza, Standard]

A dispute over the multibillion-shilling Buxton Point housing project in Mombasa turned violent after county officials were allegedly attacked while enforcing a government order suspending construction over outstanding contractual obligations.

The confrontation came a day after County Executive Committee Member (CECM) for Lands, Housing, and Urban Development Mohamed Hussein ordered GulfCap Real Estate to halt all construction activities pending the resolution of disputes involving the county government and hundreds of former Buxton Estate residents.

The officials were reportedly pelted with stones as they attempted to serve the developer with an enforcement notice, with allegations that individuals linked to businessman Suleiman Shahbal were involved in the confrontation.

Hussein condemned the incident, saying attempts to intimidate government officers would not derail efforts to enforce the law and protect public interests.

"Let them bring goons, machetes, and stones if they want. I am not intimidated. I will execute my duties, and nobody will threaten me. The law must be followed, regardless of who you are or how much money you have," he said.

"We are here for the people of Mombasa, and we will ensure their rights are protected. Nobody is above the law," he added.

The November 10 enforcement notice, issued by County Director of Physical Planning Qassim Ali, directed GulfCap Real Estate to stop further development activities and obtain valid construction permits.

The notice, issued under Section 72(1) of the Physical and Land Use Planning Act, cited construction under a varied development plan without county approval and an ongoing dispute involving the developer, former tenants, and the county government.

The notice was reportedly received by the project's manager, Billy Okendo.

At the heart of the dispute is a joint venture agreement between the county and the developer, which provides for the county to receive 10 per cent of all housing units. [Robert Menza, Standard]

At the heart of the dispute is a joint venture agreement between the county government and the developer, which provides for the county to receive 10 per cent of all housing units and commercial spaces developed in the first and second phases.

An addendum to the agreement signed on January 15, 2020, outlines the county's entitlement, with the allocation expected to be transferred upon completion of the second phase.

In a letter dated April 30, 2025, the county demanded 10 per cent of the proposed 1,800 housing units, translating to 180 apartments. The demand was renewed in February 2026, with the county seeking details on how the allocation would be implemented.

However, in correspondence dated September 22, 2026, the Department of Lands, Urban Planning and Housing expressed concern over what it described as the developer's failure to provide substantive responses to previous demands.

The county also questioned whether GulfCap had provided performance security equivalent to 10 per cent of the total construction cost for each phase, as required under the agreement.

It further demanded proof of payment of the Project Development Fee, which is payable in instalments as the project progresses.

The county said it had also raised technical and planning concerns during a meeting with the developer on April 15, 2026, including the need to address outstanding issues and resubmit the masterplan application.

But the dispute goes beyond the county's financial and contractual entitlement, with more than 500 former residents accusing the developer of failing to honour promises made when they were displaced in 2019.

John Tsuma, Secretary-General of the Buxton Tenants Welfare Association, said former residents had waited for more than seven years to return to their homes despite assurances that they would be prioritised once construction was completed.

"We are very disappointed by what happened. We had a meeting with the CECM, and he made it clear that all construction activities should stop until the outstanding issues are resolved. We did not go there to fight anybody. We wanted the directive implemented," Tsuma said.

He accused the developer of benefiting from the project while former residents continued to struggle to secure the houses they were promised.

"The developer has benefited from A to Z. He was given land by the county government, and the houses were sold off-plan. Yet, when it comes to fulfilling the promises made to former residents, we are still being taken around in circles," he said.

Tsuma said residents were not demanding free houses but wanted the affordable tenant-purchase arrangement they were promised before leaving the estate.

"We are not asking for free houses. We want the tenant-purchase arrangement that was promised to us so that we can pay for the houses and return to our homes," he said.

He also questioned why the developer had allegedly failed to surrender the county government's 184 housing units under the joint venture arrangement.

Mohamed Mzee Rubea, chairman of the evicted Buxton residents, said the money paid to the families during their displacement was a relocation allowance and not compensation for their homes.

He said the former tenants were given Sh240,000, with assurances that they would rent alternative accommodation for 12 months and return once the houses were completed.

"What we received was relocation money, not compensation for our houses. We were told to take the money and rent houses for 12 months and that we would be the first people to return once construction was completed. But here we are, more than seven years later, still waiting," Rubea said.

He said the original agreement involved 522 former tenants who were promised priority access to houses under the redevelopment.

Rubea added that each household was also promised Sh60,000 as a deposit towards acquiring a house under the tenant-purchase scheme.

"We were promised Sh60,000 as a deposit for those who would take up the houses. The developer later said the money would only be given to those who actually acquired the units. We are still waiting, and many of us have not received anything," he said. At the heart of the dispute is a joint venture agreement between the county and the developer, which provides for the county to receive 10 per cent of all housing units. [Robert Menza, Standard]

He further claimed that the county had written to the developer in 2023, 2024, and 2025 seeking engagement over the outstanding commitments.

Mutua Mutia, another former resident, said the prolonged dispute had left families frustrated, especially after they were promised they would return within a year.

"I have lived in Buxton since I was a young boy. My firstborn child is now more than 30 years old, and the history of Buxton is one that pains us. We were evicted with the promise that we would return after one year, but today it is seven years and we are still struggling," Mutia said.

The former residents are also demanding the reconstruction of an Early Childhood Development (ECD) centre demolished to pave the way for the project, as well as the construction of a promised community social centre.

Hussein said the county had yet to receive either facility or its share of the housing project.

"The county has not received its 10 per cent share to date. There was an agreement that the demolished ECD centre would be reconstructed and handed over to the county, alongside a community social centre, but we have not received either," he said.

The first phase of Buxton Point delivered 584 housing units in 2023, while the second phase is expected to provide between 1,400 and 1,500 additional apartments. Completion had been scheduled for August 2027.

However, GulfCap Real Estate Chief Executive Officer Chris Ochieng defended the developer's position, saying 492 housing units would be handed over to buyers by December.

While urging the county to stop politicising the project, Ochieng warned that the ongoing controversy risks disrupting the project’s completion and affecting hundreds of workers who depend on it for their livelihoods.

He said the county government's 10 per cent share would be transferred upon completion of the project.

He also maintained that the developer had supported displaced residents by providing Sh240,000 for relocation and offering them preferential rates to purchase apartments.

Ochieng said the continued involvement of county officials in the dispute was unfortunate, particularly at a time when 492 homeowners are expecting to take possession of their houses in December.

He noted that the controversy was not only creating uncertainty among prospective homeowners but also threatening the livelihoods of hundreds of people employed directly and indirectly through the project.

“It is very unfortunate that Mombasa County officials are bringing politics into a national project. We have 492 homeowners who expect to take possession of their units by December. Beyond the homeowners, hundreds of people depend on this project for employment and their daily livelihoods,” said Ochieng.

He called on the county leadership to allow the project to proceed without unnecessary political interference, arguing that Mombasa has previously witnessed housing projects that stalled despite significant public interest.

World.title: Sakaja defends Sh43.7b drop in Nairobi County's pending bills before Senate
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja tells Senate that the Sh118 billion in pending bills was inherited from his predecessors. [File, Standard]

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja has told the Senate that pending bills in the city have been reduced from Sh118.79 billion to Sh75.07 billion through verification and payment.

Sakaja revealed that internal verification established that the Sh43.73 billion reduction was not achieved solely through payments but also involved legal assessments, court-ordered adjustments and the verification of disputed claims.

The governor, who appeared before the Senate County Public Accounts Committee at Parliament Buildings in Nairobi on Monday, said addressing the inherited debt required establishment of a verification committee to scrutinise the entire outstanding amount and establish the validity of the claims.

“The reduction of Nairobi County pending bills by Sh 43.73 billion was not achieved entirely through cash payments but also involved adjustments arising from legal assessments, suspended government-guaranteed loans, court-ordered reductions and disputed claims,” said Sakaja.

He told the Senate Committee chaired by Homa Bay Senator Moses Kajwang that the Sh118 billion in pending bills was inherited from his predecessors and that he had constituted a committee to undertake an internal verification of the entire amount before payments were done.

Sakaja explained that the verification established that the reduction was not solely through payments but also involved adjustments arising from legal assessments, suspended government-guaranteed loans, court decisions and disputed claims.

“I would like to inform Senators that my administration has provided a detailed schedule accounting for the Sh43.73 billion pending bills reduction through adjustments and reconciliations,” he said.

The governor said that of this amount Sh1.63 billion related to legal assessments, while Sh19.14 billion represented government-guaranteed loans whose servicing had been suspended due to a lack of supporting documentation and loan schedules.

Sakaja told Senators that Sh19.2 billion related to LAPFUND interest and penalties which the County said had been reduced following a court consent that brought the claim down to approximately Sh8.2 billion.

He said that they had provided a signed indemnity form, in accordance with County Treasury rules governing misplaced payment documents, alongside a financial memo confirming that the works had been undertaken and payment made.

“The audit further raised concerns over Sh16.04 million in receivables from non-exchange transactions, which lacked sufficient supporting documentation,” said Sakaja.

The governor told senators that beyond the verification of pending bills his administration had also strengthened the county’s legal department to reduce expenditure on external legal services and protect public resources.

Sakaja noted that through the reforms, Nairobi saved approximately Sh8.48 billion in legal costs over two financial years by expanding its in-house legal capacity, handling more litigation internally and negotiating reductions in legal fees claimed by private advocates.

According to the County Assembly’s Justice and Legal Affairs Committee, of the 174 court cases concluded during the period under review, 84 were handled by the County’s in-house legal team, with 47 determined in Nairobi’s favour, representing a 56 per cent success rate.

Kajwang, commended the County for reducing its pending bills but asked the Governor to provide additional documentation supporting the payments and processes undertaken to account for the Sh43.73 billion reductions.

“The Senate County Public Accounts Committee requires further clarification on the verification exercise and the adjustments made to the outstanding debt,” said Kajwang.

World.title: Gachagua dismisses opposition divisions as 'polygamous family' rivalry
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua during a church service in Isinya, Kajiado County on November 8, 2026. [Peterson Githaiga, Standard]

Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed claims of divisions within the Opposition, describing the disagreements among its leaders as normal sibling rivalry in a polygamous family, while insisting that the coalition remains united behind plans to field a single presidential candidate in the 2027 General Election.

Gachagua said the Opposition leaders were committed to working together to challenge President William Ruto, despite their differing opinions on the timing of selecting a joint presidential flagbearer and occasional disagreements among their political camps.

Speaking during a church service in Isinya, Kajiado County, the former Deputy President likened the political differences to children from the same father competing for attention but eventually uniting whenever an external threat emerges.

“The Opposition is united to a man, and we have agreed that we will have a single presidential candidate. Everybody is committed, and we talk on a daily basis. The only challenge is normal petty problems,” he said.

He added that the disagreements should not be interpreted as a breakdown of the coalition, maintaining that such differences were healthy and expected in a broad political alliance.

“Ile shida kidogo ni ya boma, watoto wengi wa baba mmoja. Watoto huko ndani, oh, baba anakupenda kuliko mimi. Mbona ulinunua kiatu kabla mimi? Si hiyo ni kawaida kwa polygamous family?” he posed.

Gachagua said the bigger threat to Opposition unity was not necessarily disagreements among its principals but the conduct of their supporters, social media influencers and political bloggers, whom he accused of fuelling unnecessary tensions through insults and online confrontations.

He cautioned Opposition leaders against allowing overzealous supporters to dictate their political relationships, warning that unchecked political attacks could eventually weaken the coalition and undermine its common objective.

“If there is anything to separate us, it is our supporters and social media bloggers. Wanawakisha moto hakuna, watu wangu na wa Matiang'i wanatukanana na sisi tunakula breakfast pamoja,” he said.

He further claimed that some political influencers associated with his DCP party had been recruited and allegedly paid by individuals opposed to him to attack his leadership and the party.

Gachagua urged coalition principals to exercise restraint and avoid reacting to every provocation from supporters, insisting that political leaders must remain focused on the bigger picture.
