World.title: 'Inappropriate to lecture India on democracy': Meloni ally hits back at Italian leader's BJP vote theft jibe
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Italian legislator Deborah Bergamini has criticised Giacomo Filibeck, secretary general of the Party of European Socialists (PES), over his âVote thieves, step down from your seatsâ remark targeting the

(BJP), saying foreign political representatives should not intervene in the domestic political debate of a friendly country.

In a post on X, Bergamini said India had its own political institutions and judiciary to address domestic political disputes. She also pointed to the special strategic partnership between Italy and India, arguing that it was inappropriate for European representatives to lecture the country on democracy.

Deborah Bergamini is a member and national deputy secretary of Forza Italia, a centre-right political party that is part of the governing coalition supporting Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni.



Her remarks came after Filibeck, while attending the Bharat Summit 2026 organised by the Congress in Hyderabad, accused the BJP-led government of undermining democracy and expressed support for Lok Sabha leader of opposition

and the Congress.

âAn Italian representative from the European Socialists and Democrats group, while attending a meeting organised by the Indian National

, attacked Prime Minister Modiâs BJP, declaring: âVote thieves, step down from your seats.â





This stems from the Indian oppositionâs criticism of the ruling majority regarding a long-overdue revision of electoral rollsâa process intended to remove duplicate entries, the names of deceased individuals, and those who have relocated,â Bergamini said.

The revision of electoral rolls has been a point of contention between the opposition and the BJP-led government.

âI believe that, in a democracy, everyone is free to put forward whatever arguments or accusations they see fitâprovided, of course, that they can substantiate them,â she added.

Bergamini invokes India-Italy strategic partnership

Bergamini said Italy and India shared a âspecial strategic partnershipâ, with cooperation across several sectors, and argued that foreign representatives should refrain from intervening in India's internal political discussions.

âFurthermore, in instances like this, it is inappropriate to intervene in the domestic political debate of a major friendly nationâa country with which our own has established a âspecial strategic partnership,â fostering deep cooperation across all sectors,â she said.

She also questioned the appropriateness of European representatives commenting on India's democratic processes, citing the scale of its electorate.

âMoreover, as Europeans, we find it inappropriate to lecture on democracy a nation that enables 970 million citizens to cast their votes. India possesses its own political institutions and judiciary; any conflicts or disputes should be addressed and resolved in accordance with the established rules of democracy,â Bergamini said.

Filibeck backs Rahul Gandhi, BJP accuses Congress of seeking foreign help

Filibeck had said that international gatherings were important to draw global attention to what he described as challenges facing Indian democracy.

âDemocracy is under attack in India, and we need to defend it, and the best way to defend it is to stand by Rahul Gandhi and the Indian Congress Party,â he told news agency ANI on the sidelines of the summit.

He also said the PES, the Congress and other political movements across the world were part of a progressive alliance committed to social justice, climate justice, human rights and democracy.

The remarks drew criticism from BJP leaders. BJP national spokesperson and national media co-in-charge Pradeep Bhandari accused the Congress MP of seeking foreign interference in India's domestic political affairs.

In a post on X, Bhandari alleged that Rahul was seeking âregime change with foreign helpâ and acting on behalf of foreign powers seeking instability in the country.

World.title: BJP MP Ajeet Gopchade urges PM Modi to ensure representation of divyang persons in Parliament
World.content:
Rajya Sabha MP Ajeet Gopchade has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi seeking an institutional mechanism for the representation of divyang persons in Parliament and state legislatures, citing examples of countries that have created such systems in their legislatures.

The Prime Ministerâs Office (PMO) has forwarded the letter to the ministry of home affairs and law ministry "for appropriate action".

Gopchade, a BJP MP from Maharashtra, wrote to the prime minister on Sept 28, 2026, seeking examination of the feasibility of appropriate mechanisms for greater representation of divyang persons in Parliament, "including consideration of suitable candidates for nomination to the Rajya Sabha, within the existing constitutional framework".



He suggested the creation of a transparent mechanism for "identifying persons with disabilities who have exceptional achievements, professional expertise, public-service experience and demonstrated leadership, so that their knowledge and lived experience can contribute to legislative and policy-making processes".

Appreciating Modi govt's emphasis on dignity, inclusion and empowerment of differently-abled persons, including usage of the terminology 'divyang', Gopchade requested that their "representation in democratic institutions may also merit further consideration".





"A Parliament that provides meaningful opportunities for capable persons with disabilities to participate in law-making can help bring diverse experiences and perspectives into the legislative process," he underlined, while highlighting examples of different countries that have created institutional mechanisms to facilitate the participation or representation of persons with disabilities in their legislatures.

The letter cited the reservation of five parliamentary seats in Uganda for persons with disabilities, which are filled through special electoral colleges. In Japan, this category of persons has been provided an opportunity to participate in parliamentary proceedings, including through a special session involving its Upper House.

In Zimbabwe, representation of differently-abled persons in the Senate is provided through a dedicated electoral mechanism.

In Egypt, political parties are required to include candidates with disabilities in their electoral lists; while in Liberia a special constituency mechanism provides for their representation. In Namibia, a person with a disability was appointed to Parliament in 2005.

Also recalling the noteworthy precedent in the Indian Parliament in Sadhan Chandra Gupta, a distinguished lawyer and politician who became the first visually-challenged MP, Gopchade noted: "His contribution demonstrates that disability need not be a barrier to distinguished legislative service".

Though he did not cite more examples, sources close to Gopchade said Jaipal Reddy, a former Congress MP and Union minister, has been the last notable person with disability who has contributed immensely to parliamentary proceedings.

Gopchade suggested that divyang persons be given representation in Parliament through the nominated MP route, as "many exceptionally capable divyang persons may face practical difficulties in participating in electoral politics and competing through conventional electoral processes".

"This makes it worthwhile to examine whether appropriate constitutional, statutory and institutional mechanisms can be developed to facilitate their greater participation in Parliament and other legislative bodies," he said.

The PMO, acknowledging Gopchade's letter, forwarded his suggestions to the ministry of law and justice and ministry of home affairs on October 29, 2026, "for appropriate action". While the matter relating to representation of persons in Parliament primarily pertains to the ministry of law and justice, the nomination of members to Rajya Sabha primarily pertains to the ministry of home affairs, as per the Govt of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961.

World.title: PM Modi to attend Asean, East Asia summits in Manila; what's on agenda
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister

will travel to Manila on Monday for a two-day visit to attend the 23rd India-Asean Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit. Maritime security, regional stability and expanding trade ties are expected to be key focus areas at the meetings.

Announcing his visit to Manila, PM Modi said in a post on X, "Will be in Manila, Philippines later today and tomorrow to attend the following programmes: 23rd Asean-India Summit. 21st East Asia Summit."

"India attaches immense importance to close friendship with Asean nations. Iâm also looking forward to interacting with the Indian community based in the Philippines," he added.

The visit comes as India seeks to strengthen its strategic engagement with Southeast Asia amid rapid geopolitical changes in the Indo-Pacific.



The Philippines, which is chairing the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) this year, is hosting both summits.

According to the ministry of external affairs (MEA), Prime Minister will attend a dinner hosted by Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr on November 16 before participating in the India-Asean Summit and the East Asia Summit process on November 17.

Bilateral meetings with other leaders are also being planned.





Speaking at a special briefing, MEA secretary (East) Rudrendra Tandon said India's engagement with Asean, both as a regional grouping and with individual member countries, was an important part of its Act East policy.

"We strongly believe that as an Indian Ocean country that abuts this very important Southeast Asian maritime zone, a strong strategic relationship with the Asean member states, as a collective as well as individually, is good for both of us," Tandon said.

Maritime security, regional stability in focus

Maritime cooperation is expected to feature prominently in the discussions, particularly as India and Asean share adjoining maritime zones and face common regional security challenges.

India and Asean marked 2026 as the Year of Maritime Cooperation, with several activities aimed at highlighting their shared maritime interests.

New Delhi believes closer strategic cooperation with Southeast Asian countries will help both sides deal with changing geopolitical developments and contribute to peace and stability across Asia.

The East Asia Summit, an Asean-led forum involving regional and major global powers, will provide another platform for leaders to discuss international security issues and matters of common concern.

This year's summit process is being held under the theme "navigating the future", with leaders expected to focus on strengthening cooperation and building resilience amid global uncertainties.

Trade ties and AITIGA review

Economic cooperation will also be an important part of India's engagement with Asean.

Bilateral trade between India and the regional bloc stands at around $122 billion, making Asean one of India's major trading partners.

India is also pushing for an early conclusion to the ongoing review of the India-Asean Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA), which New Delhi hopes will help address trade imbalances and improve market access.

Tandon said discussions on the review were continuing, while acknowledging that negotiations involving multiple countries take time.

BrahMos, South China Sea and Myanmar

Defence cooperation between India and Asean countries has also gained momentum in recent years.

The Philippines became India's first foreign customer for the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile in 2022, signing a $375-million deal for three shore-based anti-ship missile batteries.

Philippine defence secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr recently indicated that Manila was interested in acquiring additional systems and had submitted a wish list to India.

On the South China Sea, India has maintained that any Asean-China Code of Conduct should be consistent with international law, particularly the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).

The situation in Myanmar is another issue likely to feature in regional discussions. India has opposed diplomatic isolation of Myanmar, citing its geographical proximity, shared 1,643-km border and major connectivity projects, including the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project.

Myanmar is expected to be represented in Manila by a foreign ministry official.

Quad summit , possible PM Modi-Trump meeting

The Manila visit has also drawn attention amid discussions around a possible Quad leaders' summit involving India, the US, Japan and Australia.

US secretary of state Marco Rubio had indicated last month that the Quad summit was planned alongside the wider meetings in the Philippines. However, the MEA said it had no confirmed information on the meeting or a possible interaction between PM Modi and US President Donald Trump.

A meeting between PM Modi and Trump, if scheduled, would come amid ongoing India-US trade negotiations and following recent setbacks for the Republican Party in the US midterm elections.

The developments in Delhi and Mumbai come amid the arrest of his shooters for allegedly attempting to target high-profile figures, including

, which has prompted

The gang's targets include

Most of them already have Y and Y plus category security, but to bolster it further, these actors are being assigned an additional two to four commandos, alongside armed cops and personal security officers to ensure round-the-clock protection.



The letter to Sabarmati jail was sent by Delhi Police. Jail sources said the information has not been provided yet.

Focus on barring Lawrence from issuing orders from prison

The move to study Bishnoi's visitor logs stems from the revelation made during a separate but related investigation in which an individual, whose identity has not been disclosed, claimed he was taken to Sabarmati jail by Lawrence's arrested legal team member Deepak Khatri to allegedly settle an extortion demand.





A few individuals have also deposed before a magistrate in Delhi and recorded their statements regarding Khatri's alleged extortion racket being run on Lawrence's behalf, the sources said.

The investigators now aim to understand and dismantle the mechanism that allows his syndicate to issue orders from behind bars. Despite strict confinement restrictions, intelligence and police agencies suspect that physical visitors, alongside encrypted international conduits, could be used as couriers to relay instructions to his "shadow cabinet".

World.title: Those using Form 6 to re-enroll won't be prosecuted: EC to SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

has assured

that all attempts will be made to include every eligible citizen in the electoral rolls and no prosecution would be launched against people whose names were deleted from the post-SIR draft electoral rolls, for using Form 6 for restoration of their names in the voters' lists.

EC's stand, spelt out in an affidavit filed Saturday, is in sync with the Oct 26 assurance given by a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana while hearing petitions relating to alleged large-scale deletion of voters in Maharashtra and Delhi. The CJI-led bench had said, "No one will be prosecuted for filling Form 6 seeking re-entering of their names in voters' lists."

Petitioners had highlighted voters' apprehension that they might be prosecuted for giving a false declaration in Form 6, which is used for enrolling new voters, that they had never been registered as voters before.



Errors likely in weeding out dead, non-existent voters: EC

EC said, "No prosecution will be launched against anyone for filing Form 6 merely on the ground that the applicant/elector was previously enrolled in the electoral roll(s) prior to the SIR and their names did not appear in the draft electoral rolls during the SIR."

However, EC said those filling Form 6 to restore their names in the electoral rolls must ensure their names do not figure in the voters' lists in any other assembly or parliamentary constituency.





Assuring the court that efforts have been intensified to register every eligible citizen as a voter, EC said, "A mechanism has also been directed to be put in place to ensure that no elector is deprived of the opportunity to get his/her name included in the final electoral roll, subject to fulfilment of the prescribed eligibility conditions, while taking due care to avoid duplication in enrolment."

Accepting that there may have been errors in weeding out non-existent and dead voters from the electoral rolls through SIR, the commission said, "There are challenges on count of the large numbers involved, and also because the full data is being digitised.

There have been and will be problems that arise from time to time and the commission remains alive to the need to ensure that all those who are eligible to vote find their name in the voters' lists but equally, to ensure that all inconsistencies in these lists are addressed.

"

On complaints about large-scale deletion of voters in Delhi through SIR in the ASDD (absent, shifted, duplicate and dead) category, EC said those left out of the draft electoral rolls could submit fresh enumeration forms to electoral registration officers or assistant EROs at their current residential place.

"Electors who have not shifted may submit the signed enumeration form with the statement giving the reason for the earlier non-submission of the enumeration form. They can submit it to the ERO/AERO/BLO in person or through family members. Online submission option with e-sign will be available on ECINET," it said.

World.title: Six-month traffic disruption ahead as Ranigunj railway underpass work to begin in Hyderabad
World.content:
For motorists navigating the Ranigunj rail underpass during peak hours, the familiar sight is a long queue of vehicles inching towards the narrow passage from Tank Bund, with buses, trucks, cars and two-wheelers jostling for space. What should be a short passage into a frustrating bottleneck. The proposed widening promises relief, but commuters will have to negotiate six months of traffic diversions before the work is completed.

13 metres to 22 metres

Work on widening the Ranigunj Road Under Bridge (RuB) is expected to begin within a week. The existing carriageway, which is around 13 metres wide and currently accommodates two-way traffic, will be expanded to 22 metres to facilitate four-way movement. Officials expect the additional width to ease congestion and improve traffic flow along the busy stretch.

Traffic will be diverted through alternative routes. Under the proposed plan, vehicles travelling from MG Road towards Paradise and Ranigunj will be asked to take a left towards Distillery Road, pass through another road underbridge and proceed towards Karbala before joining MG Road.

Buses and trucks will be diverted from Old Ambedkar towards Liberty, Kavadiguda and Musheerabad, while smaller vehicles will be routed through Karbala and Ranigunj. To facilitate smoother movement at Karbala, the concerned agency has been asked to provide an additional three metres of road space to enable one-way traffic.

Officials said that if congestion builds up near Karbala Maidan, a portion of the traffic will be diverted through Minister Road and Rasoolpura. Flexi boards and signboards have been put up along the stretch to alert motorists about the upcoming work and diversions.

A. Chandra Shekar, who works at the Nampally court, commutes every day from Bolarum to reach work by 9 a.m., travelling through the stretch during the morning rush hour. He said the diversions would mean a longer commute for the next six months, but felt the eventual improvement would justify the inconvenience. “Although it will be a struggle to make the extra ride to dodge the stretch for six months, I speak for everyone when I say that this will bring much relief to a lot of commuters,” he said.

For Kalpana C, the congestion is not restricted to peak hours. She travels along Hussain Sagar Road from Himayatnagar towards her home in Rasoolpura and said the stretch frequently gets choked. “I take the Hussain Sagar Road to come home in Rasoolpura from Himayatnagar and it chokes up at any given time. Check the maps and it will be red constantly, especially the road towards Paradise from Tank Bund,” she said.

An official traffic advisory detailing the vehicle-wise diversion routes and restrictions will be issued by the Hyderabad Traffic Police before construction begins. Commuters will be advised to follow the notified routes and plan their journeys accordingly.

World.title: About 70 km of Greater Chennai Corporation roads to be handed over to Highways
World.content:
The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) is handing over key roads in Chennai, including Arcot Road, Usman Road, Nelson Manickam Road, Tondiarpet High Road, New Avadi Road, and Madhavaram Milk Colony Road, the State Highways Department.

Around 70 km of roads and portions of roads are on the list prepared by the corporation.

“They are being transferred since most of them are major bus route roads, which are contiguous with or connected to highways located within the city limit. It is for better administrative efficiency and maintenance. We have sent the proposal to the State government,” an official source in the GCC said.

The civic body will not get any road in exchange, as it did the last time it handed over some road stretches to the Highways.

The roads that are to be taken over are quite long, including Dr. MGR Salai-Arcot Road (6.4 km), Konnur High Road that is 5.4 km, New Avadi Road (5.2 km), and Tondiarpet High Road (4.8 km). The longest is the 7.21-km Kodambakkam-Sriperumbudur Road (Arcot Road).

Official sources in the Highways said works such as profile corrections of roads, restoration of road surfaces, and construction of storm-water drains would be carried out.

Maintenance contracts

“We plan to introduce five-year performance-based maintenance contracts (PBMC) for these roads. The maintenance will be done by the same contractor who does the profile correction,” a source said.

The PBMC, in its earlier avatar, was introduced ten years ago, and given to contractors other than those who laid the roads.

World.title: Low-pressure area forms over Bay of Bengal, likely to intensify into depression by November 15
World.content:
A low-pressure area has formed over the southeast Bay of Bengal and is likely to intensify into a depression by November 15, the IMD said on Friday (November 13, 2026).

The system formed at 5:30 a.m. under the influence of an upper-air cyclonic circulation over the central Andaman Sea and adjoining Andaman and Nicobar Islands, according to the latest weather update.

"The low-pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal is likely to move northwestwards and intensify into a depression by November 15," it said.

It is likely to move northwestwards and become a well-marked low-pressure area around November 14 before intensifying into a depression over the same region, IMD said.

Under its influence, squally weather with wind speeds of about 50 kmph, gusting up to 60 kmph, is likely over the Andaman Sea on November 13 and 14 and over the southeast Bay of Bengal from November 13 to 16.

Wind speeds are likely to increase up to 55 kmph, with gusts reaching 65 kmph, over the southwest Bay of Bengal from November 15 to 17 and over the central Bay of Bengal on November 16 and 17.

World.title: Ex-Bangladesh PM Hasina says if death is the price to pay for returning home, she is ready to face it
World.content:
Ousted Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, sentenced to capital punishment after she was toppled in 2024, told AFP on Monday (November 16, 2026) she would return home in December despite “the threat of death”.

Ms. Hasina fled to India in August 2024 after a student-led uprising ended her iron-fisted 15-year rule, and has remained in hiding ever since.

She was sentenced to death in absentia last year after a Bangladeshi court convicted her of crimes against humanity over a deadly crackdown on protesters.

“I am fully aware of the risks I face if I return,” she told AFP in an email interview.

“But I have made my decision, and no threat of death will keep me away from my own country.”

Her insistence on going back comes days after Bangladesh said she would face execution if she returned, adding that she has no further legal recourse after missing the deadline to appeal against her conviction.

The 79-year-old has repeatedly rejected the legitimacy of the trial.

Dhaka has sought her extradition from India, which says the request is under legal review.

Ms. Hasina said the stance was “contradictory”.

“For months, they have demanded my return. Yet now that I am taking practical steps to come home, they appear to be more interested in threatening me... than actually allowing it to happen,” she said.

“Frankly, I find these contradictory statements from the Bangladeshi authorities rather revealing.”

‘If death is the price’

Analysts suggest her promise to return is an attempt to remain politically relevant, retain the loyalty of supporters and keep alive a party that once dominated Bangladesh but whose activities are now banned.

She may also be counting on the possibility that the government would find it difficult to execute the daughter of Bangladesh’s founding leader, despite her death sentence.

Ms. Hasina denied that her Awami League party was involved in a recent spate of petrol bomb attacks in Bangladesh, as authorities have alleged.

She said she had no intention of seeking India’s assistance to arrange her return.

“Why would I ask another country to extradite me, when I have already decided to return voluntarily?” she said.

“Extradition is a matter between two sovereign states. India will make its own decisions according to its laws, policies and national interests,” she said.

Ms. Hasina also faces a string of other charges, including corruption allegations.

“More than 600 false cases have been filed against me,” she said.

Her lawyers had applied for a Bangladeshi passport and national identity card through the country’s high commission in New Delhi, she said.

“I am already making preparations to return to Bangladesh in December,” she said.

“I do not wish to die. I want to live and continue serving my country. But if death is the price I must pay for returning home, I am prepared to face it.”

World.title: NCW calls for inquiry, seeks report from DGP over Kallakurichi issue
World.content:
The National Commission for Women (NCW) has written to the Tamil Nadu Director-General of Police seeking a fair and impartial enquiry into the allegations that “C. Arul Vignesh, MLA from Kallakurichi, Tamil Nadu, sent obscene WhatsApp messages to J.E. Padmaja, District Collector, Kallakurichi.”

The NCW in a social media post said its chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar has written to the DGP, Tamil Nadu, seeking a “fair and impartial enquiry into the allegations, including examination of the representations reportedly made by the District Collector to senior officials and the action taken thereon.”

The Commission, which took suo motu cognisance of a media report, has called for the preservation and examination of relevant digital evidence and emphasised that the matter must be investigated without any political or external influence, irrespective of the position held by the person concerned, according to its social media post.

Also read: TVK faces criticism from Congress over law and order in Tamil Nadu, allegations against Kallakurichi MLA

“The Commission has sought a detailed Action Taken Report (ATR) within seven days. The dignity, safety and security of women public officials must be upheld without exception. No position or influence can place anyone above accountability for alleged harassment or misconduct,” it said.

World.title: Cyclone Akvan to cross Andhra coast between Nellore and Tuni by November 20 noon, says IMD
World.content:
Cyclone Akvan, expected to form over the Bay of Bengal on Monday evening, is very likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni by noon on November 20 as a very severe cyclonic storm, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said in its forecast on Monday (November 16, 2026). Winds at landfall may reach 120-130 kmph, gusting to 145 kmph.

That leaves about 500 km of coast in play, that is, nearly half of Andhra Pradesh’s 1,053-km shoreline. Machilipatnam sits roughly in the middle. Weather experts are monitoring the system as it may change its course again.

The Deep Depression over Southeast & adjoining Southwest Bay of Bengal moved north-northwestwards with the speed of 06 kmph during past 06 hours and lay centered at 0830 hours IST of today, the 16th November, 2026 over the same region, near Latitude 11.2°N and Longitude 86.4°E, about 630 km east-northeast of Trincomalee (Sri Lanka), 690 km west of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman & Nicobar Islands), 700 km east-southeast of Chennai (Tamil Nadu), 800 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 910 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha). It is very likely to continue to move north-northwestwards, intensify further into a Cyclonic Storm over the central parts of south & adjoining westcentral Bay of Bengal in the evening of today, the 16th November and into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal in the evening of 17th November, 2026. Thereafter, it is likely to intensify further and move west-northwestwards and cross Andhra Pradesh & Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni, by noon of 20th November, 2026 as a very severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 120-130 kmph gusting to 145 kmph. — India Meteorological Department (@Indiametdept) November 16, 2026

Initial forecasts had indicated that the system may move towards north coastal Andhra Pradesh. The latest IMD bulletin places its landfall in central and south coastal Andhra Pradesh.

Previously, very severe cyclonic storm Arnab made landfall near Narsapur, part of central Andhra Pradesh, and severe cyclonic storm Murasu near Ongole in south coastal Andhra Pradesh.

Krishna district, of which Machilipatnam is a part, has seen devastating cyclones in the past, including the infamous 1977 Diviseema cyclone. However, the district was spared much of the damage during Arnab and Murasu.

బంగాళాఖాతంలో తీవ్రవాయుగుండం ప్రస్తుతానికి చెన్నైకు700 కి.మీ., విశాఖపట్నంకు800 కి.మీ.,గోపాల్‌పూర్ కు 910కి.మీ దూరంలో కేంద్రీకృతమై ఉంది. సాయంత్రానికి తుపానుగా, రేపు తీవ్రతుపానుగా మారే అవకాశం ఉంది. #Akvan #Cyclone #AndhraPradesh #APSDMA #RTGS #WeatherUpdate #weather #WeatherUpdate https://t.co/itmX4gtEiV — Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (@APSDMA) November 16, 2026

Meanwhile, the depression over the southeast Bay of Bengal concentrated into a deep depression over the southeast and southwest Bay of Bengal in the early hours of Monday (November 16, 2026). The system moved north-northwestwards at 6 kmph during the past six hours, and at 8.30 a.m., it lay centred about 630 km east-northeast of Trincomalee in Sri Lanka, 690 km west of Sri Vijaya Puram in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, 700 km east-southeast of Chennai in Tamil Nadu, 800 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh and 910 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha.

The system is very likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm over the central parts of the south and west-central Bay of Bengal by Monday evening, and into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by Tuesday evening (November 17). It is then likely to intensify further and move west-northwestwards towards the coast.

Squally weather, with wind speeds touching 50-60 kmph, may begin along the coast from Monday. It is likely to increase gradually, becoming a gale as the system intensifies further. Sea conditions are very likely to be rough to very rough till November 17, after which they will worsen, the IMD said.

Pre-cyclone watch

The IMD has issued a pre-cyclone watch for the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts. Moving north-northwestward at 8 kmph, the system is projected to reach near the Andhra Pradesh coast around the night of November 19 as a very severe cyclonic storm.

“The current atmospheric steering points towards the coastal stretch between north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha. It is too early to predict the landfall point of the storm,” a meteorologist told The Hindu.

District administrations have been placed on high alert and have advised a complete suspension of offshore operations.

Fishermen told to stay ashore till November 20

Fishermen have been told not to venture into the sea until November 20. Fishermen’s leader Arjili Dasu said the recurring weather disruptions had crippled livelihoods during Karteeka Masam, when fish sales already slump.

Fisheries Joint Director L.B.S. Vardhan said Cyclone Arnab caused damage worth ₹307 lakh to fisheries in Visakhapatnam district: ₹123 lakh in partial damage and ₹184 lakh in full damage. No damage was recorded during Cyclone Murasu.

“We have submitted our assessment reports to the higher-ups. We are awaiting their decision regarding the compensation payment,” Mr. Vardhan told The Hindu on Monday.

World.title: One more dies in elephant attack in Hassan’s Belur taluk
World.content:
Less than 48 hours after a woman was killed in an elephant attack at Chowdanahalli in Belur taluk, another person died in a similar incident at Nagenahalli in the taluk on Monday (November 16, 2026).

Hafees Ur Rahman, aged around 60, was working at a coffee estate when he encountered an elephant, which trampled him to death. The body was shifted to Belur for post-mortem. The incident is expected to trigger another round of protests by local residents.

Following the death of Jayamma, 65, at Chowdahalli on Saturday (November 14) evening, people of Belur taluk staged a protest on Sunday (November 15) with the body. They blamed the Forest Department’s negligence for the series of deaths due to human-elephant conflict in the region.

The protest was called off only after the Forest Department assured them that action would be taken to drive away the wild elephants roaming in the area. However, within hours of the protest ending, another person died under similar circumstances.

World.title: European Union nations to unveil Rwanda deal for migrant return hub
World.content:
Five European Union countries including Germany and Denmark are set to announce Monday (November 16, 2026) a deal to establish a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda, the first such facility outside the bloc.

The group, also comprising Austria, Greece and the Netherlands, has been gunning to open a so-called "return-hub" despite rights groups' concerns, after the EU cleared the way with a recent toughening of migration rules.

The five have kept the location under wraps as they negotiated with potential hosts, but European diplomats and other people briefed on the talks have indicated Rwanda as the chosen country.

The African Great Lakes nation had confirmed in August it had begun "preliminary discussions" with several European States.

And it is sending a delegation to a migration conference in Vienna, where several sources said the agreement would be unveiled at a press conference on Monday (November 16, 2026).

"We shall see next week in Vienna," Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker told reporters Friday (November 13, 2026), when asked about the matter.

Suffering and harm

The announcement is to mark the culmination of an EU push to boost deportations launched in 2024, on the back of a souring of public opinion on migration.

Migrant arrivals have steadily declined over the past three years, as the bloc struck deals to stem departures with a host of countries in Africa and West Asia.

But migration has remained a hot-button issue, fuelling far-right electoral gains across the bloc.

Policymakers' focus has thus turned to improving the repatriation system, which currently sees less than 30% of people who are ordered to leave the bloc actually returned to their country of origin.

An EU reform granting authorities broader detention powers and allowing for the creation of return hubs was approved earlier this year.

Proponents say such centres, which would serve either as the final destination or as transfer centres for those expelled, could facilitate repatriations and act as a deterrent for would-be irregular migrants.

But critics have questioned their effectiveness, pointing to the hurdles faced by similar projects and likening them to "legal black holes" that could see migrants stranded in limbo with little oversight.

The choice of Rwanda has also caused concern, with Human Rights Watch pointing to its "well-established record of repression of dissent, arbitrary detention, ill-treatment in detention" and support for armed rebels in neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo.

"Paying Kigali to host a deportation program would not only cause suffering and harm to those deported, it would finance and provide political leverage to a Government responsible for serious human rights abuses at home and abroad," said the group's senior Africa researcher, Clementine de Montjoye.

Welcome centre

Rwanda had in 2022 reached a similar deal with Britain to take irregular migrants before their asylum claims were heard in the island nation. The accord was later scrapped by London.

It is among a number of African countries to have received migrants from the United States under a similar, contested U.S. immigration scheme championed by President Donald Trump.

Unlike the discarded British plan, the EU's scheme would see rejected asylum-seekers sent to the African nation.

U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said last week that Britain was following "with interest" the European push on return hubs, as it weighs its own "next steps" to curb illegal migration.

The five EU countries have expressed hope to have a centre up and running in 2027.

Diplomatic sources say the hub in Rwanda will be initially run as a pilot, hosting about 100 people, with each of the five nations possibly sending around 20 migrants.

It would not be a detention facility, with Kigali inclined to name it a "welcome centre" to underscore the possibility for some migrants to stay and work in the country, a source said.

And the United Nations' International Organization for Migration (IOM) could play an ancillary role.

"IOM has a long history of providing assistance to migrants in situations of transit, including in complex contexts," an IOM spokesperson said, adding the agency was in discussions with some EU countries "on plans for the establishment of return hubs or similar mechanisms".

World.title: Woman linked to Nagpur coaching class booked for explicit messages to minors
World.content:
A 24-year-old woman associated with the management of a coaching institute in Kamptee has been booked under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and the Information Technology (IT) Act for allegedly transmitting sexually explicit photographs and videos to minor students through WhatsApp.

According to the FIR, the alleged offences took place between July 14 and July 31, 2026. The case was registered late on Saturday at the Old Kamptee police station following a complaint from child protection authorities.

The accused has been booked under Section 12 of the POCSO Act, 2012, which prescribes punishment for sexual harassment of a child as defined under Section 11 of the Act, and Sections 67 and 67A of the IT Act, 2000, relating to the electronic transmission of obscene and sexually explicit material, respectively.

World.title: AAP, BJP trade barbs as Delhi women celebrate another Chhath amid Yamuna froth
World.content:
The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and the Bharatiya Janata (BJP) traded barbs over the weekend as thousands of people performed Chhath rituals in the Yamuna amid thick, white foam. The opposition AAP accused the Rekha Gupta-led Delhi government of failing to clean the river and of alleged publicity stunts. The BJP responded by citing celebrations at 1,400 ghats and claiming that more than half of the river had been cleaned in two years.

AAP and its leaders shared on social media visuals of women praying in the Yamuna amid dense froth. “Not AI, this is Yamuna on Chhath,” AAP said in the post. The party’s Delhi unit chief, Saurabh Bharadwaj, claimed thousands of fish had died due to the pollution in the river, and crores had been “wasted on false propaganda.

बीजेपी की 4 इंजन वाली सरकार के यमुना को साफ करने के तमाम दावों की आज पोल खुल गई! जहरीले झाग के बीच छठ व्रतियों को इस तरह मनाना पड़ा छठ का महापर्व। https://t.co/jvvlKTZ5No — AAP (@AamAadmiParty) November 15, 2026

The BJP rejected these claims. On Sunday, BJP’s Delhi unit posted visuals of the celebrations on X, saying they showed “the power of your one right vote”. It said that more than half the length of Yamuna, where Chhath was once banned, had been cleaned during the two years of BJP rule, and that the Chief Minister now celebrates the festival in the river. The BJP also claimed that it achieved in a year and a half what AAP and Congress could not in 27 years.

ये है आपके एक सही वोट की ताकत 🔥 जिस यमुना जी में छठ बैन था, अब उसी यमुना जी को मात्र 2 साल के अंदर आधे से ज़्यादा साफ़ करके उसी में छठ मनाती दिल्ली की सनातनी CM ❤️ https://t.co/xCUwhmhqvV — BJP Delhi (@BJP4Delhi) November 15, 2026

The Delhi Chief Minister prayed at the ghat in Sonia Vihar on November 15 (Sunday) and at Hathi Ghat on Monday. Gupta wrote on X on Monday, “..A divine morning filled with faith, devotion and blessings! Joined thousands of devotees at Hathi Ghat to offer Usha Arghya to the rising Surya Dev, praying for the happiness, health and prosperity of every Delhi family. Heartfelt gratitude to Team Delhi for making this Chhath Mahaparv truly Divya and Bhavya, with beautifully prepared ghats and thoughtful arrangements for every Chhathvrati…”

Beyond the claims

The official picture is more complicated than either party’s account. The Delhi Pollution Control Committee’s most recent published water-quality report covers samples taken on September 7, before the festival. At ISBT Bridge, the report recorded biochemical oxygen demand of 30 mg/L and dissolved oxygen of 2.9 mg/L, against a standard of 5 mg/L or more for the river’s C-class criteria. Fecal coliform stood at 35,000 MPN per 100 ml, far above the 2,500 maximum permissible limit. Phosphate measured 0.98 mg/L there, up sharply from 0.18 mg/L at the same site in a comparable September sample last year. At the Haryana border, at Asgarpur, dissolved oxygen was recorded as nil, phosphate was 1.05 mg/L and fecal coliform reached 38,000. Only Palla and Wazirabad met the dissolved-oxygen standard.



Phosphates and surfactants trigger froth formation. These pollutants from untreated sewage and detergents used in homes and industries upstream, coupled with a sudden fall in water at Okhla barrage, agitate foaming agents already in the water. This leads to the formation of foam, which accumulates in Kalindi Kunj ghat. The froth is worst in the post-monsoon months because of low-flow river conditions. The foam carries ammonia and phosphates that can cause respiratory and skin problems.

Pollutants such as ammonia are a serious concern as they affect the city’s water supply. Last week, Delhi Jal Board officials noted a spike in pollution levels in Yamuna and fish deaths. The DJB cannot treat raw water with more than 1 part per million (mg/L) of ammonia at its plants. Higher levels make chlorine less effective and can create harmful chloramine compounds, so the DJB cuts production at its water treatment plants when readings spike. The Delhi Pollution Control Committee’s September analysis recorded ammonia of 1.85 mg/L at Asgarpur and 1.12 mg/L at ISBT Bridge, both above the 1 mg/L level at which the board says its plants cannot treat raw water effectively.

World.title: How Nvidia’s export-banned Blackwell chips are showing up in Chinese AI models
World.content:
Nvidia’s advanced Blackwell generation of chips, which are barred from export to China, were used to train leading open-weight AI models developed by Chinese companies, including DeepSeek and Moonshot AI, according to a new research study.

The Trump administration allows Nvidia to ship its less powerful Hopper generation ‘H200’ and ‘H20’ chips to China or Chinese-owned firms, with a 25 per cent cut of the sales going to the US government. The chipmaking giant’s Blackwell GPUs (Graphics Processing Units) are not permitted to be exported to America’s largest geopolitical rival.

However, six open-weight AI models released by four Chinese companies since April 2026 contain numerical patterns or ‘fingerprints’ that suggest they were trained on Nvidia’s Blackwell hardware, according to the report by Will DePue, a former OpenAI researcher who leads the nonprofit research group Unemployment Labs. Earlier models from the same companies match the older Hopper generation chips.



The report’s findings published on Thursday, November 12, are based on an analysis of the weights of large language models (LLMs) released openly by DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group.

A model’s weights are the billions of adjustable numbers that determine how it processes information and produces answers. They can also reflect the configurations of the chips used to train them, the report said. It claims to provide compelling evidence that closely watched Chinese AI models such as Moonshot’s Kimi K3 and DeepSeek’s V4, bear fingerprints from training on export-restricted Blackwell chips.

The findings come at a time when a spy scandal surrounding Nvidia and its former CEO Jensen Huang has renewed calls by US lawmakers for tougher restrictions limiting China’s access to advanced US chips.

Huang stepped down last week after news reports of a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based cloud company Megaspeed, whom US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing. In addition to the extramarital affair he has acknowledged, Huang was also reported to have had at least two other past intimate relationships with Nvidia employees. Beyond these alleged relationships, Nvidia’s potential liability for export control violations may have also influenced its decision to part ways with Huang.



US officials and news reports have previously claimed that DeepSeek and Moonshot AI were using export-restricted Blackwell chips. Unemployment Labs’ report looks to provide technical evidence, extracted from the models’ own published weights, to support these claims.

To be sure, the findings do not show that these models were trained entirely on Nvidia chips or that US-imposed export control laws were necessarily violated. For instance, some Chinese firms are known to remotely access computing resources at offshore data centres in countries such as Malaysia, where Nvidia is permitted to export Blackwell chips.

Still, the report could raise questions about the effectiveness of US export controls and challenge the perception of China catching up with the US in the AI race, if the former’s leading developers still depend on access to cutting-edge Nvidia chips.

Key findings from the report

As part of its investigation, the report said that it recovered traces of the models’ initial values before training adjusts these numbers. These initial values are generated at random by an algorithm called Philox. The researchers then searched for the hardware configurations and initial configurations that reproduce these initial values. For models such as DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Kimi K3, the researchers also confirmed the match on physical Blackwell chips.

In particular, the report found the following:



-Blackwell fingerprints: DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MiniMax-M3 models matched Nvidia’s Blackwell (B200 or B300) chips, which have 148 processor cores called streaming multiprocessors (SMs). DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, Kimi K3.1-Pro, and Ling-3.1-flash models were trained on Blackwell GB200 or GB300 chips which have 152 processor cores.

-Method validation: To verify the accuracy of the method used, researchers analysed 24 AI models whose developers had publicly revealed what hardware they had used to train them. “In every case, our method agrees with the public announcement,” the report said.

-Recent upgrades: The Chinese models trained using Blackwell GPUs are recent ones launched in 2026. For instance, DeepSeek-V3 was released in 2024 and trained on Hopper chips, allowed for export to China, whereas DeepSeek V4 (released in April 2026) read as Blackwell-trained.

-Mixed-generation training: Most of the open-weight models were trained using a mix of Hopper and Blackwell generation of chips. For instance, Moonshot AI’s Kimi K2.7-Code is built on the Hopper-era weights but contains a small part that matches the B200 or B300. The Hopper readings do not identify a specific chip such as H800s, H100 SXMs, and H200s because they share the same fingerprint.



-Large scale training runs: Based on the size of each model and the amount of training data required, the researchers estimated that Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro each needed thousands of Blackwell GPUs running for two to three months.

-Estimated costs: Based on a previous Wall Street Journal report that said 36,000 Blackwell chips installed in Malaysia for ByteDance’s use would cost more than $2.5 billion, the report calculated the cost for some of these clusters to be roughly $200 million to $300 million at roughly $70,000 per GPU. “These figures cover only the final training runs; the labs’ total spending on export-controlled GPUs is likely in the billions of dollars,” it added.

-Notable exceptions: Not every Chinese AI lab relies on Blackwell chips. Models from Alibaba, Zhipu, Tencent, Xiaomi, and StepFun all read as Hopper-trained, as per the report. Meituan, another Chinese developer, trained its LongCat-2.0 model entirely on ‘AI ASIC superpods.’

Why has US imposed chip export restrictions?

Nvidia’s advanced GPUs are widely used to develop cutting-edge AI ​models, ​making the company key to the US race against China to build superior AI systems. For years, the ⁠US government has sought to limit China’s access to Nvidia’s chips because it does not want the Chinese military to benefit from them.



The Biden administration had introduced broader, tiered restrictions on exporting advanced chips and chipmaking equipment to countries outside the US, including China and India.

After returning to the White House for a second term, US President Donald Trump rescinded Biden’s ‘AI Diffusion Rule’, which had imposed new restrictions on chip exports. However, his administration also added more than 80 companies, most of them Chinese, to the US Entity List in 2025, barring them from acquiring US technology on national security grounds.

Despite these curbs, gaps remain. US export controls largely focus on the destination to which chips are shipped, rather than where they are installed or who ultimately uses them. This reportedly allows companies to keep GPUs in data centres in Malaysia and Singapore while allowing customers in China to access the computing power remotely.

Over 2,75,000 Nvidia AI chips were imported to Malaysia in 2024 and 2025, according to nonprofit research organisation Epoch AI.



The export controls have also led to mass smuggling of Nvidia GPUs to China. Analysts estimate that more than 1.5 gigawatts (GW) worth of restricted Nvidia hardware, which could be equivalent to up to 1.5 million GPUs, has reached China, according to a newsletter by semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis.

Epoch AI estimates that about two million advanced chips entered China in 2024 and 2025 through schemes designed to hide their final destination. Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has argued that keeping global markets, including China, open to its chips would help the US maintain its technological lead. Nvidia has also previously denied reports that its chips were being illegally smuggled into China.

The US Commerce Department, led by Secretary Howard Lutnick, has faced questions over its handling of investigations into suspected chip smuggling. Reports say investigators failed to identify suspicious buyers, while Nvidia officials also reportedly intervened in the department’s probe into Singapore-based Megaspeed.

World.title: Blacklisted over child abuse in US, man’s plea to enter India rejected by Delhi High Court
World.content:
The Delhi High Court has refused to interfere with the Centre’s decision to deny entry into India to a person of Indian origin holding an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card, after authorities informed the court that he had been blacklisted for being a registered child sex offender in the United States.

Justice Amit Mahajan observed that once the authorities received information that an individual had been involved in a crime of such a nature in a foreign country, they were within their rights to prevent him from entering India.

“Once the respondents have received information that an individual has been involved in a crime of such nature in a foreign country, they are well within their rights to prevent such a person from setting foot on Indian soil,” the court said on November 3.

World.title: World News Today Live Updates: Two tankers catch fire in Strait of Hormuz after mine incidents, Iran says

World.title: Sonia Gandhi recalls her first meeting with Rajiv Gandhi: ‘Someone I would love to be with’
World.content:
Congress Party leader Sonia Gandhi, 79, recently recalled what drew her to her late husband, Rajiv Gandhi, when they first met. “Of course, he was very good-looking. Food in England in those days was awful. So, I was looking for a restaurant and food closer to my kind of food. There was this Greek restaurant where many European and Indian students went. When I first met him, I felt almost immediately that I would love to be with him. Of course, I learned that it was the same for him. A common friend introduced us. He was a very gentle-looking person. It touched me,” the politician and author shared in a video shared on her X.

DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to.

Taking a cue from her candid reflection, we asked an expert about what makes gentleness stand out.



Here’s what you should consider (Photo: Freepik) Here’s what you should consider (Photo: Freepik)

Delnna Rrajesh, psychotherapist and relationship breakthrough coach, said that long before the conscious mind forms an opinion, the body has already decided whether it feels safe or threatened in someone’s presence.

“This is called neuroception, a term coined by Dr Stephen Porges in his Polyvagal Theory. It is the unconscious detection of safety or danger through facial expressions, tone of voice, posture, and the overall energy a person carries. When someone radiates genuine gentleness, it is not a performance. It is the expression of a regulated nervous system. The body recognises it instantly; the heart just knows it, even when the mind has not yet caught up,” described Delnna.

This is why gentleness moves us more than grand gestures ever can. “It bypasses logic. It speaks directly to the oldest, most primal part of the brain that is wired for one question and one question only: Am I safe here?”

In a small Greek restaurant in Cambridge my journey of love began. Rajiv and I created a world filled with love, laughter and memories. On 10th November, I share that world with you. https://t.co/zvN5Rqqstf — Sonia Gandhi (@SoniaGandhi) October 24, 2026

Now here is what most people confuse. Gentleness is not weakness. “It is the opposite. Weakness hides behind aggression. Gentleness requires a person who is deeply secure within themselves, someone who does not need to dominate, prove, or perform,” Delnna shared with indianexpress.com.

Gentleness is what builds that safety. Not once, but daily. “In the tone of a response during an argument. In the patience offered during someone’s worst season. In the quiet act of choosing softness when the world has given every reason to harden,” shared Delnna.



And in love, that is not just the starting point. It is the whole architecture, shared Delnna.

World.title: Class 10 girls found dead on Himachal riverbank in suspected twin suicide
World.content:
Two minor girls, aged 14 and 15, were found dead on a riverbank in a suspected twin suicide in Himachal Pradesh‘s Bilaspur district within 24 hours after they went missing, the police said Monday. Rescue teams recovered the body of one girl Sunday evening, followed by that of the other girl Monday morning.

Abhishek Dhiman, Superintendent of Police, Bilaspur, said the two girls were friends and in Class 10. One came from a migrant family from Nepal that had been residing in the district for a long time, while the other was a local resident.

According to police, the girls left their homes on Saturday morning, telling their families that they were going to Sundernagar town in the Mandi district to appear for an examination. In the evening, the families reported to the police that the girls were missing.

World.title: Pakistan links regional cooperation with Afghanistan to action against terrorism at ECO moot
World.content:
Pakistan desires a peaceful, prosperous and stable Afghanistan, but meaningful progress towards regional cooperation requires the Afghan authorities to address the legitimate security concerns of neighbouring countries, particularly the threat of terrorism, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on Monday.

He was addressing the 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Council of Ministers in Islamabad, where dignitaries from ECO member states have converged to attend the moot.

Currently, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Tajikistan, Iran, Turkiye, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyz Republic and Uzbekistan are part of the ECO.

However, no one from Afghanistan is attending the moot, according to the list of delegations for the meeting shared by the Foreign Office.

In his opening remarks at the meeting, Dar said a stable Afghanistan, at peace with itself and all its neighbours and fully integrated into the ECO framework, would benefit the Afghan people as well as the wider region by opening up avenues for trade, transit and economic cooperation.

“At the same time, meaningful progress requires the Afghan authorities to address the legitimate security concerns of the neighbouring countries, particularly the threat of terrorism,” he added.

He stressed that a secure and stable environment was essential for sustained regional economic partnerships, adding that these considerations remained central to Pakistan’s broader connectivity agenda.

“Regional connectivity rests on more than the routes that link us. It depends upon trust between states and confidence that international commitments will be honoured. Unresolved disputes and the non-fulfillment of international obligations can erode that trust and impede economic progress,” said Dar.

The foreign minister emphasised that respect for international law and treaties is essential to enduring economic partnerships between countries.

Pakistan, which holds the ECO chairmanship for 2026-27, is hosting the meeting under the theme “Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO”.

Five priorities

Outlining Pakistan’s priorities during its chairmanship of the ECO, Dar identified five key areas of focus, including expanding trade and investment, strengthening regional connectivity, advancing the ECO Trade Agreement, building regional resilience and promoting human development.

The foreign minister said the region’s natural resources, energy reserves, agricultural potential and strategic location offered considerable opportunities for economic cooperation, but realising that potential required functioning transport corridors, efficient border procedures and predictable transit arrangements.

He said Pakistan would work towards wider market access, stronger regional value chains and greater private sector participation, particularly by small and medium-sized enterprises, to boost trade and investment among member states.

“Closer interaction among our business communities can help translate commercial potential into greater trade and investment.”

On connectivity, Dar said Pakistan would seek to improve transport and transit links between Central Asia, South Asia and Pakistani ports on the Arabian Sea. Harmonised customs procedures, efficient border management and predictable transit arrangements were essential to making regional trade routes commercially viable, he added.

The foreign minister also highlighted the need to advance the ECO Trade Agreement, saying the negotiating strategy and roadmap approved by ECO trade ministers in November 2025 provided a basis for modernising the agreement. Pakistan would support efforts to develop a more effective, inclusive and digitally enabled regional trade framework, he said.

On regional resilience, Dar called for closer cooperation in disaster preparedness, early warning systems, sustainable water management and climate-resilient infrastructure, noting that climate change and growing pressure on water and energy resources posed serious challenges to regional economies.

He also underscored the importance of human development, particularly in education, research, innovation and vocational training, saying greater opportunities in these areas could equip young people with skills needed by changing economies. Promoting entrepreneurship and professional exchanges would further strengthen regional integration, he added.

The foreign minister maintained that the five priorities were interconnected and their success would depend on collective efforts by member states. He expressed Pakistan’s readiness to work with ECO members and the organisation’s secretariat on initiatives relating to trade facilitation, transit connectivity and disaster preparedness.

Regional peace and diplomatic efforts

Dar cautioned that peace and stability were essential for economic development, warning that conflict and insecurity in the region could disrupt trade routes, energy supplies, investment and economic projects.

“Peace and development reinforce each other,” he said.

He added that Pakistan remained “deeply concerned about conflict and instability” in the region.

“Their consequences extend beyond national boundaries, disrupting trade routes, energy supplies, investment, and the economic projects of our peoples.”

He said that Pakistan has consistently advocated for “the peaceful resolution of disputes through dialogue and diplomacy in accordance with international law and the United Nations Charter”.

Referring to Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts in the US-Israeli war on Iran, Dar said, “Pakistan will continue these diplomatic efforts in support of dialogue, de-escalation, and lasting regional stability.”

He said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir “remained closely engaged with brotherly countries and international partners to facilitate peaceful outcomes”.

Senior officials meet to finalise agenda

Senior officials of the ECO finalised the agenda and draft Islamabad Communiqué ahead of the organisation’s 30th Council of Ministers meeting.

According to a statement issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA), the Senior Officials Meeting (SOM) was held on Nov 15 under the chairmanship of Foreign Secretary Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad.

The meeting was attended by senior officials from ECO member states, representatives of the ECO Secretariat, and delegates from the organisation’s specialised agencies and regional institutions.

The officials reviewed preparations for the ministerial meeting and finalised its agenda and the draft Islamabad Communique for consideration by the foreign ministers.

They also reviewed the activities undertaken by the ECO Secretariat during the year, including ongoing programmes and initiatives, outcomes of sectoral ministerial meetings, and the work of subsidiary bodies and specialised institutions, the ministry said.

Administrative and financial matters of the organisation also came under discussion, with participants exchanging views on measures to improve its effectiveness.

The SOM serves as a preparatory forum for the Council of Ministers, enabling member states to assess progress, discuss issues of mutual interest and build consensus on proposals and draft documents ahead of ministerial-level deliberations.

Who is attending the meeting?

Delegates attending the meeting include Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, Tajikistan’s Minister of Foreign Affairs Sirojiddin Muhriddin, Turkmenistan’s Foreign Minister Rashid Meredov and Azeri Deputy Foreign Minister Elnur Mammadov.

Turkish Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Musa Kulaklikaya, Kazakhstan’s Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Arman Issagaliyev, Kyrgyz Republic’s Deputy Foreign Minister Kairat Tursunkulov and Uzbek Deputy Foreign Minister Babor Usmanov Masudovich, along with Northern Cyprus’s Minister of Foreign Affairs are also attending the moot in Islamabad.

ECO Secretary General Dr Asad M. Khan is also present at the meeting, along with the secretary general of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA), Sultan Hajiyev.

Additional input from Ameer Hamza.

World.title: Water demand outstrips supply in Punjab: UN agency
World.content:
• FAO report says province losing 5.5bn cubic metres of groundwater annually

• Highlights growing need for water resource management

• Recommends setting up commission to review policies, existing strategies

• Identifies shortcomings in data collection, info consolidation

ISLAMABAD: A detailed assessment of Punjab’s water resources by a United Nations specialised agency has warned of serious challenges ahead, saying the province’s water demand already exceeds supply across all sectors.

The Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said groundwater was being depleted by about 5.5 billion cubic metres annually over a five-year period, while surface water resources were also under growing pressure.

To assess the province’s water stress, the FAO sought expert advice from water specialists, including former Water and Power Development Authority (Wapda) chairman Shamsul Mulk and former Indus River System Authority (Irsa) chairman Rao Irshad Ali Khan.

The findings, published in a report titled Water and Land Accounting in Punjab, were based on annual water accounts covering five water years from 2012 to 2017. The report highlighted the growing need for comprehensive water resources management, saying Punjab required more advanced and integrated water services across different sectors and regions.

It strongly recommended the establishment of a commission to conduct a one-time review of provincial water resources, water-related policies, institutional mandates and existing strategies.

The commission’s tasks would include ensuring coherence between national and inter-provincial policies and water initiatives, and establishing an integrated mechanism to assess the impact of transboundary water projects and other interventions.

It would also identify overlapping responsibilities and changes needed in institutional mandates, assess water and land resources, current demand and projections until 2050, and establish a provincial coordination cell within the Planning and Development Department for day-to-day operations.

Given Punjab’s major contribution to the national economy, the management of its water resources is particularly critical, especially as Pakistan’s overall water supply is considered insecure.

The gap between water supply and demand has become particularly acute in Punjab’s urban areas because of limited access to freshwater and declining groundwater reserves, the report observed.

Agricultural production is also increasingly at risk because of water stress and the depletion of groundwater storage, it said. Freshwater shortages have led to greater reliance on the recycling of low-quality water, while pollution from agro-chemicals and urban wastewater has intensified.

The analysis estimated that Punjab needed an additional 10 billion cubic metres of usable water annually to bridge the supply-demand gap and sustain its groundwater aquifer.

It stressed the need for timely intervention, including exploring ways to increase surface water resources, improve gro­undwater recharge and develop provincial mechanisms for inter-seasonal water transfers.

The report said rivers flowing through Punjab and its freshwater bodies had diminished significantly, with river flows declining by about 30 billion cubic metres following the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty with India.

The province has only 1.7 per cent of wetland areas, while its natural landscape has declined considerably. Rainfall remains the only source of water outside canal command areas and urban centres, it noted.

The report also observed that groundwater recharge sources had diminished, reducing the province’s net renewable water resources.

Punjab’s canal system operates as a run-of-the-river system for half the year and cannot draw its full authorised share of river water. “The reduction in drainage flows suggests a consistent water supply and demand gap,” it added.

A technical diagnosis of the water accounts identified four main challenges: increasing spatio-temporal water scarcity; continuous groundwater depletion; competition among sectors for water and unaccounted inter-sectoral water transfers; and the need to protect annual renewable water resources, wetlands and the natural landscape.

The report also identified shortcomings in data collection and information consolidation. It recommended expanding the land-use classification system to cover the entire province.

World.title: Separate legislative assembly in Islamabad on the cards
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The government has intensified its efforts to set up a separate legislative assembly in Islamabad.

If all goes as planned, a legislative assembly will be set up in the capital city, which will be headed by an elected mayor. Some months ago, a high-profile committee headed by Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal had finalised recommendations, which were presented to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. The recommendations proposed the devolution of powers from the federation to Islamabad Capital Territory as a federating unit, with a provincial-style government. It was stated that the proposed Islamabad Assembly would have 27 members and would be headed by an elected mayor/chief minister.

However, new proposals are now emerging for setting up a separate legislative assembly. Some TV channels reported on Sunday that the boundaries of Islamabad would also be expanded and that there were chances that Haripur, Murree and parts of Rawalpindi would be made part of Islamabad. When contacted, a senior government officer said that it was clear that a new, separate legislative assembly would be set up in Islamabad.

“As far as making Haripur, Rawalpindi and Murree part of Islamabad is concerned, nothing is final yet. They are part of separate provinces, and we will see if they can be made part of Islamabad or how laws passed by Islamabad will be implemented in these areas. So, again, nothing is final; these are discussions. But yes, Islamabad will have a separate legislative assembly,” he said.

It is relevant to note here that local government elections in Islamabad have been facing inordinate delays, as the elections have been postponed at least five times during the last four years, with the government always stating that new legislation is being made for a “vibrant system”. As per the latest schedule, elections were supposed to be held on Dec 20, but the Islamabad High Court suspended the schedule on a petition which pleaded that polls could not be held until the legal status of the existing constituency delimitation was conclusively determined.
